lines.japanese:
夜中。
　携帯電話の狂騒的な呼び出しに、忍は睡眠を中断
された。
lines.english: The middle of the night. The frenzied ringing of his cell phone tore Shinobu from sleep.

lines.japanese:
寝ぼけているのか、文句一つ言わず、ほとんど自
動的に忍は手を伸ばした。
lines.english: Perhaps still half asleep, Shinobu reached for it almost automatically, without a word of complaint.

lines.japanese: 受信。
lines.english: Call connected.

lines.japanese: 『寝てました？』
lines.english: “Were you asleep?”

lines.japanese:
夜中だ。
　寝ていて当然だと思うが、口には出さなかった。
lines.english: It was the middle of the night. He thought it was perfectly reasonable to be asleep, but said nothing.

lines.japanese: 「葉子」
lines.english: “Youko.”

lines.japanese: 『港の葉子です』
lines.english: “This is Youko at the harbor.”

lines.japanese:
わからなくなった。
　時を追って葉子のことがわからなくなっていく気
がした。
lines.english: He no longer understood. With every passing moment, it seemed he understood Youko less and less.

lines.japanese:
『あの、兄の件なんですが……
　夜に出て行ったっきり、戻ってこなくて……』
lines.english: “Um, it’s about my brother… He went out tonight and hasn’t come back…”

lines.japanese:
針が心を貫く錯覚。
　しかし具体的な像を結ばないのだ。
lines.english: It felt as though a needle had pierced his heart. Yet no concrete image would form.

lines.japanese:
ひどく気分が悪い。
　冗談を言っている場合ではないはずだ。
lines.english: He felt violently ill. Surely this was no time for jokes.

lines.japanese: 『何かご存じかな、と思って……あの、もしもし？』
lines.english: “I thought you might know something… Hello?”

lines.japanese: 『これって失踪したのかなーと。あの？』
lines.english: “I was thinking maybe he's gone missing. Hello?”

lines.japanese: 『もしもしーもしもしーもしもしー？』
lines.english: “Hellooo? Hellooo? Hellooo?”

lines.japanese:
こんな時ばかりは、真綿を思わせる口調がどうし
ても耳に障ってしまう。
lines.english: At a moment like this, the spun-silk softness of her speech grated unbearably on his ears.

lines.japanese: しかし幸いなことに忍は、もう声を聞いてはいない。
lines.english: Fortunately, Shinobu was no longer listening.

lines.japanese: 電話をとうに取り落としている。
lines.english: He had already dropped the phone.

lines.japanese: 以降、床に嘔吐するばかり。
lines.english: After that, he could only vomit onto the floor.

lines.japanese:
森にやってきた。
　工場のそばにある森だ。
　そばといっても、歩けばかなりの時間がかかる。
lines.english: He had come to the forest. The one near the factory. Near was relative—it was still quite a walk.

lines.japanese: 学校には、行くつもりはなかった。
lines.english: He had no intention of going to school.
(Itsuki.)

lines.japanese:
足取りには迷いがない。
　何度も通った道だ。
　踏み分けられ、うっすらと地肌が道をなしている。
lines.english: There was no hesitation in his stride. He had walked this way many times. A faint trail of bare earth showed where the vegetation had been trampled down.

lines.japanese: （葉子）
lines.english: (Youko.)

lines.japanese:
恐れる時ほど忍の足は森に向く。
　懸念が大きいほど忍の心は大樹を頼る。
lines.english: The more afraid he was, the more his feet turned toward the forest. The greater his worries, the more his heart relied on the great tree.

lines.japanese: 大樹―――
lines.english: The great tree—

lines.japanese:
この森には、樹がある。
　別段、変わったところのない樹である。
　森で最も大きい……といったものでもない。
lines.english: There was a tree in this forest. Nothing about it was especially unusual. It wasn't even… the largest tree in the woods.

lines.japanese:
自然保護の人間が気に掛けるものでも、信仰の対
象となるものでもない。
lines.english: It was not the sort of tree to interest conservationists, nor was it an object of worship.

lines.japanese:
ただ、古い。
　老樹だ。
lines.english: It was simply old. An ancient tree.

lines.japanese:
この街よりも長く生き、さらには国が定まる前か
ら生きている。
lines.english: It had lived longer than this town—indeed, since before the nation itself had taken shape.

lines.japanese:
存在を知るのは忍の他、沙也加だけである。
　他の人間には、さして意味のあるべきものでもない。
lines.english: Apart from Shinobu, only Sayaka knew it existed. To anyone else, it held no particular significance.

lines.japanese:
むしろ不気味なものに違いない。
　樹は歪だからだ。
lines.english: If anything, they would have found it eerie. The tree was misshapen.

lines.japanese:
荒縄をよってねじったような姿。
　草深い森にふさわしい、暗緑色の塊。
lines.english: Its form was like a length of coarse rope twisted upon itself. A dark-green mass at home in a forest dense with undergrowth.

lines.japanese:
より背の高い木々があるせいか、樹冠を抜けるた
め、枝を広く高く張り巡らせている。
lines.english: Perhaps because taller trees surrounded it, its branches spread far and high to break through the canopy.

lines.japanese:
周囲の木に絡みつき、締め上げ、利している。
　若者にしがみつく老人のようにも、見えるかも知
れない。
lines.english: Its branches wound around the nearby trees, constricting them, using them. It might have looked like an old man clinging to the young.

lines.japanese:
姿形が醜悪になるのは仕方ないと思えるほど、長
い時を越えてきた。
lines.english: It had lived through so many years that its ugly shape seemed only to be expected.

lines.japanese:
この樹は王と呼ばれても良い。
　幸い植物に心はない。
　樹に心はない。
lines.english: This tree might well be called a king. Fortunately, plants had no hearts. A tree had no heart.

lines.japanese:
醜状ほどに精神性が病むこともなく、王が世界の
病巣となるようなこともない。
lines.english: Its spirit could not sicken to match its hideous shape, nor could this king become a canker in the world.

lines.japanese: 「はっ、はっ……」
lines.english: “Hah, hah…”

lines.japanese:
濃すぎる森林の空気に悪酔いしながら、なかば駆
け足で中央に向かう。
　この森を歩くには、周囲に目をやらないことだ。
lines.english: The forest air was so thick it left him drunk and sick as he half ran toward its center. The trick to walking these woods was never to look around.

lines.japanese:
得体の知れないものが潜んでいる気がしてなら
ない。
lines.english: He could not shake the feeling that something unknowable was lurking among the trees.

lines.japanese:
市街に近い。
　広大な樹林ではない。
lines.english: It lay close to the city. This was no vast woodland.

lines.japanese:
しかし、深い―――
　深度が感じられる。
lines.english: And yet it was deep— somehow, it had depth.

lines.japanese:
面積としては取るに足らない。
　伽藍のような地下空間が広がっているわけでもない。
lines.english: Its area was negligible. No cathedral-like expanse opened beneath the ground.

lines.japanese:
空間は……空は無限に続くが、それは“王の森”
に限ったことではない。
lines.english: Space… the sky went on forever, but that was hardly unique to the “King's Forest.”

lines.japanese:
物理的には狭い森である。
　木々の立ち並ぶ様が、壁の如き様相になってくる。
lines.english: Physically, it was a small forest. Yet the trees standing rank upon rank began to look like walls.

lines.japanese: 樹上の層が光を遮り、行く先をことさら薄暗くする。
lines.english: The layers overhead blocked the light, making the way ahead especially dim.

lines.japanese: 臆することなく忍は進んだ。
lines.english: Shinobu pressed on without faltering.

lines.japanese:
そして―――森の中枢、忘却された揺籃の地へ
滑り出た。
lines.english: And then—he emerged into the forest's heart, the forgotten cradle.

lines.japanese: 王樹は歪曲した身をさらす。
lines.english: The king-tree bared its twisted body.

lines.japanese:
不思議とそこは、樹冠部が円形に切り取られ、陽
光を取り込んでいた。
lines.english: Strangely, the canopy there formed a circular opening that admitted the sunlight.

lines.japanese: 人の手では、無論ない。
lines.english: No human hand had made it, of course.

lines.japanese:
時に忘却され、昔のままに取り置かれた、自然の
幾何学遺産である。
lines.english: It was a relic of nature's geometry, forgotten by time and preserved unchanged from ages past.
“Hah, hah… Nn—”

lines.japanese:
手を伸ばす。
　取りすがるように、幹に触れる。
lines.english: He reached out. He touched the trunk as though clinging to it.

lines.japanese:
ひときわ大きく息を吸い、
　額をつけた。
lines.english: He took an especially deep breath, then rested his forehead against the trunk.

lines.japanese:
そして木の根本に座り込み、眼を閉じた。
　安息のために。
lines.english: Then he sat down at the foot of the tree and closed his eyes. To rest.

lines.japanese: これからはじまる長い戦いのために。
lines.english: For the long battle that lay ahead.

lines.japanese: そして忍は、
lines.english: And Shinobu—

lines.japanese: 夢を見た。
lines.english: dreamed.

lines.japanese:
物語のように続く日々を、物語のように読み返す
ために―――
lines.english: So that he might reread, as a story, the days that had unfolded like a story—

lines.japanese: 今までの時間、英気を養った。そう思っている。
lines.english: He had spent all that time recovering his strength—or so he believed.

lines.japanese: 森での瞑想は無駄ではないはずだ。
lines.english: His meditation in the forest could not have been for nothing.

lines.japanese:
やるべきことは決まっていた。
　人の極度に少ない通りは、閑散として乾いた印象だ。
lines.english: What he had to do was clear. The almost empty street looked bleak and parched.

lines.japanese:
時間帯は日中。
　学生は学校に行っている時間帯でもある。
lines.english: It was the middle of the day. Students would be in school at this hour.

lines.japanese:
だが怪しむ者さえいない。
　やりやすくはある。
lines.english: But there was no one around to be suspicious of him. That made things easier.
(All right…)

lines.japanese: 猟奇殺人事件について調べねばならない。
lines.english: He had to investigate the bizarre murder case.

lines.japanese: （首を切って落とした……か）
lines.english: (The heads had been cut off…)

lines.japanese:
腕を組み、思案する。
　携帯を取り出し、おさめた資料に目を通す。
lines.english: He folded his arms in thought. Then he took out his phone and reviewed the files stored on it.

lines.japanese:
簡素にまとめられた情報だ。
　一般公開された事件の情報、独自の調査結果など
を入れてある。
lines.english: It was a bare-bones compilation. It included publicly available facts about the case, the results of his own inquiries, and other material.

lines.japanese:
いくらか思案し、方針を決めた。
　すでに時間の経過は著しい。
lines.english: He thought it over, then decided on an approach. Considerable time had already passed.

lines.japanese:
殺人事件における警察捜査は、初動が最も重要と
言われる。
lines.english: In a murder investigation, the initial police response was said to be the most important.

lines.japanese:
だからこそ事件発生から数時間は、特捜隊による
迅速な情報収集が行われる。
lines.english: That was why, in the first few hours after a crime, a special investigation team moved quickly to gather information.

lines.japanese:
それで犯人が特定できるケースも多い。
　なお犯人逮捕に至らない場合、捜査一課に引き継
がれることになる。
lines.english: In many cases, that alone was enough to identify the culprit. If it still failed to produce an arrest, the case would pass to the First Investigation Division.

lines.japanese:
すでに日数は経過してしまった。
　この段階で容疑者さえも挙げられていないのであ
れば、捜査はかなり難航しているということになる。
lines.english: Days had already passed. If the police had not even identified a suspect by this stage, the investigation had clearly run into serious trouble.

lines.japanese:
素人がのこのこと出張ったところで、どうなるも
のでもない。
lines.english: There was little a blundering amateur could accomplish by wandering in now.

lines.japanese: だが―――
lines.english: But—

lines.japanese: （警察は……常識にのっとった捜査しかしない）
lines.english: (The police… never investigate beyond the bounds of common sense.)

lines.japanese:
もし犯人が常識でははかれない思考・方法を持っ
ていた場合は？
lines.english: But what if the culprit's thoughts and methods lay beyond common sense?

lines.japanese:
殺害方法からしてもそうだ。
　説明のつかない部分が多い。
lines.english: The method of killing itself suggested as much. Many details defied explanation.

lines.japanese:
警察の判断力では、不透明のまま常識的な説明を
つけてしまう場合もあるだろう。
lines.english: The limits of police reasoning might lead them to settle on a conventional explanation while the truth remained obscure.

lines.japanese:
そこが付け目だった。
　幸い、人が使えないこともない。
　頼れる人間もいる。
lines.english: That was where he saw an opening. Fortunately, there were people he could use. There were people he could rely on, too.

lines.japanese:
巻き返せる状況だ。
　そう、充分巻き返せるのだ。
lines.english: He could still turn things around. Yes. There was every chance he could turn things around.

lines.japanese: 火のような息を吐く。
lines.english: He exhaled a breath like fire.

lines.japanese:
欲しいものがある。
　取り戻さねばならないものがある。
　これはその聖なる第一歩なのだ。
lines.english: There was something he wanted. Something he had to reclaim. This was the sacred first step toward it.
“Nn…”

lines.japanese:
けたたましい音に、睡眠を切断される。
　瞬間的に忍は覚醒した。
lines.english: A shrill noise sliced through his sleep. Shinobu woke in an instant.

lines.japanese: 早朝だった。
lines.english: It was early morning.

lines.japanese:
直前まで完全に熟睡していたようだ。
　単純に寝るだけであれば、この殺風景な部屋の方
が、忍には合っているようだ。
lines.english: He had apparently been fast asleep until that moment. If all he needed was sleep, this bare room seemed to suit him better.

lines.japanese:
工場はやはり風雨の侵入が厳しい時もある。
　また医療施設で泊まることもあるが、そちらは論
外である。
lines.english: At times, far too much wind and rain found its way into the factory. He sometimes slept at the medical facility as well, but that was out of the question.

lines.japanese:
完全に閉鎖された空間は、人を不安にするだけだ。
　薄暗い個室に閉じこもる行為と変わりない。
lines.english: A completely sealed space only made people uneasy. It was no different from shutting himself away in a dim little room.

lines.japanese: 「……よし、五時ジャスト」
lines.english: “…Good. Five o'clock exactly.”

lines.japanese:
歯を食いしばって、身を立てる。
　胃が重い。
lines.english: He gritted his teeth and hauled himself upright. His stomach felt heavy.

lines.japanese:
朝日が苦痛。
　頭が痛む。
lines.english: The morning light was agony. His head throbbed.

lines.japanese:
いつ崩れるかも知れない体調。
　引きずって、行かねばならない。
lines.english: His body felt ready to give out at any moment. Still, he had to drag himself onward.

lines.japanese: 「忍……もう起きたんですか？」
lines.english: “Shinobu… You're up already?”

lines.japanese:
千鳥もまた寝起きだったのか、普段は見ることが
できない寝癖がぴんと自己主張していた。
lines.english: Perhaps Chidori had just woken too. A rebellious cowlick— the sort he never normally saw—stood bolt upright.

lines.japanese:
指さすと、自分でもわかっていたのか、恥ずかし
そうに片手で押さえた。
lines.english: When he pointed to it, she pressed it down with one hand, looking embarrassed—apparently she had noticed it already.

lines.japanese: しかし手を離すと、ばねのように戻る。
lines.english: The moment she let go, it sprang back into place.

lines.japanese: 「……ええと……おはようです」
lines.english: “…Um… good morning.”

lines.japanese:
「休むとは聞いていましたけど……
　何かすることがあったんですか？」
lines.english: “I heard you were taking the day off… Did you have something to do?”

lines.japanese: 「……実は、ずっと調べものをしてて」
lines.english: “…Actually, I've been looking into something.”

lines.japanese: 申し訳なさそうに告白する。
lines.english: He admitted it apologetically.

lines.japanese: 「足を使って？」
lines.english: “Out in the field?”

lines.japanese: 「まあ」
lines.english: “More or less.”

lines.japanese: 千鳥は理解に苦しんでいるようだった。
lines.english: Chidori seemed to have trouble making sense of that.

lines.japanese:
「よくわからないんですが……わかりました。
　それで、今日はこれから？」
lines.english: “I don't really understand… but all right. And you're going out today?”

lines.japanese: 「……そのつもりだったり……」
lines.english: “…That was the idea…”

lines.japanese: 一瞬、千鳥は難しい顔をした。
lines.english: For an instant, Chidori looked troubled.

lines.japanese: 「……止めても無駄なんでしょうね……」
lines.english: “…There's no point trying to stop you, is there…?”

lines.japanese: 「友達のことだから」
lines.english: “It's about a friend.”

lines.japanese: 「わかりました。ご自由に」
lines.english: “Very well. Do as you please.”

lines.japanese: 「すぐ外に？」
lines.english: “Are you heading out right away?”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「補導されたらごめんなさい」
lines.english: “Sorry in advance if the police pick me up.”

lines.japanese: 「バカですね」
lines.english: “You're an idiot.”

lines.japanese:
ぎこちなく微笑む。
　そして台所に向かった。
lines.english: She smiled awkwardly. Then she headed for the kitchen.

lines.japanese:
「朝食くらいは食べていきなさい。
　何か簡単に作ります」
lines.english: “At least eat breakfast before you go. I'll make something simple.”
“…Okay.”

lines.japanese:
きっと黒こげのトーストが出てくる。
　炭素の塊は滋養とは言えないだろう。
lines.english: No doubt she would serve him blackened toast. A lump of carbon could hardly count as nourishment.

lines.japanese:
だが妙にうきうきした様子で、忍は椅子に座るの
だった。
lines.english: Even so, Shinobu took his seat, looking strangely cheerful.

lines.japanese:
（……ずっと、こんな関係でいられたら
　いいのにな……）
lines.english: (…I wish we could stay like this forever…)

lines.japanese:
いつもは遠い義姉との関係が、今日はとても近し
く感じられるのだった。
lines.english: Today, his usually distant older sister felt very close.

lines.japanese:
表に出た。
　胃の中からこみ上げてくるものを、なんとかこら
える。
lines.english: He stepped outside. He fought down what was rising from his stomach.

lines.japanese:
「……自家製マーマレード、か……
　またいきなり……強烈なワザを……うぷ」
lines.english: “…Homemade marmalade… Another surprise attack… and a vicious one… Urp.”

lines.japanese:
炭素よりは栄養価は高そうだが、柑橘系はある種
の逆流感覚を連想させ、きつい。
lines.english: It seemed more nutritious than carbon, but citrus reminded him of the feeling of something coming back up. It was hard to take.

lines.japanese: 「さて」
lines.english: “All right.”

lines.japanese: 歩き出す。
lines.english: He started walking.

lines.japanese: 調査のために。
lines.english: To investigate.

lines.japanese:
一度あずさの家の前で立ち止まる。
　白い家はどこか寂しげに佇み、人のいる気配がない。
lines.english: He stopped outside Azusa's house. The white house stood there forlorn, with no sign of anyone inside.

lines.japanese:
早朝だからだろうか。
　もちろん普通であれば寝ている時間で、あずさも
また同様のはずだ。
lines.english: Was it simply because the hour was so early? Of course, people would normally be asleep at this hour, and Azusa should be no exception.

lines.japanese:
数分その場に立ち尽くして、いよいよ忍は重い踵
を持ち上げることができた。
lines.english: After standing there for several minutes, Shinobu finally forced his leaden feet to move.

lines.japanese:
馴染みの風景に背を向けて、離れる。
　距離を離すごとに、足取りは軽く力強くなっていく。
lines.english: He turned his back on the familiar sight and moved away. The farther he went, the lighter and stronger his stride became.

lines.japanese:
少年は急いて進む。
　今は細かなことは考えない。
　ただ友のために、体を動かすばかり。
lines.english: The boy hurried onward. For now, he would not think about the details. He simply kept moving for his friend.

lines.japanese:
陰鬱かも知れない明日に見ぬ振りを決め込んで、
今と過去とを高めあげる。至高まで。
lines.english: He shut his eyes to whatever gloom tomorrow might hold and exalted the present and the past—raised them to the sublime.

lines.japanese:
まさに今と過去こそが、友の価値なのだから。
　明日仲良くいられることが保証されずとも、友な
のだから。
lines.english: What made a friend valuable was precisely the present and the past. Even if there was no guarantee they would still be close tomorrow, a friend remained a friend.

lines.japanese: やがて忍は駆けている。
lines.english: Before long, Shinobu broke into a run.

lines.japanese: 人間・貴宮忍として駆けている。
lines.english: He ran as Shinobu Atemiya—a human being.

lines.japanese: （斎―――どこにいるんだ！）
lines.english: (Itsuki—where are you!?)

lines.japanese:
駅前。
　事件現場である。
lines.english: Outside the station. One of the crime scenes.

lines.japanese:
昼間だが、それなりの人間が歩いている。
　ここで殺傷行為が行われたとは信じがたい。
lines.english: It was broad daylight, with a fair number of people walking past. It was difficult to believe an act of violence had occurred here.

lines.japanese:
現場はロープで隔離されていた。
　警官はいない。
lines.english: The site had been cordoned off with rope. There were no police officers.

lines.japanese:
アスファルトの一部、かすかな血痕がこびりつい
て、黒く濁っている。
lines.english: A faint bloodstain clung to one patch of asphalt, turning it a muddy black.

lines.japanese: 少量である。
lines.english: There was very little of it.

lines.japanese: （こんなものなのか？　首を切られて？）
lines.english: (Is that all? After someone was beheaded?)

lines.japanese:
風雨に流されてしまったのだろうか、とも考えら
れる。
lines.english: Perhaps the wind and rain had washed it away.

lines.japanese:
考えるべき部分が多すぎた。
　もとより捜査技術など忍にはない。
　できることをするしかないのだ。
lines.english: There were far too many questions. Shinobu had no investigative training in the first place. He would simply have to do what he could.

lines.japanese:
周囲をうかがい、内側に入ってみる。
　無関心な人々は咎めだてることもない。
lines.english: He checked his surroundings, then stepped inside the cordon. The indifferent passersby made no attempt to stop him.

lines.japanese:
奇異な行動に視線を寄越すだけである。
　膝をつき、地面に触れてみる。
lines.english: They merely gave him curious looks. He knelt and touched the ground.

lines.japanese:
当たり前ではあるが、血は乾いて染みていた。
　交通の邪魔にならないためか、現場の保持は最低
限のものだ。
lines.english: Naturally, the blood had dried into the pavement. Perhaps to keep from obstructing traffic, no more than the bare minimum had been done to preserve the scene.

lines.japanese: ここには、証拠といえるものはない。
lines.english: There was nothing here one could call evidence.

lines.japanese:
忍は立ち上がり、ロープをまたいで
　携帯を取り出し、次の現場を確認する。
lines.english: Shinobu rose and stepped over the rope. He took out his phone and checked the next location.

lines.japanese: 「学校……か」
lines.english: “The school…”

lines.japanese: 忍の母校でもある。
lines.english: It was his old school.

lines.japanese:
懐かしい場所ではある。
　感傷にひたる時間が惜しい。
lines.english: The place brought back memories. There was no time to indulge in sentiment.

lines.japanese: 問題の花壇に近づこうとした時、強く誰何された。
lines.english: As he approached the flower bed in question, someone barked a challenge.
“…Who's there!?”
“…Sir?”

lines.japanese: 見知った顔。ただし数年以上前の。
lines.english: He knew the face, though he had not seen it in years.

lines.japanese: 「お、君は……ああ、えーと？」
lines.english: “Oh, you're… Ah, what was it?”

lines.japanese: 「貴宮です」
lines.english: “Atemiya.”

lines.japanese:
「おお、そうだったそうだった。
　久しぶりじゃないか。何年ぶりだ？」
lines.english: “Ah, yes, of course. It's been ages. How many years has it been?”

lines.japanese: 警戒から一転、破顔した。
lines.english: His face broke into a smile, all wariness gone.

lines.japanese: 「ご無沙汰しております」
lines.english: “It’s been a long time, sir.”

lines.japanese: 「どうした？　何か用か？」
lines.english: “What brings you here? Did you need something?”

lines.japanese:
「いえ、用というわけでもなかったんですけど……
　ちょっと気になって」
lines.english: “No, I didn't really come for anything in particular… It was just on my mind.”

lines.japanese: 「気になる？」
lines.english: “On your mind?”

lines.japanese: 「あの事件が」
lines.english: “The incident.”

lines.japanese: 本宮と呼ばれた教師は、途端に表情を曇らせた。
lines.english: Motomiya's face immediately clouded.

lines.japanese: 「……母校だものなあ」
lines.english: “…It was your old school, after all.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「ちょうど、そこでな」
lines.english: “It happened right there.”

lines.japanese: 示した箇所はちょうど花壇のそば。
lines.english: He indicated a spot beside the flower bed.

lines.japanese: 「なんだか、世界が遠くなった気がしないか？」
lines.english: “Doesn't it feel as though the world has grown distant?”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 唐突とも思えた教師の物言いに、忍は惹きつけられた。
lines.english: The teacher's seemingly abrupt remark drew Shinobu in.

lines.japanese: 「嫌な世の中だ、と言ってしまえば簡単なんだがな」
lines.english: “It would be easy enough to say the world's become an ugly place.”

lines.japanese:
「それだけじゃ説明のできない不安が、世の中を覆
　っている気がしてな」
lines.english: “But I feel as if an unease that can't be explained away so easily has settled over the world.”

lines.japanese:
「貴宮はどうだ？
　学校は……その……充実してるか？」
lines.english: “What about you, Atemiya? Is school… well… fulfilling?”

lines.japanese:
充実、という単語を持ち出すために、教師はため
らいを見せる。
lines.english: The teacher hesitated before settling on the word fulfilling.

lines.japanese:
その感覚が忍には不思議とよく理解できた。
　不謹慎に思えたのだろう。
lines.english: Strangely, Shinobu understood the hesitation very well. The word must have seemed in poor taste.

lines.japanese: 「……皆、どこか不安そうではあります」
lines.english: “…Everyone does seem uneasy somehow.”

lines.japanese: 教師は無念そうな顔をした。
lines.english: The teacher looked pained.

lines.japanese: 「そうだろうな」
lines.english: “I thought as much.”

lines.japanese: 「世界が遠いというのは、よくわかります」
lines.english: “I understand what you mean about the world feeling distant.”

lines.japanese:
教師は恥ずかしげに視線をそらした。
　４０に手が届く人間が口にするには、少々若すぎ
る表現だ。
lines.english: The teacher looked away, embarrassed. It was a rather youthful turn of phrase for a man pushing forty.

lines.japanese:
大人は世界を動かす力でなければならない。
　だが大人にしてみても、社会の駆動源を見失って
久しい。
lines.english: Adults were supposed to be the force that kept the world moving. Yet even they had long since lost sight of what powered society.

lines.japanese:
もうじき止まる世界だと、誰もが知っている。
　誰も、どうすべきかわからない。
lines.english: Everyone knew the world would soon grind to a halt. No one knew what to do.

lines.japanese:
姿の見えない不安を解析することもできない。
　忍は花壇のそばに供えられた花を目にしていた。
lines.english: No one could even analyze that unseen anxiety. Shinobu looked at the flowers laid there as offerings.

lines.japanese: 「……女の子だそうですね」
lines.english: “…I heard it was a girl.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「祈っていっていいですか？」
lines.english: “May I pray for her?”

lines.japanese: 「そうしてやってくれるか」
lines.english: “Would you do that for her?”

lines.japanese:
教育上の配慮からか、血痕さえも残されてはいな
かった。
lines.english: Perhaps for the students' sake, not even a bloodstain remained.

lines.japanese: 交通のため、現場は保持されていなかった。
lines.english: To keep traffic moving, the scene had not been preserved.

lines.japanese:
往来での事件については、他二件についても同様
の処置がとられていた。
lines.english: The same was true of the other two incidents on public thoroughfares.

lines.japanese: 学校に足を向けた。
lines.english: He headed for the school.

lines.japanese: あずさがいた。
lines.english: Azusa was there.

lines.japanese:
こんな光景を過去、幾度も見たが、その度に胸を
締めつけられる。
lines.english: He had seen this sight many times before, yet each time it made his chest tighten.

lines.japanese: 泣きそうな自分を、忍は驚きとともに自覚した。
lines.english: Shinobu realized with surprise that he was close to tears.

lines.japanese: 今回のことについて、彼女はまだ何も知らない。
lines.english: She still knew nothing about what had happened.

lines.japanese:
知らないままでいられればいいと、強く願う忍だ
った。
lines.english: Shinobu desperately wished she could go on not knowing.

lines.japanese: （……斎を捜そう）
lines.english: (…I should find Itsuki.)

lines.japanese:
背を撫でた視線を、少女らしい感受性で察知した
のか、
lines.english: Perhaps, with a girl's sensitivity, she sensed the gaze brush her back—

lines.japanese: あずさは背後を見たのだった。
lines.english: Azusa turned to look behind her.

lines.japanese: すでに、誰もいなかった。
lines.english: No one was there anymore.

lines.japanese:
考え事をするには、静かな場所が望ましい。
　雑音のない、また余計な気を回す必要のない場所。
lines.english: A quiet place was best for thinking. Somewhere without noise, with nothing else demanding his attention.

lines.japanese:
何もない場所。
　聞こえない場所。
lines.english: A place with nothing. A place where nothing could be heard.

lines.japanese:
求めて歩けば自宅だったと、ただそれだけのこと
である。
lines.english: He went in search of one and ended up at home. That was all.

lines.japanese:
笑ってしまった。
　静謐を閉じこめたかのような部屋、寝台に腰を乗
せて考えた。
lines.english: He laughed. In a room that seemed to have silence sealed inside it, he sat on the bed and thought.

lines.japanese:
からっぽの心に、断片的な情報が踊っていた。
　材料は揃っていたが、心は駆動する力に欠けている。
lines.english: Fragments of information danced through his empty mind. All the material was there, but his heart lacked the force to set it in motion.

lines.japanese: 虚ろだった。
lines.english: He felt hollow.

lines.japanese:
肉体がそうであるように、心も情動というエネル
ギーを必要とするのだろう。
lines.english: Perhaps the heart, like the body, needed emotion for fuel.

lines.japanese:
確かにこの部屋に空虚を栽培したのは自分なのだ
とわかった。
lines.english: He realized he was the one who had cultivated the emptiness in this room.

lines.japanese:
疲れていた。
　横たわれば眠る。
lines.english: He was tired. If he lay down, he would sleep.

lines.japanese:
機能を低下させて、意識をサスペンド・モードに
委ねたい。
lines.english: He wanted to power down and consign his consciousness to suspend mode.

lines.japanese: 欲求といえる欲求は、それだけだった。
lines.english: It was the only desire he could still call a desire.

lines.japanese: 「考えよう」
lines.english: “Let's think.”

lines.japanese:
ひとりごち、心の帆に風を送る。
　犯行現場はひととおり見た。
　イメージ的な部分をだいぶかためることができた。
lines.english: He muttered it to himself, sending wind into the sails of his mind. He had visited all the crime scenes. He had managed to form a fairly clear picture.

lines.japanese:
固執すれば足かせだが、抑制された仮構は良い足
場となる。
lines.english: Cling to a hypothesis and it becomes a shackle. Keep it in check, and it offers solid footing.

lines.japanese:
仮想イメージを忍は卑怯なほど自在に使い、届く
高みの上限を引き上げる。
lines.english: Shinobu manipulated hypothetical images with almost unfair dexterity, raising the upper limit of his reach.

lines.japanese:
携帯を取り出し、メモ書き機能を呼び出した。
　得た印象を書き記していく。
lines.english: He took out his phone and opened the memo function. He began recording his impressions.

lines.japanese:
現場は多くのことを告げる。
　犯人がまるで場所を選んでいないことは、注目す
べき点だ。
lines.english: A crime scene spoke volumes. One point was worth noting: the culprit did not appear to choose the locations at all.

lines.japanese:
人通りが激しい箇所、目撃されやすい箇所が確か
にある。
lines.english: Some of the sites were undeniably busy and highly visible.

lines.japanese:
往来の中での被害者さえいる。
　だというのに、目撃報告がいまだに得られないの
である。
lines.english: One victim had even been attacked in the street. Yet not a single eyewitness report had emerged.

lines.japanese:
ふと、忍は遺体の検死結果を見ることはできない
かと考えた。
lines.english: It occurred to Shinobu that he might find some way to see the postmortem findings.

lines.japanese:
遺体は現場以上に、多くを語るだろう。
　だが実際の遺体がいまだに保持されているわけは
ない。
lines.english: The bodies would say even more than the scenes. But surely the bodies themselves were no longer being held.

lines.japanese:
遺族に返却されているだろう。
　葬儀が終わってしまったものもある。
lines.english: They would have been returned to the families. Some funerals had already taken place.
“…The paperwork.”

lines.japanese:
なにぶん犯罪性のある死体である。
　死体検案書と類する写真資料があるはずだ。
lines.english: These deaths involved suspected crimes, after all. There ought to be postmortem examination reports and accompanying photographs.

lines.japanese: 「ねじこんでみるか」
lines.english: “Maybe I can muscle my way in.”

lines.japanese:
携帯を手の中でくるりと回転させて握り直すと、
短縮の３を押した。
lines.english: He spun the phone once in his hand, caught it, and pressed speed dial three.

lines.japanese: （急がないと暗くなるな）
lines.english: (It'll be dark soon if I don't hurry.)

lines.japanese: 歩き出そうとして、しかし足は大地に張りついた。
lines.english: He tried to start walking, but his feet were rooted to the earth.
“…What……?”

lines.japanese: それは、瞬間だった。
lines.english: It happened in an instant.

lines.japanese:
夕刻。
　あるはずの、帰宅途中の人間の姿がない。
lines.english: Evening. There was no sign of the people who should have been making their way home.

lines.japanese: そんな刹那の空間だ。
lines.english: A space like that, for just an instant.

lines.japanese:
無風だった。
　車一台、通過しない。
　場は無音でいた。
lines.english: There was no wind. Not a single car passed. The place lay soundless.

lines.japanese:
ただ自分だけが、地表に蠢くものだった。
　そのことに気付いてしまった。
lines.english: He alone was a thing stirring on the face of the earth. And now he had realized it.
“Ah, ah, ah…”

lines.japanese:
圧倒されるしかない。
　矮小な身と精神で、横溢する緋色の狂気に抵抗が
できようものか。
lines.english: It overwhelmed him utterly. With body and mind so small, how could he resist the scarlet madness flooding all around him?

lines.japanese: （なん……だ……これ……なんだ、なんだ……？）
lines.english: (What… is… this…? What? What is it…?)

lines.japanese: 動かなかった足が、知らず駆けている。
lines.english: The legs that would not move were running before he knew it.

lines.japanese:
どこに向かっているのかわからない。
　当初の目的地ではないことだけは確かだ。
lines.english: He had no idea where they were carrying him. Only that it was not where he had meant to go.

lines.japanese:
狂乱の火に焼かれひた走る様は、気が触れた者の
それだ。
lines.english: Scorched by the fires of frenzy, he ran and ran— the very picture of a madman.

lines.japanese: （この感情は……ッッ！？）
lines.english: (What is this feeling…?!)

lines.japanese:
恐怖とも違う。
　怒りではない。
lines.english: It was not fear. Nor anger.

lines.japanese:
喜びや悲しみとも似つかない。
　予感とも過去ともつかない出来事が、流れ込んで
くる。
lines.english: It bore no resemblance to joy or sorrow. Events that might have been premonitions or might have belonged to the past came pouring into him.

lines.japanese:
個と群。
　群と個。
lines.english: The individual and the multitude. The multitude and the individual.

lines.japanese:
消えゆく人の意志。
　白色矮星のイメージ。
lines.english: Vanishing human wills. The image of a white dwarf.

lines.japanese:
光のはしご。
　空。
　闇。
lines.english: A ladder of light. Sky. Darkness.

lines.japanese:
ときほぐされる螺旋のイメージが、吐き気を催す。
　解体される人体を想起させるからだ。
lines.english: The image of an unraveling helix made him sick. It called to mind a human body being taken apart.

lines.japanese:
輝ける神の座。
　充ち満ちた孤独。
lines.english: The radiant throne of God. Loneliness, full to overflowing.

lines.japanese:
落ちくぼむ頭蓋。
　落ちくぼむ頭蓋の内側。
lines.english: A caving skull. The inside of the caving skull.

lines.japanese:
潰れていく。
　世界ではない何かが潰れていく。
lines.english: Something was collapsing. Something that was not the world was collapsing.

lines.japanese:
人々の脳が見えてしまう。
　萎縮していく。
lines.english: He could see people's brains. Shriveling away.

lines.japanese:
「ああああああああああああああああ
　ああああああああああああ―――！！」
lines.english: “Aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaah— aaaaaaaah—!!”

lines.japanese: 忍は泣いていた。
lines.english: Shinobu was crying.

lines.japanese: 何も理解できない。
lines.english: He understood nothing.

lines.japanese:
発作だった。
　世界で唯一、忍だけが味わう。
lines.english: It was a seizure. One experienced by Shinobu alone in all the world.

lines.japanese:
人類史に真実、個として残る虚無の病。
　助けられず、また助からない。
lines.english: A disease of the void, truly a solitary case in human history. No one could help him; there was no saving him.

lines.japanese: そのまま狂い往くのか、あるいは―――
lines.english: Would he simply go on into madness, or—

lines.japanese: そう、あるいは―――
lines.english: Yes. Or—

lines.japanese: 「ああ、あああ……ああ……」
lines.english: “Ah, aah… ah…”

lines.japanese:
壁に激突し、忍は転倒する。
　頭を打ち、しばらく芋虫のようにのたうちまわった。
lines.english: Shinobu crashed into a wall and fell. He struck his head and writhed like a caterpillar for some time.

lines.japanese: ゆっくりと身を起こし、幽鬼の足取りで逃げた。
lines.english: Slowly he pulled himself up, then fled with the gait of a ghost.

lines.japanese:
何から、どこへ、という問いが意味をなさないほ
ど無秩序に。
lines.english: He fled in such blind disorder that neither what he was fleeing nor where he was going had any meaning.
“…What the hell…”

lines.japanese: 嘆く。
lines.english: He moaned.
“…What the hell……”

lines.japanese:
足は向かう。
　無意識のうちに、安息の地へと。
lines.english: His feet carried him onward. Unconsciously, toward a place of refuge.

lines.japanese: 住宅街という奇形を抜けても、緋は追ってくる。
lines.english: Even after he left the deformity called a residential district behind, the scarlet pursued him.

lines.japanese:
燦然と輝く真紅の恐怖から、忍は逃れることはで
きない。
lines.english: Shinobu could not escape the brilliant, blazing terror of that crimson.

lines.japanese: 人が過去から逃れることができないように？
lines.english: As no one can escape the past?

lines.japanese: いや、違う。
lines.english: No. That was wrong.

lines.japanese: しっ
lines.english: lost

lines.japanese:
破滅の未来を幻視した者が、今を生きながら今を
失したようにである。
lines.english: It was like someone who had glimpsed a ruined future, living in the present while losing it.

lines.japanese:
世を焼く幻想は、それほど過酷に忍の背を撫でつ
けた。
lines.english: The vision of the burning world stroked Shinobu's back with terrible cruelty.

lines.japanese: そして、喘ぎながら工場の入り口に立つ。
lines.english: And so he stood gasping at the entrance to the factory.

lines.japanese: 扉は閉まっている。
lines.english: The door was closed.
“…Ah… ah…”

lines.japanese:
別の恐怖がある。
　そこに誰もいなかったなら。
lines.english: Another fear awaited him. What if there was no one inside?

lines.japanese: （ひとりだったら―――）
lines.english: (If I'm alone—)

lines.japanese: 身が竦んだ。
lines.english: His body froze.

lines.japanese: （死を、連想してしまう―――）
lines.english: (I'll think of death—)

lines.japanese:
夢想される死だが、現実に宿主を殺してしまうだ
ろう。
lines.english: An imagined death, but one that would surely kill its host in reality.

lines.japanese:
高次の幻想は殺傷力を秘めるものだ。
　火傷の錯覚が、実際に人を焼くように。
lines.english: Higher-order illusions harbored lethal force. Just as the illusion of a burn could truly sear the flesh.

lines.japanese:
だが、事ここに至って忍はいくぶん冷静さを取り
戻す。
lines.english: Only then did Shinobu recover a measure of his composure.
(…Death.)

lines.japanese: （死……だけどそれは……無だ……）
lines.english: (Death… but death is… nothingness…)

lines.japanese: （暗闇だ）
lines.english: (Darkness.)

lines.japanese: （死は怖くない……孤独が怖いんだ……）
lines.english: (I'm not afraid of death… I'm afraid of being alone…)

lines.japanese: （だから落ち着け、貴宮忍）
lines.english: (So calm down, Shinobu Atemiya.)

lines.japanese:
（おまえが、何を取り戻そうとしているか、
　思い出せ―――）
lines.english: (Remember what it is you're trying to get back—)

lines.japanese: 扉にすがる。
lines.english: He clung to the door.

lines.japanese:
大きく呼吸を繰り返す。
　呼気に揺れる肩の上下が、小さくなっていく。
lines.english: He took deep breath after deep breath. The rise and fall of his shoulders gradually eased.

lines.japanese:
やがて持ち上げられた顔は、若干青ざめてはいた
が、理性を宿していた。
lines.english: When he raised his head at last, his face was a little pale, but reason had returned to it.

lines.japanese: 奇しくも、工場にいる。
lines.english: By some strange chance, he had ended up at the factory.

lines.japanese:
すでに冷静ではあるが、振り向く気力がわいてこ
ない。
lines.english: He was calm again, but could not summon the strength to turn around.

lines.japanese:
日暮れまであと少し。
　孤独でもいい。
lines.english: Only a little time remained before sunset. It did not matter if he was alone.

lines.japanese: 忍は扉にかけた手に、力を込めた。
lines.english: Shinobu tightened his grip on the door.

lines.japanese: そこに、斎が立っていた。
lines.english: Itsuki stood there.
“…Itsuki?”

lines.japanese: 呆気ない、邂逅であった。
lines.english: Their reunion was almost anticlimactic.

lines.japanese:
問いつめたいと思っていた。
　話したいことがあった。
lines.english: Shinobu had meant to demand answers. There were things he wanted to say.

lines.japanese:
全て、どうでもよくなってしまった。
　落ち着いた斎の雰囲気が、工場に広がっていた。
lines.english: Suddenly none of it mattered. Itsuki's tranquility suffused the factory.

lines.japanese:
長くここにいたようだ。
　忍にはそれがわかった。
lines.english: Itsuki seemed to have been here a long time. Shinobu could tell.

lines.japanese:
理解できるとともに、今までの悩みとつらみが些
細なことになった。
lines.english: The realization made all the worry and pain that had plagued him until now seem trivial.

lines.japanese: 「久しぶりって、気がする……」
lines.english: “It feels like… it's been a long time.”

lines.japanese: 少年は顎を引くような仕草で、照れくさげに頷く。
lines.english: The boy ducked his chin and nodded, almost bashfully.

lines.japanese:
奥へ、と忍を招いた。
　拒絶する理由はない。
lines.english: He invited Shinobu farther inside. There was no reason to refuse.

lines.japanese:
自分の椅子に座って待っていると、二人分飲み物
を持って斎がやってきた。
lines.english: Shinobu sat waiting in his own chair until Itsuki returned with drinks for them both.

lines.japanese: マグカップにはいささか不釣り合いな……緑茶だ。
lines.english: Green tea—rather incongruous in a mug.

lines.japanese: 熱い。
lines.english: Hot.

lines.japanese:
恐怖と興奮で萎縮した胃に流し込む。
　全身のこわばりがときほぐされ、忍はくつろいだ
気分になった。
lines.english: He poured it into his stomach, clenched tight by fear and excitement. The tightness throughout his body slowly unraveled, and Shinobu began to relax.

lines.japanese: 「おいしい」
lines.english: “It's good.”

lines.japanese:
ただ一言だけでありながら充分な言葉が、ゆった
りと空を漂った。
lines.english: Those two simple words said all they needed to as they drifted languidly through the air.

lines.japanese:
斎はしゃんと背を伸ばし、カップを持った腕だけ
を口元に運ぶ。
lines.english: Itsuki sat perfectly straight. Keeping the rest of his body still, he raised the cup to his lips.

lines.japanese:
その姿はひどく大人びて、一抹の哀愁を忍に抱か
せた。
lines.english: He looked terribly grown-up, stirring in Shinobu a faint melancholy.

lines.japanese:
貴重な瞬間だと感じた。
　ずっとこのまま、語らっていてもいい。
　友達と話すのは楽しいものだ。
lines.english: The moment felt precious. They could have gone on talking like this forever. It was good to talk with a friend.

lines.japanese:
ただ残念なことに、斎は少々無口すぎた。
　それでも二人きりとなれば、重い口を開くことも
あった。昔のように。
lines.english: Unfortunately, Itsuki was a little too taciturn. Still, when it was just the two of them, he sometimes found his voice, as he had in the old days.

lines.japanese: 「……何か、話をしようか」
lines.english: “…Want to talk about something?”

lines.japanese: 斎は首肯する。
lines.english: Itsuki nodded.

lines.japanese:
それからしばらくは、二人のぼそぼそとしたやり
とりが続く。
lines.english: For a while after that, the two carried on a quiet, muttered exchange.

lines.japanese:
驚くほど心が穏やかになっていた。
　きっと斎を見つけることができたからだ。
lines.english: Shinobu's heart had grown astonishingly calm. Surely because he had managed to find Itsuki.
“…Kadokura, huh…?”

lines.japanese:
つい、と傾きがちな面が持ち上がる。
　そこに忍は、強い意志を見た。
　微笑さえ浮かべていた。
lines.english: Itsuki raised his habitually downcast face by a fraction. Shinobu saw a powerful resolve there. There was even a smile.

lines.japanese:
大丈夫、と。
　心配するな、と。
lines.english: I'm all right, it said. Don't worry.

lines.japanese: そんなことを彼なりの言葉で告げた。
lines.english: He conveyed all that in his own language.

lines.japanese: 「……どういう、大丈夫なんだか」
lines.english: “…What do you mean, ‘all right’?”

lines.japanese: 言われた方が当事者よりもつらくなる。
lines.english: It hurt the one hearing it more than the one caught up in it.

lines.japanese:
「いいように使われて……
　危険なことだってあるだろうに」
lines.english: “They're using you however they please… It could get dangerous.”

lines.japanese:
微笑は崩れない。
　危険を受け入れた者の顔だ。
lines.english: The smile did not falter. It was the face of someone who had accepted the danger.

lines.japanese:
力が抜けそうになる。
　仲間のために自らを前に出すのは、忍の専売とい
うわけではなかったのだ。
lines.english: Shinobu nearly went limp. He had no monopoly, it seemed, on putting himself in danger for his friends.

lines.japanese: （……なんだよ）
lines.english: (…What the hell.)

lines.japanese:
（僕なんかより、全然ちゃんとしてる
　じゃないか……）
lines.english: (You're so much more put together than I am…)

lines.japanese: （同じことを、思っているのに）
lines.english: (Even though I feel the same way.)

lines.japanese:
悲しさよりも誇りが、悔しさよりも安堵が訪れた。
　斎を取り戻して、葉子に返してやりたいと思って
いたのに。
lines.english: Pride eclipsed his sorrow; relief, his frustration. He had meant to win Itsuki back and return him to Youko.

lines.japanese: 今はもう、すっかり斎を信じたい気分で。
lines.english: But now he wanted nothing more than to trust Itsuki completely.

lines.japanese: 見てしまったのは、
lines.english: What he saw was—

lines.japanese:
「はは……ひとりで……
　空回りしすぎた……か―――」
lines.english: “Ha… Maybe I've just been… spinning my wheels all by myself—”

lines.japanese: そのときだった。
lines.english: That was when it happened.

lines.japanese:
目線が一点に、癒着した。
　舌が固まり、空気が凍りつく。
lines.english: His gaze fixed on a single point as if fused there. His tongue stiffened. The air froze.
“Itsuki…”

lines.japanese:
ようやっと押し出した声が、歪な波形を描いてい
るとわかった。
lines.english: He knew the voice he had finally forced out was tracing some grotesquely distorted waveform.

lines.japanese: はて、と首を傾げる斎。仕草が葉子と似ている。
lines.english: Itsuki cocked his head in puzzlement. The gesture resembled Youko's.

lines.japanese: そんな発見も、今は笑えない。
lines.english: Even that discovery could not make him laugh now.

lines.japanese:
どころか、叫びだしたいくらいだ。
　いや、と思いとどまる。
lines.english: Quite the opposite: he wanted to scream. No, he told himself, and held back.

lines.japanese: （……勘違いってことも……ある）
lines.english: (…I could be… mistaken.)

lines.japanese: （たまたま怪我をしたとか）
lines.english: (Maybe he just happened to hurt himself.)

lines.japanese: （たまたま、誰かのを被ったとか）
lines.english: (Maybe someone else's blood just got on him.)

lines.japanese: （でもそのどちらも―――）
lines.english: (But either way—)

lines.japanese:
千々に乱れる思考を、意志ではない何か別の力
でねじ伏せて、声帯を操る。
lines.english: He forced his scattered thoughts into submission with some power other than will and set his vocal cords moving.

lines.japanese: それはきっと恐怖だったのだと思われた。
lines.english: He thought that force must have been fear.

lines.japanese: 「……斎、そでのところ」
lines.english: “…Itsuki. Your sleeve.”

lines.japanese: 言われて確認した斎の動作が、ぴたりと止まった。
lines.english: Itsuki looked where Shinobu had indicated—and stopped dead.

lines.japanese: （そのどちらもが―――）
lines.english: (Either way—)

lines.japanese: （人と争った結果じゃないか）
lines.english: (It would mean he'd fought someone.)

lines.japanese: 一つの明確なビジョンが、像を結んだ。
lines.english: One clear vision took shape.

lines.japanese:
門倉は斎を使って、猟奇殺人を調査していると言
った。
lines.english: Kadokura had said he was using Itsuki to investigate the bizarre murder case.

lines.japanese:
いつから調査しているのだろう。
　事件はなお続いている。
　誰も犯人の姿を見ることはできない。
lines.english: How long had the investigation been underway? The incidents were still continuing. No one had been able to see the culprit.

lines.japanese:
斎は何も言わない。
　弁解もしない。
lines.english: Itsuki said nothing. He offered no excuse.

lines.japanese: やがて視線をゆっくりゆっくり忍に戻し、微苦笑。
lines.english: At last, slowly, slowly, he raised his eyes to Shinobu and gave a faint, rueful smile.

lines.japanese: （ああ―――斎、君は）
lines.english: (Oh—Itsuki. You…)

lines.japanese: 泣きそうになった。
lines.english: Shinobu nearly wept.

lines.japanese: 「平気？」
lines.english: “Are you okay?”

lines.japanese:
軽く手を振って、何でもないことを示す。
　言い訳一つしないのはいつも通り。
lines.english: Itsuki gave a little wave to say it was nothing. As always, he did not offer a word in his own defense.

lines.japanese:
袖を隠そうとしない態度も好感が持てる。
　もし弁解を口にするようであれば、かえって異常
を際立たせることになったはずだ。
lines.english: Shinobu liked the way Itsuki made no attempt to hide the sleeve. Any excuse he might have offered would only have made the whole thing seem stranger.

lines.japanese: 斎は冷静だった。
lines.english: Itsuki was calm.

lines.japanese: 冷静すぎた。
lines.english: Too calm.

lines.japanese: 「怪我かな？」
lines.english: “Are you hurt?”

lines.japanese:
わからない、と首を振った。
　まったくおかしなところのない、塚本斎である。
lines.english: He shook his head to say he did not know. There was nothing strange about him at all. This was Itsuki Tsukamoto.

lines.japanese:
おかしくないはずの斎が、確たる決意のもと、無
言を決め込んでいた。
lines.english: Yet this Itsuki, who ought not to have been strange at all, had firmly resolved to say nothing.

lines.japanese: 忍は友に、隠し事をされていると悟った。
lines.english: Shinobu realized his friend was hiding something from him.

lines.japanese:
どんな理由があったのか。
　どんな経緯によるものか。
lines.english: Whatever the reason. Whatever path had brought him here.

lines.japanese: この斎は語るまい。
lines.english: This Itsuki would not speak.

lines.japanese: 視野が音もなく傾く。
lines.english: His field of vision tilted soundlessly.

lines.japanese:
忠実な友人でいてくれた、この数年間。
　忍は彼らから実に多くを学び、歩んできた。
　ぎこちない友情だった。
lines.english: For the past several years, they had stood by him as faithful friends. Shinobu had learned so much from them and come so far. Theirs had been an awkward friendship.

lines.japanese:
距離感に戸惑い、語るに躊躇し、結果だけを押し
つけてきた。
lines.english: He had fumbled over the distance between them, hesitated to speak, then forced his conclusions on them.

lines.japanese:
気恥ずかしいばかりの思い出を積み上げた。
　青々とした少年時代を共有したことで、彼らは互
いを肯定できたのだった。
lines.english: They had piled up one embarrassing memory after another. By sharing those green years of boyhood, they had learned to affirm one another.

lines.japanese:
が今、二人の間に溝が掘られた。
　斎が掘ったものかも知れず、忍の気持ちによるも
のかも知れない。
lines.english: But now a gulf had opened between them. Perhaps Itsuki had dug it; perhaps it had been born of Shinobu's own feelings.

lines.japanese:
嫌いなわけはない。
　だというのに、別離を予感させた。
lines.english: It was not that he hated him. And yet he sensed a parting ahead.
“…Itsuki.”

lines.japanese:
空気が陰鬱を含み、湿り気を帯びる。
　ねっとりと粘度を増し、肌にまとわりついた。
lines.english: The air grew damp with gloom. It grew thick and viscous, clinging to his skin.

lines.japanese: 「僕は君を」
lines.english: “I want to…”

lines.japanese:
いろいろな単語を選んでは捨てた。
　結局、もっともシンプルなものが生存した。
lines.english: He chose and discarded word after word. In the end, only the simplest survived.

lines.japanese: 「止めたい」
lines.english: “Stop you.”

lines.japanese: 「……そうしたい」
lines.english: “…That's what I want.”

lines.japanese:
緑茶はもう湯気を立てない。
　冷めてしまった。
　二人が冷静でいるように。
lines.english: The green tea no longer steamed. It had gone cold. As cool as the two of them.

lines.japanese:
絆などというものは、一時のもの、ただ過去にそ
うであったことに価値があるような……意義にも類
する行為だ。
lines.english: A bond was a transient thing, an act whose only value —whose only meaning—lay in having existed in the past.

lines.japanese: また忍も、そんな考え方を喜々として掲げていた。
lines.english: Shinobu too had once brandished that philosophy with glee.

lines.japanese: 「……詳細は、いいんだ……」
lines.english: “…I don't need the details…”

lines.japanese: 言葉にするたび、考え方がまとまっていく。
lines.english: Each time he put it into words, his thoughts came together.

lines.japanese: 斎を止める。
lines.english: Stop Itsuki.

lines.japanese: その終端に向かって、方法が束ねられていく。
lines.english: Every possible means began to converge on that single end.

lines.japanese:
大切なものは、ただ一つ。
　全てが得られないのだから、ただ一つ。
　選べるものは、ただ一つ。
lines.english: Only one thing mattered. He could not have everything, so there could be only one. Only one thing he could choose.

lines.japanese: 「君を、止められれば、いい」
lines.english: “All I need… is to stop you.”

lines.japanese:
斎は首を左右に振って拒絶する。
　止まらない。やめない。
　そう言っている。
lines.english: Itsuki shook his head in refusal. He would not stop. He would not quit. That was what he was saying.

lines.japanese: 「いや、僕はもう決めたんだ……」
lines.english: “No. I've already decided…”

lines.japanese: 「それが君の選んだことであっても……」
lines.english: “Even if this is what you chose…”

lines.japanese: 「善であっても悪であっても構わない」
lines.english: “I don't care whether it's good or evil.”

lines.japanese: 「斎の身柄だけを、保護できればいい」
lines.english: “If I can just take custody of you, that's enough.”

lines.japanese: 「そのあとのことは……」
lines.english: “As for what comes after…”

lines.japanese:
ぼんやりと宙を眺めて考える。
　答えは出なかった。
lines.english: He stared vaguely into space and thought. No answer came.

lines.japanese: 「……あとで考えよう」
lines.english: “…I'll think about that later.”

lines.japanese:
「だから……今ここで、僕は……
　君を止めてしまうことにする」
lines.english: “So… here and now, I've decided… to stop you.”

lines.japanese: 忍は立ち上がる。
lines.english: Shinobu stood.

lines.japanese:
対して斎は座ったままでいる。
　前髪で隠れた目線が見えない。
lines.english: Itsuki, by contrast, remained seated. Shinobu could not see the eyes hidden by his bangs.

lines.japanese: 「葉子と一緒に、ずっと僕のそばにいるべきだ、斎」
lines.english: “You and Youko should always stay by my side, Itsuki.”

lines.japanese: 「世の中のことは、どうでもいい」
lines.english: “I don't care about the rest of the world.”

lines.japanese: 「なんとかする」
lines.english: “I'll find a way.”
“So—”

lines.japanese: しかし斎は、肯うことはなかった。
lines.english: But Itsuki did not assent.
“…I see.”

lines.japanese: 静かに、息を吐き出した。
lines.english: Shinobu let out a quiet breath.

lines.japanese:
そしてポケットから、小さな模型銃のようなもの
を取り出す。
lines.english: Then he drew something like a tiny model gun from his pocket.

lines.japanese: テーザー銃だ。
lines.english: A TASER.

lines.japanese:
スタンガンの一種で、無用な電光を生じさせず、
威嚇効果の一切を省いた完全鎮圧目的で用いられる
ものである。
lines.english: A kind of stun gun, it produced no superfluous arcs of electricity, dispensed with intimidation altogether, and was designed solely to subdue its target.

lines.japanese:
マイオトロンと同様、実際に行使することのみに
機能が絞られている。
lines.english: Like a Myotron, it was designed for one thing only: actual use.

lines.japanese:
それは侵略の証だ。
　相手の自由を剥奪する器物だ。
lines.english: It was proof of invasion. An instrument for stripping another of freedom.

lines.japanese:
絆と侵略に変わるところなどない。
　肯定するか拒絶するか、いずれかでしかない。
lines.english: There was no essential difference between a bond and an invasion. One could only accept it or refuse it.

lines.japanese: 「なら、力ずくで留め置こう」
lines.english: “Then I'll hold you here by force.”

lines.japanese: 優しく銃を構える。
lines.english: Gently, Shinobu leveled the gun.

lines.japanese:
斎は反応しない。
　座ったまま。とうに決着はついてしまったかのよ
うだ。
lines.english: Itsuki did not react. He remained seated, as if the outcome had been settled long ago.

lines.japanese:
斎に逆転する術は―――いや、そもそも逆転する
必要が、最初からあったのかどうか。
lines.english: Did Itsuki have any way to turn the tables—or rather, had there ever been any need for him to do so?

lines.japanese:
前髪に隠れる双眸は、影に沈んでかすかに波打つ。
それは涙か。あるいは虹彩のきらめきか。
lines.english: His eyes, hidden beneath his bangs, lay drowned in shadow; a faint ripple crossed them. Were those tears? Or the glimmer of his irises?
“…Itsuki.”

lines.japanese: 工場は粛として音もなく、来るべき時を待っていた。
lines.english: The factory waited in solemn silence for what was to come.

lines.japanese: 未来が嫌いだった。
lines.english: He hated the future.

lines.japanese: 見通しのない明日が苦手だった。
lines.english: He could not abide a tomorrow he could not foresee.

lines.japanese:
決して今を生きようとはしなかった。
　絆は積み重ねである。
　過ぎ去ったことがらである。
lines.english: He had never once tried to live in the present. A bond was something built layer by layer. It belonged to what had already passed.

lines.japanese:
先を見れば、永続の保証のないものである。
　そして出会った瞬間に、生まれるものでもない。
lines.english: Looking ahead, there was no guarantee it would last. Nor could a bond spring into being the moment two people met.

lines.japanese:
今という瞬間から振り返り、連綿と重ねられてき
た皮膜の厚みを、喜びをもって見るものが絆なのだ。
lines.english: A bond was the joy of looking back from the present and seeing how thick those unbroken layers had grown.

lines.japanese:
明日を憎む気持ち。
　過去を慈しむ気持ち。
lines.english: His hatred of tomorrow. His tenderness for the past.

lines.japanese:
二つは親和し、心中にてかたい結び目となる。
　人間・貴宮忍の、それは全てと言えた。
lines.english: The two feelings fused into a hard knot inside him. For the human being Shinobu Atemiya, that knot was everything.

lines.japanese: 「失う、わけには、もう―――」
lines.english: “I can't… lose… not again—”

lines.japanese: 声が震える。
lines.english: His voice trembled.

lines.japanese: 「これを、失うわけには」
lines.english: “I can't lose this.”

lines.japanese: ゆっくりと、非現実的な夕日の色がくすんでいく。
lines.english: Slowly, the unreal color of the sunset began to dim.

lines.japanese: 暮れる―――
lines.english: Night fell—

lines.japanese:
斎がゆっくりと膝を伸ばした。
　忍の目にそれは、まるでスローがかって見える。
lines.english: Itsuki slowly straightened his knees. To Shinobu, he seemed to move in slow motion.

lines.japanese:
老人を思わせる、弱々しい動作。
　忍は警戒の必要性をまったく感じなかった。
lines.english: It was the feeble movement of an old man. Shinobu felt no need whatsoever to be on guard.

lines.japanese:
しかし実際は、優れた動きだった。
　ゆるやかに見えていただけだ。
lines.english: In truth, however, it was a masterful movement. It had merely looked slow.

lines.japanese: 忍は知らない。
lines.english: Shinobu did not know.

lines.japanese:
古武術の伝える、余人に錯覚を引き起こす動作……
刹那に対する技術を。
lines.english: He knew nothing of the movement preserved in the old martial arts—one designed to deceive the observer… a technique for exploiting the instant.

lines.japanese:
認知のズレは半秒を稼ぐ。
　相手の認識より半呼吸分早く行動できる。
lines.english: That gap in perception bought half a second. It let one move half a breath ahead of the opponent's awareness.

lines.japanese:
それは接近戦においては大きなアドバンテージで
ある。
lines.english: In close combat, that was an enormous advantage.

lines.japanese:
実際のところ、斎は忍の呼吸を見ながら一瞬で立
ち上がった。
lines.english: In fact, Itsuki had watched Shinobu's breathing and risen in an instant at precisely the right moment.

lines.japanese: 決して、反応できない半秒を選んで。
lines.english: He had chosen a half-second in which Shinobu could not possibly react.
“Huh…?”

lines.japanese: 両者は対峙する。
lines.english: The two faced one another.

lines.japanese:
座していたことのマイナスは消えた。
　忍の優位性は、手にした遠隔攻撃手段だけとなった。
lines.english: The disadvantage of having been seated was gone. Shinobu's only remaining edge was the ranged weapon in his hand.

lines.japanese:
（どうする？　どうする？　斎が、抵抗する？
　……どうする？　どうしたらいい？）
lines.english: (What do I do? What do I do? Itsuki's going to resist? …What do I do? What am I supposed to do?)

lines.japanese: 予期せぬ困惑が訪れていた。
lines.english: Unexpected confusion seized him.

lines.japanese:
相手は友人だ。
　説得がベストであり、武器を用いるというのは最
後の手段だった。
lines.english: This was his friend. Persuasion was the best course; using a weapon was the last resort.

lines.japanese:
反撃は忍の予想になかった。
　覚悟はしていても、咄嗟には動かないのが引き金
にかけた指というものだ。
lines.english: Shinobu had never expected him to fight back. However prepared he was, the finger on the trigger would not move on reflex alone.

lines.japanese: この混乱によりさらに半秒のロス。
lines.english: His confusion cost him another half-second.

lines.japanese: 一秒―――
lines.english: One second—

lines.japanese: 必要にして充分な時間だ。
lines.english: Necessary—and sufficient.

lines.japanese: 斎の身が沈んだ。
lines.english: Itsuki's body sank.
“……What?”

lines.japanese: ほとんど反応できなかった。
lines.english: Shinobu was barely able to react.

lines.japanese:
動作の切り替えには、一瞬の溜めがある。
　反復運動の際、身体と筋肉にかかる種々の負担が
そうさせる。
lines.english: Every change from one movement to another requires a split-second pause. The strain that repetitive motion places on the body and muscles makes that inevitable.

lines.japanese:
見ている側にも、同様の認識がある。
　この認識より早いタイミングで切り替わる動きを
見た時、認知上の戸惑いが起こる。
lines.english: The observer shares that expectation. When a movement changes sooner than expected, the mind hesitates.

lines.japanese:
ほとんど棒立ちに近い状態に忍は陥った。
　重力を利用したのだと、直感が告げた。斎は膝を
抜いただけなのだ。
lines.english: Shinobu was left standing almost perfectly still. Instinct told him Itsuki had used gravity. He had merely let his knees give way.

lines.japanese:
単に落下を制した運動も、訓練によって魔術の類
と大差ない精度を持つ。
lines.english: With training, even a controlled fall could be executed with a precision little different from magic.

lines.japanese: 人体最速の運動で、曲線を描く。
lines.english: The fastest movement the human body could produce followed a curve.

lines.japanese: 門倉流組討・駆術・上弦―――
lines.english: Kadokura School of Grappling—Kakejutsu: Waxing Moon—

lines.japanese: かすかな前への勢いをつけて、斎は落ち、跳ねた。
lines.english: With the faintest forward momentum, Itsuki dropped—and sprang.

lines.japanese:
滑らかな動きは半月を連想させる。
　斎の重心は腕状の軌跡を描き、忍の懐に終着して
のけた。
lines.english: The fluid movement called to mind a half-moon. Itsuki's center of gravity traced an arc, ending neatly inside Shinobu's guard.

lines.japanese: 手の甲、だった。
lines.english: The back of his hand.

lines.japanese: テーザー銃を腕ごと、柔らかくずらしたのは。
lines.english: That was what gently swept the TASER aside, arm and all.

lines.japanese:
全身の筋肉が力む間もない。それが訪れるのには、
あと０．２７秒が必要だったからだ。
lines.english: There was not even time for the muscles throughout Shinobu's body to tense. They required another 0.27 seconds.

lines.japanese: 身構える瞬間を、いともたやすく外されていた。
lines.english: Itsuki had effortlessly robbed Shinobu of the instant he needed to brace himself.

lines.japanese:
なすがままに水平に滑った手は、半秒遅れて反射
運動を示した。
lines.english: Shinobu's hand, swept helplessly sideways, twitched in reflex half a second late.

lines.japanese: 引き金を引いたのだ。
lines.english: He pulled the trigger.

lines.japanese: テーザー銃はスタンガンの一種である。
lines.english: A TASER is a kind of stun gun.

lines.japanese:
危険がまったくないとは言わないが、より最悪の
結果を招くよりはと思って携行していたものだ。
lines.english: It was not entirely without danger, but Shinobu carried it in the hope of avoiding a far worse outcome.

lines.japanese:
かつては国内販売はされていなかったが、最近で
は登録すれば誰でも入手できる。
lines.english: Once unavailable for domestic sale, anyone could now obtain one by registering.

lines.japanese:
そのかわり使用記録の義務があり、犯罪性は抑制
されている。
lines.english: In exchange, every use had to be logged, which discouraged criminal use.

lines.japanese:
そういう類の非致死性武器である。
　装弾数というものはない。
lines.english: It was that sort of nonlethal weapon. The very idea of ammunition capacity did not apply.

lines.japanese:
ただ一度きりの使い捨て。即ち、タイミングを外
された一撃は虚しく中空にまき散らされた。
lines.english: It was disposable, good for a single use. Thrown off its timing, that one shot scattered uselessly through empty air.

lines.japanese:
飛び出した電極は斎の体をとらえることはなく、
忍の鎮圧能力はこの瞬間失われた。
lines.english: The electrodes shot wide of Itsuki, and in that instant Shinobu lost his means of subduing him.

lines.japanese:
してみれば早期に能動的防御運動を仕掛けてきた
ことも、動揺を誘うための布石の一つだったと考え
るべきだろう。
lines.english: Seen in that light, Itsuki's decision to move first in his own defense must have been one more calculated step meant to unsettle him.

lines.japanese: 忍は駆け引きに負けた。
lines.english: Shinobu had lost the contest of wits.

lines.japanese: 同じ土俵にさえ入っていなかった。
lines.english: He had never even entered the ring.

lines.japanese:
止めるという行為の上澄みだけで、斎を説得しよ
うとした。
lines.english: He had tried to persuade Itsuki with nothing but the shallowest notion of what stopping him actually meant.

lines.japanese:
もし忍が機械であったなら、斎の運動に意味づけ
を行うこともなく、外される機もまた存在しない。
lines.english: Had Shinobu been a machine, he would have assigned no meaning to Itsuki's motion, and there would have been no moment in which to throw him off.

lines.japanese: 迎撃は成立していたかも知れない。
lines.english: His interception might have succeeded.
“…Itsuki—!”

lines.japanese:
術理もなくつかみかかる。
　取り押さえる形ばかりの、意志なき動きで。
　己とともに斎の姿を見失うことになった―――
lines.english: He lunged at him without art or method. The movement had the shape of a restraint, but no will behind it. He lost sight of Itsuki—and of himself—
“Huh…?”

lines.japanese: 気が付けば……半身すれ違う形で、隣に斎がいる。
lines.english: Before he knew it… Itsuki was beside him, their bodies halfway past each other.

lines.japanese: 首の下に、手が差し込まれていた。
lines.english: A hand had slipped beneath his throat.
(What… are you doing?)

lines.japanese:
声に出したつもりだった。
　しかし声帯は機能しなかった。
lines.english: He thought he had spoken aloud. But his vocal cords would not work.
(My throat…?)

lines.japanese:
夜の黒みとは異なった影が、視野の上から帳の如
く降りてきた。
lines.english: A shadow unlike the blackness of night descended like a curtain over his vision.
(…What… is this…?)

lines.japanese:
苦しくはない。
　痛くはない。
lines.english: There was no discomfort. It did not hurt.

lines.japanese: ただ……おかしいとだけ感じられた。
lines.english: It merely… felt wrong.
(…I'm being knocked—)

lines.japanese:
最後に忍が見たものは、血に濡れて赤黒く染まっ
た袖口。
lines.english: The last thing Shinobu saw was a cuff soaked in blood, stained a blackish red.
(No—)

lines.japanese: 発する言葉もなく、心は閉じた。
lines.english: With no words left to utter, his mind closed.

lines.japanese: 意識を喪失したのを見て、そっと手を抜く。
lines.english: Seeing that Shinobu had lost consciousness, Itsuki gently withdrew his hand.

lines.japanese:
力を失った体を抱き起こし、ソファに寝かせて、
シーツをかけた。
lines.english: He lifted the limp body, laid it on the sofa, and covered it with a sheet.

lines.japanese: 見下ろす視線に、一片の侮蔑も悪意もありはしない。
lines.english: There was not a trace of contempt or malice in his downward gaze.

lines.japanese:
夜気を纏った斎の顔は、苦渋とも怒気ともつかな
い硬質のそれだ。
lines.english: Wrapped in the night air, Itsuki’s face was hard, his expression neither quite anguish nor quite anger.

lines.japanese:
やがて少年は、腰を折った。
　意識のない忍に対し深々と頭を下げる。
　敬うように―――
lines.english: At last the boy bent at the waist. He bowed deeply to the unconscious Shinobu. As though before one he revered—

lines.japanese:
次いで踵を切り返し、背を向けた。
　表情が一変していた。
lines.english: Then he pivoted on his heel and turned his back. His expression had changed completely.

lines.japanese: 決然と、胸に覚悟を秘めた者の顔だった。
lines.english: It was the resolute face of someone who had steeled himself.

lines.japanese: 歩く。
lines.english: He walked.

lines.japanese: 入口のところに葉子が立っていた。
lines.english: Youko stood at the entrance.

lines.japanese:
二人は兄妹でありながら、互いに言葉一つかわさ
ず……交差していった。
lines.english: Brother and sister though they were, they passed each other without a single word…

lines.japanese:
二度と交わらないようにも、受け取れる行為では
なかったろうか？
lines.english: Could their passing not be read as a sign that their paths would never cross again?

lines.japanese:
咎める者は、意識を放棄していた。
　斎の姿が夜陰に乗じ消えてから、葉子は掠れた息
を吐き出した。
lines.english: The only one who might have reproached them lay unconscious. Only after Itsuki vanished under the cover of night did Youko release a ragged breath.

lines.japanese: 「……兄さん」
lines.english: “…Brother.”

lines.japanese:
その憐憫を、妹が兄に投げかけることは許されな
かったのである。
lines.english: His sister was not permitted to show him that pity.

lines.japanese: （いない……か）
lines.english: (So he's not here…)

lines.japanese:
斎の姿がないことで、しかし門倉屋敷に変化が訪
れた様子はない。
lines.english: Yet Itsuki's absence had brought no apparent change to the Kadokura estate.

lines.japanese:
人工的とも思える和の静寂に、石を踏む音さえ浮
き彫りにされそうだった。
lines.english: Against a Japanese stillness that seemed almost artificial, even the sound of a footstep on stone might have stood out in sharp relief.
(Itsuki…)

lines.japanese: だが確かに、このような場所にいるはずもない。
lines.english: But of course Itsuki could not possibly be in a place like this.

lines.japanese:
気休めであった。
　門倉のこともあるが、葉子のことも気に掛かった。
lines.english: It was only for his own peace of mind. Kadokura worried him, but so did Youko.

lines.japanese:
だから忍ぶようにして、様子を見に来たのである。
　事件解決への期待を込めての行動ではなかった。
lines.english: That was why he had slipped in to see how things stood. He had not come expecting to solve the case.

lines.japanese:
単に心に残る未練の気泡が、精神にわずかな劣化
―――情をもたらしただけのことだ。
lines.english: A lingering bubble of attachment had merely caused a slight deterioration in his mind—emotion.

lines.japanese:
門倉の庭にいると、世に音が満ちていることさえ
疑わしくなってくる。
lines.english: In the Kadokura garden, he could almost doubt that the world was full of sound at all.

lines.japanese:
思考がどこまでも澄んでいく。
　波立たない水面のような精神状態は、少年時代を
思い返させて懐かしく、また悲しかった。
lines.english: His thoughts grew clearer and clearer. His mind, still as an unruffled surface of water, carried him back to his boyhood with nostalgia—and sorrow.

lines.japanese: かつての生は、諦めとともにあった。
lines.english: His earlier life had been one of resignation.

lines.japanese:
諦念が彼を年齢よりも落ち着かせ、稚気を喪失さ
せた。
lines.english: Resignation had made him calmer than his years and robbed him of childishness.

lines.japanese:
誉められるべきものではない。
　人間性を放棄していることであり、心には巨大な
虚無をこじあけるものでもあった。
lines.english: There was nothing admirable in that. It was a surrender of his humanity, one that tore a vast void open in his heart.

lines.japanese:
ぎこちなくも健全な関係性に寄らねば、埋まるこ
とのない隙間だった。
lines.english: A void only awkward but wholesome human bonds could ever fill.

lines.japanese:
行かねばならない。
　止めねばならない。
lines.english: He had to go. He had to stop it.

lines.japanese:
失われた安息を蘇生するために。
　かすかな貢献でしかないとしても。
lines.english: To restore the refuge he had lost. Even if his contribution was only slight.

lines.japanese: 縁に人が立った。
lines.english: A figure appeared on the veranda.

lines.japanese:
今いる場所は、死角となっていて見つかることは
ない。
lines.english: He stood in a blind spot. There was no chance of being seen.

lines.japanese:
葉子だった。
　胸が締められるかすかな音を聞いた。
lines.english: It was Youko. He heard the faint sound of his heart tightening.

lines.japanese:
葉子はぼんやりと庭を眺めている。
　特に怪しんでいる様子はないことから、空気を吸
いに出てきたものと推察された。
lines.english: Youko gazed absently out across the garden. There was no sign of suspicion. He supposed she had merely come outside for some air.

lines.japanese: ほどなくして葉子は再び室内に戻っていく。
lines.english: Before long, she went back inside.

lines.japanese:
（けど、見つからないうちに立ち去った方が良さそ
　うだ）
lines.english: (Still, I'd better go before she sees me.)

lines.japanese: 仮に見つかっても、どうということもないのだろう。
lines.english: Even if she did find him, nothing would likely come of it.

lines.japanese:
不法侵入は咎められるかも知れないが、葉子は許
すはずだ。
lines.english: She might rebuke him for trespassing, but Youko would surely forgive him.

lines.japanese:
ただ……鈍さを自認する妹が、時に兄など及びも
つかない鋭敏さを発揮することは、貴宮忍も認める
ところである。
lines.english: Still… even Shinobu had to admit that Youko, slow by her own account, could sometimes show a keenness her brother could never hope to match.

lines.japanese:
無用な心配をさせる必要はない。そう思った。
　自分の問題である。そうも思っていた。
lines.english: There was no reason to worry her needlessly. Or so he thought. This was his problem. Or so he believed.

lines.japanese: 調査の拠点には、駅前を使っていた。
lines.english: He had been using the area outside the station as his base for the investigation.

lines.japanese:
携帯が着信を告げた。
　通話ではなく、添付メールのようだ。二件。どち
らも貴宮千鳥からのものだ。
lines.english: His phone announced an incoming message. Not a call. Two emails, apparently with attachments—both from Chidori Atemiya.

lines.japanese: 確認する。
lines.english: He checked them.

lines.japanese: 一件目―――
lines.english: The first—

lines.japanese:
TITLE:依頼の件
　
　
　依頼の件について。
　確認を。
lines.english: SUBJECT: Your request   Regarding your request. Please review the following.

lines.japanese:
市内に限定し、主要な有段者を調査。
　死後一年以上経過したものは除外。
　また本籍が本市にない者については調査漏れの可
能性がある（住所不定者等）。
lines.english: Survey limited to notable dan-ranked practitioners within the city. Persons dead for more than one year excluded. Persons whose registered domicile lies outside the city may have been overlooked (e.g., persons of no fixed address).

lines.japanese:
一般有段者については資格の有無ばかりではなく、
実質的に術理を体得している者について、調べられ
る範囲で全て列挙したものである。
lines.english: For ordinary dan-ranked practitioners, inclusion was not limited to formal credentials. The following also lists, as comprehensively as the available information permits, anyone who has effectively mastered the principles of an art.

　阿刀田浩一郎（３５）無所属……市内ボランティア
活動に参加中

　門倉秋作（７９）門倉流居合斬道……死亡
　門倉誠也（５３）門倉流居合斬道……消息不明
　門倉一（８２）門倉流居合斬道……病没
　門倉彦座（２１）門倉流組討

消息不明

……消息不明
　塚本斎（　　）門倉流組討
　辻野正三（７８）＊＊剣友会名誉会長……死亡

lines.japanese:
この一年、新規で取引された大型刀剣類は存在し
ない。
　現在、登録された刀剣についての調査は、専門知
識を有する担当者の不在のため、困難な状況にある。
lines.english: No full-sized swords have changed hands within the past year. At present, registered swords are difficult to investigate because no personnel with the necessary specialist knowledge are available.

lines.japanese: （ほとんどが死亡……あるいは行方不明、か）
lines.english: (Most of them are dead… or missing.)

lines.japanese: 拳を握りこむ。
lines.english: He clenched his fist.

lines.japanese:
