lines.japanese: 「お砂糖抜きのミルクなしでございます」
lines.english: “Your coffee: no sugar, no milk.”

lines.japanese: 「……まさにそれこそ僕の望むものだよ、メイ」
lines.english: “…Precisely what I wanted, May.”

lines.japanese: 「旦那様」
lines.english: “Master.”

lines.japanese: イメージプレイはすでにはじまっている。
lines.english: The role-play was well underway.

lines.japanese: 「うん、美味い」
lines.english: “Mm. That's good.”

lines.japanese: 「恐悦至極」
lines.english: “I am deeply honored.”

lines.japanese: 「実にほどよい。温度はどれくらいかね？」
lines.english: “Just right. And the temperature?”

lines.japanese: 「少し低めの９０度となっております」
lines.english: “A slightly low ninety degrees Celsius.”

lines.japanese: 「素晴らしい」
lines.english: “Splendid.”

lines.japanese: 優雅にがぶ飲み。味もわかるまいに。
lines.english: He guzzled it with consummate elegance. Not that he could tell how it tasted.

lines.japanese: 「かたやメイ度の方は９８％となっております」
lines.english: “Meanwhile, my May-d content stands at ninety-eight percent.”

lines.japanese:
「それはそれは、むせかえるほどにメイドではない
　か」
lines.english: “My, my. That's enough maid to choke on.”

lines.japanese:
くだらない洒落に、向けられる沙也加の視線は吹雪
そのものだ。
lines.english: The look Sayaka leveled at the awful pun was a blizzard all its own.

lines.japanese:
難儀なもので、当の二人は気づきもしない。
　できないのである。
lines.english: The trouble was that the two of them did not even notice. By then, they could not.

lines.japanese:
幻想遊戯というイマジナリー・スペースに属する
二人には、到底感じられない世間の（身内だが）荒
波であった。
lines.english: The two of them occupied the imaginary space of make-believe. They could never feel the rough seas of the outside world —even when those seas came from their own circle.

lines.japanese: 「う、なんか悔しくなってきた……」
lines.english: “Ugh. Now I’m getting frustrated…”

lines.japanese: 「放っておきなさい」
lines.english: “Leave them alone.”

lines.japanese: 「あたしのは怒って、アレは怒らないのー？」
lines.english: “You got mad at me. Why aren't you getting mad at that?”

lines.japanese:
「……関わりたくないという気持ちでいっぱいなの
　よ……」
lines.english: “…Because every part of me is screaming not to get involved…”

lines.japanese: 「うー」
lines.english: “Hmph.”

lines.japanese: 納得のいかない顔で、あずさは葉子を見やった。
lines.english: Unconvinced, Azusa looked over at Youko.

lines.japanese: 「あたしもお金ためてコスプレしよう……」
lines.english: “I'm gonna save up and cosplay too…”

lines.japanese: 「メイドとは元来“銘奴”と呼ばれ、」
lines.english: “Maids were originally known as ‘marked slaves,’ and—”

lines.japanese:
「政略的に嫁ぐことを望まない貴族の娘などが特別の
　教育を受け由緒ある愛の奴隷となり、自らの意志に
　おいて仕えるべき主……愛紳士を捜し、」
lines.english: “daughters of noble houses unwilling to enter political marriages would receive special training, become pedigreed slaves of love, and set forth of their own free will in search of a master worthy of their service—a gentleman of love—”

lines.japanese:
「そのもとに奉公に出るというまるでできすぎた
　コミックのような聖なる行為からおこった職業
　なのでありまして、」
lines.english: “and enter his household. The profession thus arose from a sacred rite so preposterously perfect it might have come straight out of the pages of a comic book—”

lines.japanese:
「本場アルビオン（英国の雅称）におきましてはま
　さに淑女の中の淑女とされ、」
lines.english: “and in its homeland, Albion—the poetic name for Britain—they are considered ladies among ladies—”

lines.japanese:
「昼はわきまえた女中として家中を切り盛りし夜は
　疲れた紳士を癒す尽きることのない愛の密壺とな
　ることが求められるという……」
lines.english: “by day, they are expected to know their place as serving girls and run the household; by night, they become inexhaustible honeypots of love and soothe their weary gentlemen…”

lines.japanese: 「それはそれは崇高なものなのですよ？」
lines.english: “It is a most exalted calling, you know?”

lines.japanese: 今日もノリノリだった。
lines.english: She was in fine form again today.

lines.japanese:
もやもやとした渦巻き模様が、全てだった。
　前後左右、上下に至るまで、全てが歪んでいた。
lines.english: All he could see was a hazy pattern of whorls. Everything was distorted—front and back, left and right, above and below.

lines.japanese:
模様は幽玄とした迷路のようでもあり、刻一刻と
その形を変えた。
lines.english: The pattern was like an unfathomable maze, its shape changing from moment to moment.

lines.japanese:
忍は迷っていた。
　有り様に混迷していた。
lines.english: Shinobu was lost. Lost in confusion over the shape of his own existence.

lines.japanese:
自己を見失いやすいのは、年頃のせいばかりでは
ないだろう。
lines.english: It was probably not only his age that made it so easy to lose sight of himself.

lines.japanese: （貴宮忍って……なんだろう）
lines.english: (What… is Shinobu Atemiya?)

lines.japanese: だが自分を捜しても、たやすく見つかりはしない。
lines.english: But no matter how he searched, finding himself would not be easy.

lines.japanese: （どうでもいいか……そんなものは……）
lines.english: (Who cares…? About any of that…)

lines.japanese:
だから迷い続ける。
　足掻くこともない。
lines.english: And so he went on wandering, making no effort to struggle free.

lines.japanese: 自分が何者かなど、どうでもいいことであった。
lines.english: Who he was did not matter.

lines.japanese: いつも後悔のないように生きたいと思っていた。
lines.english: He had always wanted to live without regret.

lines.japanese:
心残りなく時を重ねる自信はなかった。
　七人の輪は、最高に輝かしいものであった。
lines.english: He had no faith that he could go on living without leaving regrets behind. The circle of seven was the brightest thing he had ever known.

lines.japanese:
ささやかな希望を食い尽くそうとする虚無との、
唯一無二の戦う術だった。
lines.english: It was his only weapon against the void that threatened to devour even his meager hopes.

lines.japanese: だが―――砕けてしまう。
lines.english: But—it would shatter.

lines.japanese:
照り映えるのではなく、内面から燃焼することに
よって輝く自立した環は……永遠のものではない。
lines.english: That self-sustaining ring did not shine by reflected light; it burned from within. Yet it was not eternal.

lines.japanese:
子供の自分から積み上げた記憶の群れを、忍は貴
石のように抱え込む。
lines.english: Shinobu clutched the memories he had built up since childhood to his chest like jewels.

lines.japanese: とりこぼさないよう―――
lines.english: So as not to let a single one slip away—

lines.japanese:
（自分について考えると……みんな思い出ばかりが
　浮かんでくる）
lines.english: (Whenever I think about myself… nothing but memories comes to mind.)

lines.japanese: （これだけが、僕の全てだ）
lines.english: (They're all I am.)

lines.japanese: （だけど充分なんだ、文句なんてない）
lines.english: (And that's enough. I have no complaints.)

lines.japanese:
（だから……
　その唯一のものを、奪わないでくれ……）
lines.english: (So… please don't take away the only thing I have…)

lines.japanese: 麻痺していた五感が、かすかに異物をとらえた。
lines.english: His numbed senses caught the faint trace of something foreign.

lines.japanese:
渦紋を重ねたような心象世界は、いわば全てがノ
イズであり、異物となれば即ち清音である。
lines.english: The inner world of overlapping whorls was nothing but noise; anything foreign to it could only ring out as a clear tone.

lines.japanese: （これは……鼻歌？）
lines.english: (Is that… humming?)

lines.japanese:
和音にさえなっていない単調なはずの旋律が、豊
かな色彩をまとった優しい刃となって、忍の空虚を
切り裂いた。
lines.english: The melody should have been monotonous, not even a chord. Yet it came clothed in rich color, a gentle blade slicing open Shinobu’s emptiness.

lines.japanese: そして忍は、いつもの工場に立ち返るのだった。
lines.english: And then Shinobu found himself back in the familiar factory.

lines.japanese: 夜の工場。
lines.english: The factory at night.

lines.japanese:
眼前で、ドラム缶の炎が小さく爆ぜる。
　肌寒いほどの夜気が背中に感じられた。
lines.english: Before him, the fire in a steel drum crackled softly. He felt the chill of the night air at his back.

lines.japanese:
寝ていたわけではないようだが、四肢に流れる血
流は鈍く、少し寒かった。
lines.english: He did not seem to have been asleep. Yet the blood seemed to move sluggishly through his limbs, and he felt a little cold.

lines.japanese: 「……またやったか……弱い心だ……」
lines.english: “…There I go again… I'm so weak…”

lines.japanese: 自ら、両の頬を叩く。
lines.english: He slapped himself across both cheeks.

lines.japanese: そして五センチほど前に出て、炎に近づこうとした。
lines.english: Then he moved about five centimeters forward, trying to get closer to the flames.

lines.japanese: が、足下に塗料で赤線が引かれている。
lines.english: But a red line had been painted across the floor at his feet.

lines.japanese:
『火扱ってるんだから、こっから前に行ったらダメ
　だからね』
lines.english: “We're handling fire, so don't go past this line, okay?”

lines.japanese:
火元責任者の言うことには逆らえない。
　刷り込まれていた。
lines.english: One did not disobey the fire-safety officer. That rule had been drilled into him.

lines.japanese:
諦めて、忍は手だけを伸ばしてかじかんだ指先を
焙るように温めた。
lines.english: Giving up, Shinobu reached out and held his numb fingertips over the heat.

lines.japanese:
鼻歌は遠くから漂ってくる。
　肉の焼けるいい香りとともに。
lines.english: The humming drifted in from somewhere far off, along with the delicious smell of meat cooking.
“…Who's there?”

lines.japanese: 姿が見えないので、呼びかけると、
lines.english: He could not see anyone. When he called out—

lines.japanese: 「あ、忍さん、瞑想終わりました？」
lines.english: “Oh, Shinobu. Finished meditating?”

lines.japanese:
調理スペースから、葉子が真横にひょいと顔を出
した。
lines.english: Youko poked her head out sideways from the cooking area.
“Meditating…”

lines.japanese: 「夕ご飯つくってますよー」
lines.english: “I'm making dinner.”

lines.japanese: 「食べる」
lines.english: “I'll eat.”

lines.japanese: 反射的にこたえた。
lines.english: He answered on reflex.

lines.japanese: 「葉子も？」
lines.english: “Are you staying too?”

lines.japanese: 「はい、今日は泊まろうかと」
lines.english: “Yes. I thought I might spend the night.”

lines.japanese:
最近は、それぞれの家庭事情もいろいろと複雑に
なってきており、工場の拡充が急務であった。
lines.english: Lately, everyone's home life had grown complicated in one way or another, so expanding the factory had become urgent.

lines.japanese:
忍や章二がソファで一夜を過ごすことからはじま
り、ベッドを拾ってきたり、近くの打ち捨てられた
事務所からパーティションを運んできたりと、
lines.english: It started with Shinobu and Shouji spending nights on the sofa. Then they scavenged beds and hauled partitions over from a nearby abandoned office.

lines.japanese: 複数が宿泊できる設備が整いつつある。
lines.english: Little by little, they were equipping the place to accommodate several people overnight.

lines.japanese:
各人の私物も、だいぶ増えているのが現状だった。
　なにしろ一人一人の個室に近い空間もあるのだから。
lines.english: Their personal belongings had multiplied too. Each of them now had something close to a room of their own.

lines.japanese:
ただ工場にいれば火を囲むことが多く、それらは
私物置き場以上の役目は果たさなかった。
　特に示し合わせることもなく、そうなった。
lines.english: But at the factory, they usually gathered around the fire, so their rooms served as little more than storage. No one had planned it that way. It had simply happened.

lines.japanese:
人それぞれであり、仲間とは関係なく自身のプラ
イベートを大切にする者もいる。
lines.english: Everyone was different. Some valued their private lives apart from the friendships they shared.

lines.japanese:
薄情、ということではなく、それが人間の個性と
いうものだからだ。
lines.english: That was not heartlessness. It was simply part of individuality.

lines.japanese:
が、七人については、奇妙な一致を見ていた。
　強要せず集いあい、集えば面を合わせて語る。
lines.english: The seven of them, though, had achieved a strange accord. They gathered without compulsion and, once together, faced one another and talked.

lines.japanese: ひとところ
lines.english: All in one place.

lines.japanese:
七人もの男女が一所にいて、誰も妥協せず今の形
に噛み合っていることは……ちょっとした奇跡を思
わせた。
lines.english: Seven young men and women, all in one place, fitting together exactly as they were without any of them compromising themselves… It felt like a minor miracle.

lines.japanese: 「……葉子、泊まるのか……」
lines.english: “…So you're staying tonight…”

lines.japanese: 忍の記憶では、あまりないことだった。
lines.english: As far as Shinobu remembered, she rarely did.

lines.japanese: （腐っても門倉、だもんな）
lines.english: (Once a Kadokura, always a Kadokura, I suppose.)

lines.japanese: （……自宅に戻っても、斎もいない、か……）
lines.english: (…Then again, Itsuki isn't there even if she does go home…)

lines.japanese:
忍は鼻をすすった。
　最近よく涙が出る。
lines.english: Shinobu sniffled. Tears had been coming easily lately.

lines.japanese: 「おまっとさんです」
lines.english: “Sorry to keep you waiting.”

lines.japanese: カートを押して、葉子がやってきた。
lines.english: Youko wheeled in the cart.

lines.japanese: 「……その台車……」
lines.english: “…That cart…”

lines.japanese: 「拾いました」
lines.english: “I found it.”

lines.japanese: 「ここまで……」
lines.english: “You brought it all the way here…?”

lines.japanese: 「乗ったり、押したりして運びました」
lines.english: “I brought it here by riding it and pushing it.”

lines.japanese: 「……乗ったのか……」
lines.english: “…You rode it…”

lines.japanese: 「レストランかホテルの備品なんでしょうね」
lines.english: “It must have belonged to a restaurant or hotel.”

lines.japanese: 「メイドにはカートというものです」
lines.english: “A maid has to have a cart.”

lines.japanese: 追及はやめて、料理を眺めた。
lines.english: He let the matter drop and looked over the food.

lines.japanese: 原始肉。
lines.english: Caveman meat.

lines.japanese: 焼きニンニク。
lines.english: Roasted garlic.

lines.japanese: 鰻重。
lines.english: Grilled eel over rice.

lines.japanese: レバーの串焼き（ネギ挟み）。
lines.english: Skewered liver with scallions.

lines.japanese: 以上である。
lines.english: That was the entire menu.

lines.japanese:
「家の方に、親類から食べきれないほどの食料が送
　られてきたのです」
lines.english: “Some relatives sent my family more food than we could possibly eat.”

lines.japanese: 「おいしそう、だけど……」
lines.english: “It looks delicious, but…”

lines.japanese: 「そうそう、これもありました」
lines.english: “Oh, yes. There was this as well.”

lines.japanese: コト、とポケットから出したビンを置いた。
lines.english: With a little clink, she pulled a bottle from her pocket and set it down.

lines.japanese: ビール酵母（亜鉛配合）の錠剤。
lines.english: Brewer's yeast tablets, fortified with zinc.

lines.japanese: 何かおかしい。
lines.english: Something was not right here.

lines.japanese: 気付かない。
lines.english: He did not notice.

lines.japanese: 「さあ召し上がれ旦那様」
lines.english: “Please help yourself, Master.”

lines.japanese: 棒読みである。
lines.english: Her delivery was flat.

lines.japanese:
何か怪しくはないか？
　忍はそんなに鋭くない。むしろ鈍い。
lines.english: Wasn't there something suspicious about all this? Shinobu was not especially observant. If anything, he was dense.

lines.japanese: やはり、原始肉、これだろう。
lines.english: Yes, it had to be the caveman meat.

lines.japanese:
インパクトが強すぎて、策謀の香りをかき消して
しまうのだ。
lines.english: Its impact was so overwhelming that it drowned out every whiff of conspiracy.

lines.japanese: 「……これを食べるのははじめてだ……」
lines.english: “…I've never eaten this before…”

lines.japanese: 「ぐーるぐーる」
lines.english: “Round and round!”

lines.japanese:
葉子はゼスチャーで焼いてみせた。
　忍の喉が鳴った。
lines.english: Youko pantomimed turning it on a spit. Shinobu swallowed audibly.

lines.japanese: いったい何の肉なのだろう。
lines.english: What animal could the meat possibly have come from?

lines.japanese:
無意味な詮索だった。
　圧倒的存在感の前には、あまりにも些細なことで
ある。
lines.english: Pointless speculation. Before that overwhelming presence, the question was far too trivial to matter.

lines.japanese:
聞けば、浪漫も失せる。
　この２１世紀にマンモスが生存していないことを、
わざわざ確認するまでもない。
lines.english: Asking would ruin the romance. There was no point confirming that mammoths had not survived into the twenty-first century.

lines.japanese: 夢を食う。獏のように。
lines.english: He would devour the dream. Like a dream-eating tapir.

lines.japanese: 忍は宣言した。
lines.english: Shinobu made his declaration.

lines.japanese: 「僕はこの肉を食べたいと思う」
lines.english: “I believe I shall eat this meat.”

lines.japanese: 「どうぞ」
lines.english: “Be my guest.”

lines.japanese: 恭しく、葉子は低頭した。
lines.english: With due reverence, Youko bowed her head.

lines.japanese: 突きだした骨を、両手で掴む。
lines.english: He grasped the protruding bone in both hands.

lines.japanese:
おお、まるでダンベルのように頼もしい重みでは
ないか。
lines.english: Oh, what a reassuring heft it had— like a dumbbell.

lines.japanese:
「ノーチョップスティック、ノーフォーク、
　ノーソイソースでお召し上がりください」
lines.english: “Please enjoy it with no chopsticks, no fork—Norfolk— and no soy sauce.”

lines.japanese: 箸も肉さしも醤油も、この肉世界には必要ない。
lines.english: Chopsticks, meat forks, and soy sauce had no place in this world of meat.

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう、葉子」
lines.english: “Thank you, Youko.”

lines.japanese: そして忍は、
lines.english: And then Shinobu—

lines.japanese: 堪能した―――
lines.english: Feasted to his heart's content—

lines.japanese:
腹膨れればなんとやら。目蓋が重い。
　忍はソファでうとうとしはじめた。
lines.english: A full belly, and you know what comes next. His eyelids grew heavy. Shinobu began to doze on the sofa.

lines.japanese: 「泊まってくね……」
lines.english: “I'll stay over…”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “All right.”

lines.japanese: 「このまま寝ちゃおうかな」
lines.english: “Maybe I'll just fall asleep right here.”

lines.japanese: 「お風呂しませんか？」
lines.english: “How about a bath?”

lines.japanese: 「……ここのお風呂はー……」
lines.english: “…The bath here is…”

lines.japanese: 渋る。
lines.english: He hesitated.

lines.japanese: 「体くらい拭きますよ」
lines.english: “Then at least let me give you a wipe-down.”

lines.japanese: 衣服を脱がそうとする。
lines.english: She started undressing him.

lines.japanese: 「ちょ、やめ……」
lines.english: “Hey—stop…”

lines.japanese:
身もだえたが、葉子はやめない。
　臆することなく衣服をはいでいく。
lines.english: He squirmed, but Youko did not stop. Undaunted, she kept peeling away his clothes.

lines.japanese: 「よいしょ、よいしょ」
lines.english: “Heave-ho, heave-ho.”
“…Ah… don't…”

lines.japanese: 胸板を露出し、巧みに指先でくすぐった。
lines.english: She bared Shinobu's chest and deftly tickled it with her fingertips.

lines.japanese: 「ん……んちゅ……」
lines.english: “Nn… nch…”

lines.japanese: 唇で挟んだ。
lines.english: She caught it between her lips.

lines.japanese: 「ううっ、な、なに、を……？」
lines.english: “Wh-what are you…?”

lines.japanese:
「葉子の舌で、ご奉仕いたします。
　れろろろろろろろ」
lines.english: “Youko’s tongue is at your service. Lllrlrlrlrlrlr.”

lines.japanese: 身をよじって呻いた。
lines.english: Shinobu twisted and groaned.

lines.japanese: 「ぎゃーーーーーーー」
lines.english: “Gyaaaaaah!”

lines.japanese: イキそうになった。
lines.english: Shinobu nearly came.

lines.japanese: 寸前で、葉子をクローで引きはがすことができた。
lines.english: At the last instant, he managed to pry Youko off with a claw hold.

lines.japanese: 「いたたた……」
lines.english: “Ow, ow, ow…”

lines.japanese: 「あのね」
lines.english: “Look.”

lines.japanese: 「はい、ごめんなさい」
lines.english: “All right. I'm sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「やれやれ」
lines.english: “Good grief.”

lines.japanese: 眠気が覚めてしまった。
lines.english: He was wide awake now.

lines.japanese:
ソファに二人して座る。
　間に微妙な距離ができていた。
lines.english: The two of them sat on the sofa. An awkward little gap had opened between them.

lines.japanese: 「……ちょっと、そういうの、危ないので……」
lines.english: “…That sort of thing is… kind of dangerous.”

lines.japanese: 「危ない？」
lines.english: “Dangerous?”

lines.japanese:
「僕も男だから……その、明日を夢見るますらお候
　補生だから……」
lines.english: “I'm a man too… an aspiring man among men with dreams of tomorrow…”

lines.japanese: 「国つくり、そして罪つくりですね」
lines.english: “Building nations and breaking hearts, I see.”

lines.japanese:
「うん……じゃなくて、
　ヘンなところ触られると……困る」
lines.english: “Yes… I mean, no. That's not the point. If you touch me in weird places… we have a problem.”

lines.japanese: 「……今日はそんな溜まってないんですか？」
lines.english: “…You're not that pent-up today?”

lines.japanese: 忍は吹いた。
lines.english: Shinobu sputtered.

lines.japanese: 「今日はって……」
lines.english: “What do you mean, today…?”

lines.japanese: 「人間は一年中発情してるものですよ」
lines.english: “Humans are in heat all year round, you know.”

lines.japanese: 「いや……そうじゃなくて」
lines.english: “No… that's not what I meant.”

lines.japanese: 「溜まっていたとしても……その……」
lines.english: “Even if I were pent-up… I mean…”

lines.japanese: 「私はいいんですよ？」
lines.english: “I don't mind, you know?”

lines.japanese:
タイミングを一切取らない斬り込みだった。
　あっけにとられて、葉子の顔をまじまじと見つめた。
lines.english: It was an attack delivered without the slightest concern for timing. Dumbfounded, Shinobu stared into Youko's face.

lines.japanese:
いつもの彼女だった。
　羞恥も躊躇もない。
lines.english: She was her usual self. No embarrassment. No hesitation.

lines.japanese: （この子……武術の読み合い合戦、下手だろうな）
lines.english: (She must be terrible at that whole reading-your-opponent game.)

lines.japanese: いつだって自分のタイミングで仕掛ける。
lines.english: She always struck whenever she felt like it.

lines.japanese:
相手を戸惑わせるが、しかし機をはかることがな
いのであれば、理は通るまい。
lines.english: She might catch an opponent off guard, but without any sense of timing, there was no logic to it.

lines.japanese: 「何してらっしゃるんです？」
lines.english: “And what have you been up to?”
“What…?”

lines.japanese: 「昼間、いろいろと歩き回っていたようですけど」
lines.english: “You seemed to be walking all over town today.”

lines.japanese: 愕然とした。
lines.english: He was stunned.

lines.japanese:
（……ヘンなところに鋭いんだよなぁ……
　この人……）
lines.english: (…She's perceptive about the strangest things…) (This girl…)

lines.japanese: 「気になることでも？」
lines.english: “Something on your mind?”

lines.japanese: 「聞きますよ？　聞きますとも」
lines.english: “I'll listen. Of course I'll listen.”

lines.japanese: 心配が、嬉しかった。
lines.english: It made him happy to know she worried about him.

lines.japanese:
彼女は一人で抱えていた荷物を、半分引き受けて
くれると言った。
lines.english: She had offered to shoulder half the burden he had been carrying alone.

lines.japanese: どれだけ心の重荷を、取り払ってくれたことか。
lines.english: How much weight had she lifted from his heart?

lines.japanese: だが。
lines.english: But.

lines.japanese: （明かすことはできない……斎のことは、まだ……）
lines.english: (I can't tell her… Not about Itsuki. Not yet…)

lines.japanese:
（もし知れば……葉子ははやるかも知れない……
　身内の恥と……）
lines.english: (If she knew… Youko might rush into action… might see it as a stain on the family…)

lines.japanese: （それだけは、させられない）
lines.english: (I can't allow that.)

lines.japanese:
（もし……最悪の結果であった場合……
　それを下すのは門倉でも葉子でもなくて、）
lines.english: (If… it comes to the worst… then judgment must come not from Kadokura, and not from Youko, but—)

lines.japanese:
目を閉じた。
　そして決意がかたまっていく音を聞いた。
lines.english: He closed his eyes and heard his resolve harden into place.

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう、葉子―――」
lines.english: “Thank you, Youko—”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 葉子の手を捧げ持つ。
lines.english: He held Youko’s hand reverently.

lines.japanese:
「葉子、いつも優しくしてくれるから……
　楽になってる」
lines.english: “You've always been so kind to me… It takes some of the weight off.”

lines.japanese: 「忍さん……」
lines.english: “Shinobu…”

lines.japanese: 眉根を寄せて、忍の目を見つめた。
lines.english: Her brows knitted as she searched his eyes.

lines.japanese: 「また、助けてくれようとしている」
lines.english: “You're trying to save me again.”

lines.japanese: 「……違うよ」
「一人で抱えてる」
lines.english: “You're keeping it all to yourself.”

lines.japanese: 先ほど自分で叩いた頬を、葉子は両手で包み持った。
lines.english: Youko cradled in both hands the cheeks he had slapped earlier.

lines.japanese: 「どうしよう……どうしたらいいのかわからない」
lines.english: “What should I do…? I don't know what to do.”

lines.japanese: 「もうしてくれたよ、葉子は」
lines.english: “You already have.”

lines.japanese: 「…………そんなのは」
lines.english: “…But that's…”

lines.japanese: きっ、と表情を引き締める。
lines.english: Her expression sharpened.

lines.japanese:
「忍さん、私たちの関係がいつか壊れると
　思ってます」
lines.english: “You think our relationship is going to fall apart someday, don't you?”

lines.japanese: びく、と忍は震えた。
lines.english: Shinobu flinched.

lines.japanese:
「ずっと前からそう。
　最初から……そんな心配、不安をいだいてた」
lines.english: “You always have. From the very beginning… you've carried that fear. That dread.”
“Youko, you…”

lines.japanese:
「だから私たちと話すひとつひとつを、大切に味わ
　ってた」
lines.english: “That's why you treasured every moment you spent talking with us.”

lines.japanese:
「私は最初、あなたがどうしてそんなことをして
　いるのか理解できなかった。
　見えもしなかった」
lines.english: “At first, I couldn't understand why you were doing that. I couldn't even see it.”

lines.japanese:
「ある時、不意にそれが浮き彫りになって……
　私は、意味を知りたくなりました」
lines.english: “Then one day, it suddenly came into focus… and I wanted to know what it meant.”

lines.japanese:
「……私はバカだから、うまい説明をつけることが
　できなかった……そのことを忍さんに問いかける
　言葉も見つからなかった……」
lines.english: “…I'm not smart, so I couldn't find a good explanation… I couldn't even find the words to ask you about it…”

lines.japanese:
「みんなと話して笑っているのに、あなたは心で
　泣いていた」
lines.english: “You'd laugh and talk with everyone, but inside you were crying.”

lines.japanese:
「イヤなのではない。だけど泣いてる。
　嬉しいのに、泣いてる。
　それが……私の知ってる忍さんです」
lines.english: “It wasn't that you hated it. But you cried. You were happy, and still you cried. That's… the Shinobu I know.”

lines.japanese: 「……わかるのか……人の、心が？」
lines.english: “…You can understand… a person's heart?”

lines.japanese: 「わかりませんよ」
lines.english: “No. I don't.”

lines.japanese: 力無く微笑む。
lines.english: She smiled wanly.

lines.japanese:
「ただ私は、心の喫水線が人より低くて……
　だから、流れ込んでくる誰かの心を、自分のもの
　のように感じられて……」
lines.english: “It's just that my heart rides lower in the water than most… so when someone else's heart comes pouring in, I can feel it as though it were my own…”

lines.japanese:
「そして相手は気付かないんです……
　見られていることに」
lines.english: “And the other person doesn't realize… that they're being seen.”

lines.japanese:
「私の自我が低い位置にあるものだから。そして
　輪郭の曖昧なものだから……どこからかが自分で
　も、どこからが私か、誰も判別できないから」
lines.english: “Because my sense of self sits so low. Because its boundaries are so vague… No one, not even me, can tell where they end and I begin.”

lines.japanese:
「そうやって心に触れて、同じものを見ても……同
　じ感想を抱くわけじゃない……同じ心でも、私に
　はまったく理解できないものもあるから……」
lines.english: “Even when I touch a heart that way and see what it sees… that doesn't mean I feel the same… There are things in that same heart I cannot understand at all…”

lines.japanese: 「でも理解する必要はなかったんです」
lines.english: “But I did not need to understand.”

lines.japanese:
「それが私みたいな女の、門倉での役目だったんで
　すから」
lines.english: “That was what a woman like me was for in the Kadokura family.”

lines.japanese:
葉子は今や双眼を大きく見開いて、氾濫する感情
の奔流を、忍に流し込んでいた。
lines.english: By then, Youko's eyes were wide, pouring a torrent of emotion into Shinobu.

lines.japanese:
「一族にはこんな人間がたまに生まれて、相手の心
　を察知する能力が高くて……その精度は、自我が
　乏しければ乏しいほど高くて―――」
lines.english: “Every so often, someone like me is born into the family—someone with an unusually keen gift for sensing what lies in another person's heart… The less of a self we possess, the more precise that ability becomes—”

lines.japanese:
「だから私は余計な知識を得ないよう、情緒が宿ら
　ないよう、人形として育てられて―――」
lines.english: “So they raised me as a doll, never letting me acquire unnecessary knowledge or develop emotions—”

lines.japanese: 「袋だって、言われて！」
lines.english: “They called me a bag!”
“A bag?”

lines.japanese:
「私は同席する。
　門倉が掌握したい誰かと同席する」
lines.english: “I would be present. I would sit with someone Kadokura wanted to bring under its control.”

lines.japanese:
「そして足下に流れる私の心は、ほとんど抵抗なく
　相手との共有を果たして、同じものを……
　相手の心の内を目にして……そして」
lines.english: “And my heart would flow beneath their feet, merging with theirs almost without resistance. I would see what they saw… look inside their heart… and then—”

lines.japanese: 「複写されて―――」
lines.english: “It would be copied into me—”

lines.japanese:
「私は問いかけられる。
　おまえは何を考えているのか、って」
lines.english: “Then they would question me. They would ask what I was thinking.”

lines.japanese:
「そして私は答える。機械のように、本心を……
　その誰かさんが隠したかったかも知れないことも、
　そうでないことも、訊かれるままに」
lines.english: “And I would answer like a machine, speaking their true thoughts… even things that person might have wanted to hide, as well as things they hadn’t. I answered whatever they asked.”

lines.japanese: 「……記憶の袋」
lines.english: “…A bag for memories.”

lines.japanese:
「その問答に必要な最低限の理解力と言葉。
　それが私に与えられる、最大のものだった」
lines.english: “The bare minimum of understanding and language needed for those exchanges. That was the most they ever gave me.”

lines.japanese:
「門倉が崩壊しなかったら……私は……心尽きるま
　で、盗み読む人形として、人の尊厳を踏みにじり
　続けることになったんです」
lines.english: “If Kadokura hadn't collapsed… I would have gone on until there was nothing left of my heart, a doll stealing secrets from people's minds and trampling their dignity again and again.”

lines.japanese:
「権力を維持するための、人のかたちをした何かと
　して」
lines.english: “Something in the shape of a person, made to maintain power.”
“…Youko… you…”

lines.japanese:
「あの頃、私には心なんてなかった。
　ないと思ってた」
lines.english: “Back then, I had no heart. Or I thought I didn't.”

lines.japanese: 「あなたが、掬い上げて見せてくれるまでは」
lines.english: “Until you scooped it up and showed it to me.”

lines.japanese: 震える両手が椀を作る。
lines.english: Her trembling hands curved into a bowl.

lines.japanese: 「……これっぽっちしか、ありませんでしたけど」
lines.english: “…There was only this tiny bit.”

lines.japanese:
「でも、確かにそれは私で……それは……
　はじめての……自分、でしたよ？」
lines.english: “But it really was me… it was… the very first… self I'd ever had, you know?”

lines.japanese:
「忍さんの中にも、同じくらいのものしかありませ
　んでしたね」
lines.english: “There was only about that much inside you, too.”

lines.japanese: 「あなたと私は、似たようなものだったんです」
lines.english: “You and I were much alike.”

lines.japanese:
「なのに私たちに近づいて、何か大きな痛みを受け
　て、そして……変質した」
lines.english: “And yet you came close to us, suffered some terrible pain, and then… you changed.”

lines.japanese:
「決意変わりは色のうつろい。冷たい灰色の塊は、
　いつしか山吹色に映えて……綺麗だった―――」
lines.english: “As your resolve changed, so did your color. That cold gray mass came, in time, to glow a brilliant gold… It was beautiful—”

lines.japanese:
「あなたは急速に心を豊かにしていった……驚くほ
　どのはやさで……」
lines.english: “Your heart grew so much richer… with astonishing speed…”

lines.japanese:
涙を隠しもしない葉子の唇は、喘ぐような性急さ
で忍の口を吸った。
lines.english: Making no attempt to hide her tears, Youko kissed Shinobu with breathless urgency.

lines.japanese: 少し不器用な口づけだった。
lines.english: The kiss was a little clumsy.

lines.japanese: 「それを見ながら、私も育ちました」
lines.english: “Watching you, I grew too.”

lines.japanese:
「どんな人間にも、育ちを導く太陽が必要です……
　そして誰もがそれを見失ってる」
lines.english: “Every human being needs a sun to guide their growth… and everyone has lost sight of it.”

lines.japanese: 「だけど今は……黄昏？　今は黄昏？」
lines.english: “But now… is it twilight? Is it twilight now?”

lines.japanese:
「ほら、似たような考えをしてます……
　これから来る夜が……コワイ、から……？」
lines.english: “See? We're thinking the same thing… because we're… afraid of the night ahead…?”

lines.japanese: 「忍さんも、光り輝くものを求めている……」
lines.english: “You're searching for something radiant too…”

lines.japanese: 「でも私たちにとっては、あなたがそれでした」
lines.english: “But to us, you were that sun.”

lines.japanese: 「あなたは私の、光射す庭―――」
lines.english: “You are my garden bathed in light—”

lines.japanese: 「……一命を賭けて、仕えたいと思えます」
lines.english: “…I could stake my life on serving you.”

lines.japanese: 「葉子たちが……僕に仕える必要なんてない……」
lines.english: “None of you… need to serve me…”

lines.japanese: 「これは僕自身の欲望でもあるんだから」
lines.english: “Because this is my own desire, too.”

lines.japanese: 葉子は薄く笑った。
lines.english: Youko gave a faint smile.

lines.japanese: 「本当のお日様だって、きっとそうなんです」
lines.english: “I'm sure the real sun is just the same.”

lines.japanese:
「自分のために光って、そしてついでに何かを温め
　ている」
lines.english: “It shines for itself and, in passing, warms whatever happens to be nearby.”

lines.japanese:
「忍さんの意志は関係ない。私たちが、勝手に好き
　なだけ」
lines.english: “Your will has nothing to do with it. We love you entirely of our own accord.”

lines.japanese: 「兄のことで、悩まないで」
lines.english: “Don't worry about my brother.”

lines.japanese: ああ、と忍は嘆息した。
lines.english: Shinobu breathed out a soft ah.

lines.japanese: （知っていた……んだ……やっぱり……）
lines.english: (She knew… She did know, after all…)

lines.japanese: 「好き。ただ、好き」
lines.english: “I love you. I just love you.”

lines.japanese:
ついばむほどに小刻みに、吸い付いてくる。
　もう忍は抵抗していなかった。
lines.english: Her lips found his again and again in tiny, pecking kisses. Shinobu no longer resisted.

lines.japanese:
確かに、心底で目前の少女と繋がっているかすか
な感覚があった。
lines.english: Deep down, he could indeed feel a faint connection to the girl before him.

lines.japanese:
胸を押さえると、胸板ごしにつかみ取れそうな熱
があり、じんわりとてのひらを熱くした。
lines.english: When he pressed a hand to his chest, the heat beneath it felt almost solid— as if he could grasp it through the wall of his chest. Slowly, it warmed his palm.

lines.japanese: 同時に、圧迫された体内を炉のように加熱する。
lines.english: At the same time, it heated his constricted insides like a furnace.

lines.japanese:
他人ではない。
　一部であった。
lines.english: She was not another person. She was part of him.

lines.japanese: 忍はいっとき冷静になり、告げた。
lines.english: Shinobu recovered his composure for a moment and spoke.

lines.japanese: 「投射」
lines.english: “Projection.”

hyperlinks.preview: The passage of light, sound, or the like through matter to the surface of another substance. The cas

japaneseHyperlinks.preview: The passage of light, sound, or the like through matter to the surface of another substance. The cas

lines.english: “…What?”

lines.japanese: 「投射能力」
lines.english: “Your capacity for projection.”

lines.japanese: 「とうしゃ……？」
lines.english: “Projection…?”

lines.japanese: 「無意識の作用による自我の防衛機制の一つだよ」
lines.english: “It's one of the ego's unconscious defense mechanisms.”

lines.japanese:
「精神医学の言葉で……自分の内面に対する拒絶が
　あるとき、それを他人のものであると転嫁してし
　まう心の作用さ」
lines.english: “It's a psychiatric term… When you reject something within yourself, your mind attributes it to someone else as though it belonged to them.”

lines.japanese:
「自分が相手を好きなのに、それを求められない時
　……相手が自分を好きだと思いこんでしまう。
　そういうことがあるんだ」
lines.english: “Say you love someone, but can't allow yourself to want them… You might convince yourself that they're the one who loves you.”

lines.japanese:
「葉子のはそれと同質でありながら、相手の機微を
　取り込む……まったく今までにないタイプの投射
　なのだと思う」
lines.english: “I think yours is the same sort of thing, but it also takes in the subtleties of the other person… an entirely new kind of projection.”

lines.japanese:
「自我が確立されない状態が長く続けることで、他
　者性と自己性を曖昧にしつつ……」
lines.english: “If the ego remains unformed for long enough, blurring the boundary between self and other…”

lines.japanese:
「無垢な感受性を残せば、似たような状態を意図的
　に作ることができるかも知れない……」
lines.english: “and preserving an innocent sensitivity, perhaps a similar state could be produced deliberately…”

lines.japanese: 「それはきっと、門倉の秘伝なんだ」
lines.english: “That must be one of Kadokura's secret methods.”

lines.japanese:
「そして今という時代には、成立しやすい新しい形
　の投射」
lines.english: “A new form of projection more likely to arise in the modern age.”

lines.japanese: 「僕も病気なんだ。君とは違うけど」
lines.english: “I'm sick too, though not in the same way.”

lines.japanese: 「ここが、壊れてるんだ」
lines.english: “This part of me is broken.”

lines.japanese: 頭を指さす。
lines.english: He pointed to his head.

lines.japanese: 「因果関係の計算と予測が、早いんだ」
lines.english: “I can calculate and predict cause and effect very quickly.”

lines.japanese: 「演算、能力……？」
lines.english: “A computational… ability?”

lines.japanese: 「適切な言葉だ」
lines.english: “That's an apt term.”

lines.japanese:
「だから、人よりいろいろなことを予測したり、
　計算したりできる」
lines.english: “That's why I can predict and calculate more than most people can.”

lines.japanese:
「……残念ながらそれで、賢い人間になれるという
　わけでもなかったけど」
lines.english: “…Unfortunately, that didn’t make me wise.”

lines.japanese: 自嘲した。
lines.english: He laughed at himself.

lines.japanese:
「ほんの少しのことだから。
　対して、ありとあらゆる因子群は、外側に向かっ
　て無限に広がっていて……」
lines.english: “My gift amounts to very little. Beyond it, whole networks of factors spread outward without end…”

lines.japanese:
「とても先々を完全に見通すことはできなくて……
　うねる様子を無力に眺めるだけなんだ」
lines.english: “I can never see perfectly what lies ahead… All I can do is watch it heave and churn, powerless.”

lines.japanese: 「周囲は、薄暗い影だった」
lines.english: “Everything around me lay in dim shadow.”

lines.japanese:
「過去の輝きというともしびがあまりにも居心地が
　良くて……思い出に最上の価値があると思った」
lines.english: “The past shone like a lamp, and its light was so comforting… I came to believe that memories were the most precious thing of all.”

lines.japanese: 「だから、集めた」
lines.english: “So I gathered them.”

lines.japanese: 「利己的だと思うよ、実際」
lines.english: “It was selfish of me. I know.”

lines.japanese:
「寂しかった。長く暗い道のりを、僕らは歩いてい

lines.japanese:
が、こういった認識でなければならない。
　情報が物足りないのは当然だった。
　今自分が立っている場所こそが、最先端なのだ。
lines.english: But this was how he had to frame it. No wonder the available information seemed inadequate. Shinobu stood at the very frontier.

lines.japanese:
望んで立っている。
　千鳥とは、無茶をしないと約束した。
lines.english: He was standing there by choice. He had promised Chidori that he would not do anything reckless.

lines.japanese: 危険なことだから、命を粗末にしないと。
lines.english: The danger was why he had promised not to throw his life away.

lines.japanese:
厳密には、死ななければ良いのだが、彼女は納得
するかどうか。
lines.english: Strictly speaking, all he had to do was avoid dying—but whether she would accept that distinction was another matter.

lines.japanese: （……生き残って……叱られよう）
lines.english: (…I'll survive… and let her scold me.)

lines.japanese: （だってあの人は、僕の姉さんなんだから）
lines.english: (Because she's my sis.)

lines.japanese:
死ななければいい。
　そう、生きていれば―――
lines.english: Not dying was enough. Yes—as long as he lived—

lines.japanese:
未来は見ないようにしていた。
　明るいはずはなかったから。
lines.english: He had made a point of not looking toward the future. It could not possibly be bright.

lines.japanese:
だから機械に徹した。
　恐怖はなかった。機械だから。
lines.english: So he had made himself a machine. A machine felt no fear.

lines.japanese:
しかし友ができた。
　並んで歩き、いつも一緒にいる。そんな関係だ。
lines.english: But then he made friends. Friends who walked beside him, always at his side.

lines.japanese:
彼は臆病になった。
　恐怖が再燃した。
lines.english: He became a coward. His fear reignited.

lines.japanese: それは未来に置かれた、いつか来る崩壊という恐怖。
lines.english: It was fear of the collapse that waited somewhere ahead.

lines.japanese: 下地はあったのだ。
lines.english: The foundation had been there all along.

lines.japanese:
門倉のこと。
　その他、いろいろなこと。
lines.english: Kadokura. And so many other things.

lines.japanese:
（……苦しむために……
　斎や葉子と友達になったわけじゃないのに……）
lines.english: (…I didn't become friends with Itsuki and Youko just so I could suffer…)

lines.japanese:
恨めしいと感じたことはある。
　しかし誰を憎む筋でもない。
　考えれば、今の状況も最善というわけではない。
lines.english: There were times he felt bitter. But there was no one he had any right to hate. And when he thought about it, things as they stood were hardly ideal either.

lines.japanese:
これから来たる対決のことを考えれば、逃げてし
まいたいくらいだ。
lines.english: The thought of the confrontation ahead made him want to run away.

lines.japanese: （だけど……歩もう）
lines.english: (But… I'll walk on.)

lines.japanese: そう決めた。
lines.english: He decided.

lines.japanese: 絶望に向けて、出発！
lines.english: Forward, into despair!

lines.japanese:
それを発見したのは、昼もだいぶまわってからだ
った。
lines.english: It was well past noon when he found it.

lines.japanese: （これは……）
lines.english: (This…)

lines.japanese:
現場保持のこともあり迷ったが、結局しゃがんで
触れてみた。
lines.english: He hesitated, mindful of preserving the crime scene, but finally crouched and touched it.

lines.japanese: （……野菜……か。これは？）
lines.english: (…A vegetable…? Is that what this is?)

lines.japanese:
食い散らかされた、それは大根の一部らしい。
　へたが落ちていた。トマトのものだ。
lines.english: The gnawed remains appeared to be part of a daikon radish. A stem lay nearby. A tomato stem.

lines.japanese:
他、わからないが食いカスのようなものが散乱し
ている。
lines.english: Other unidentifiable scraps of food lay scattered about.

lines.japanese: （……獣が荒らしたような……）
lines.english: (…As if an animal had torn into them…)

lines.japanese: 少し歩いていくと、雑木林の隣は畑だった。
lines.english: A short distance on, the thicket gave way to a field.

lines.japanese:
盗んだ野菜を、ここで食い荒らしたのだろう。
　人としての尊厳を捨ててまで。
lines.english: He must have stolen the vegetables and devoured them here. Even at the cost of his dignity as a human being.

lines.japanese: だが家を出て、もはや寄る辺などないはずなのだ。
lines.english: But having left home, he could have no refuge left.

lines.japanese:
広漠としたこの現代社会では、一人の少年が野山
で生きることなどできはしない。
lines.english: In the vastness of modern society, a boy alone could never survive in the wild.

lines.japanese: 拳をかためた。
lines.english: Shinobu clenched his fist.

lines.japanese:
無念だった。
　あるいは憐憫だった。
lines.english: Bitter regret. Or perhaps pity.

lines.japanese:
情けにしても、これほど強い情念を凝縮させたこ
とはない。
lines.english: Even if this was pity, he had never felt it gather into such a fierce knot of emotion.

lines.japanese: 野菜泥棒。野菜泥棒！
lines.english: A vegetable thief. A vegetable thief!

lines.japanese: そんな境遇が彼に相応しいとは思えない。
lines.english: Such a fate did not suit him.

lines.japanese:
殺人者である。敵である。だが……社会的弱者で
はなかったはずだ。
lines.english: He was a murderer. An enemy. But… surely he had not been one of society’s vulnerable.

lines.japanese:
なりふり構わず糧を得ねばならないほどの、立場
ではなかった。
lines.english: He had not been in a position where he had to scrounge for food at any cost.

lines.japanese:
お世辞にも恵まれていたとは言えないが、それで
もである。
lines.english: No one could call him fortunate, but even so— not this.

lines.japanese:
（……君のために……
　やはり僕が終わらせてあげるべきなんだな）
lines.english: (…For your sake… I really am the one who should put an end to it.)

lines.japanese:
（そうなんだな？
　君が正気だったら……そう願ったんだろ？）
lines.english: (Isn't that right? If you were sane… that's what you'd want, right?)

lines.japanese:
（だったら僕は……過去の……
　今までの君を信じるしかない）
lines.english: (Then I have no choice but to believe in the person you were… in the person you've always been.)

lines.japanese: （誰よりも尊厳について想っていた、君を―――）
lines.english: (In you—the one who cared more deeply about dignity than anyone—)

lines.japanese: 手のなかで、握りしめられた野菜のかすが潰れた。
lines.english: The vegetable scraps were crushed in his clenched hand.

lines.japanese:
その後、畑に隣接した民家を訪ねてみると、幸い
なことに人が住んでいた。
lines.english: Afterward, he visited the house beside the field. Fortunately, someone lived there.

lines.japanese: ５０代の男だった。
lines.english: A man in his fifties.

lines.japanese:
畑泥棒について質問してみたところ、家人は把握
していた。
lines.english: When Shinobu asked about the crop thief, the homeowner knew about it.

lines.japanese:
気配はなかったが、朝起きてみると畑が荒らされ
ていたそうだ。
lines.english: He hadn't noticed anyone, but when he woke that morning, he found the field ransacked.

lines.japanese: が、時代も時代だと考え、放っておいたと言う。
lines.english: Given the times, he said, he had decided to leave it alone.

lines.japanese: まずは適切な判断である。
lines.english: A sensible decision under the circumstances.

lines.japanese:
「三日前のことかな。怖いから、最近は。
　それからずっと家にこもったままだ」
lines.english: “Must've been three days ago. It's dangerous these days. I've been holed up inside ever since.”

lines.japanese:
どこか元気のない声で、男は言った。
　久しぶりに人と話した、という様子だった。
lines.english: The man sounded dispirited, as though this were his first conversation in a long time.

lines.japanese: 「あんた、警察の人？」
lines.english: “Are you with the police?”

lines.japanese: 正直に答えるわけにはいかない。
lines.english: Shinobu could not answer honestly.

lines.japanese:
適当にごまかすしかなかった。
　しかし男は励まされたようだ。
lines.english: He had no choice but to give an evasive answer. Even so, the man seemed encouraged.

lines.japanese: 「良かったよ、あんたみたいな若者がいるって」
lines.english: “I'm glad there are still young people like you around.”

lines.japanese: 戸締まりの用心を告げて、立ち去った。
lines.english: Shinobu advised him to keep his doors locked, then left.

lines.japanese: 道ばたで、彼ははたと気付いた。
lines.english: He stopped short by the roadside as a thought struck him.

lines.japanese: （……武器、いるかな）
lines.english: (…Do I need a weapon?)

lines.japanese: テーザー銃について考えた。
lines.english: He considered a TASER.

lines.japanese: 却下した。
lines.english: Rejected.

lines.japanese:
千鳥に頼めばどうにかなったかも知れないが、
一度しか使えないのは問題外だ。
lines.english: Chidori might have been able to procure one, but a weapon he could use only once was out of the question.

lines.japanese:
相手の力量を考えれば、怖くて選択できたもので
はない。
lines.english: Given his opponent's skill, relying on one was too frightening to contemplate.

lines.japanese:
両手にそれぞれ構えて、腰のベルトにもたくさん
さして臨めば、あるいは……とも思うが……圧倒的
に恥ずかしい。
lines.english: Perhaps he could hold one in each hand and line his belt with spares… but that would be… unspeakably embarrassing.

lines.japanese: 却下却下。
lines.english: Rejected, rejected.

lines.japanese:
しばし考えて、彼は携帯を開いた。
　古いメールを確認する。
lines.english: After a moment's thought, he opened his phone. He checked an old email.
Tatemachi Fine Sword Polishing Address / *********** Telephone / ***-***-****

lines.japanese: すぐそばだ。
lines.english: It was very close by.

lines.japanese:
携帯から預金口座を確認する。
　千鳥に回そうかとも考えたが、さすがにやめてお
いた。
lines.english: He checked his bank account from his phone. He considered billing Chidori, but thought better of it.

lines.japanese:
彼女の怒る姿に興味はあるが、その怒られ方は、
違う。
lines.english: He was curious to see her angry, but not like that.

lines.japanese: 残額は充分にあった。
lines.english: His balance was more than sufficient.

lines.japanese:
給与というわけでもないが、使い道のない金銭は
ずっとムダに蓄積されてきたのだ。
lines.english: It was not exactly a salary, but money he had no use for had been piling up for a long time.

lines.japanese:
先ほどのメールに戻り、リンクボタンを押して直
接電話をかけた。
lines.english: He returned to the earlier email, pressed the link button, and called the number directly.

lines.japanese:
少し話をして、購入。
　円が通じて幸いだった。
lines.english: After a brief conversation, he made the purchase. Fortunately, yen was still accepted.

lines.japanese:
すぐに電話帳を開き、開店中のデパートか百貨店・
スポーツ用品店を検索する。
lines.english: He immediately opened the directory and searched for an open department store or sporting-goods shop.

lines.japanese: 駅前のデパートが一つ、開店中だった。
lines.english: One department store near the station was still open.

lines.japanese:
ゴルフバックを購入し、たてまちに寄った。
　書類にサインをして、現物を受け取る。
lines.english: He bought a golf bag, then stopped by Tatemachi. He signed the paperwork and received the item.

lines.japanese: 「……それに入れちゃうの？」
lines.english: “…You're putting it in there?”

lines.japanese: もちろん。
lines.english: Of course.

lines.japanese: 「犯罪ってこたぁないよね？」
lines.english: “This isn't for a crime, right?”

lines.japanese: あのね―――
lines.english: Oh, come on—

lines.japanese: 「一応、確認させてね」
lines.english: “I just have to make sure.”

lines.japanese:
店主は書類に記載した保護者……千鳥に電話をか
けた。
lines.english: The shopkeeper called the guardian named on the form… Chidori.

lines.japanese: 電話を切った。
lines.english: He hung up.

lines.japanese: 「毎度あり」
lines.english: “Thanks for your business.”

lines.japanese:
謝罪もなしだった。
　店を出る。
lines.english: There was no apology. Shinobu left the shop.

lines.japanese:
メールが飛んできた。
　千鳥からだ。
lines.english: A new email came in. From Chidori.

lines.japanese:
TITLE:緊急
　
　
　＊＊町＊＊－＊＊－＊＊メゾンドザウルス１０３
lines.english: SUBJECT: URGENT   **-**-**, **-cho, Maison de Saurus, Apt. 103

lines.japanese: 駆けだした。
lines.english: He broke into a run.

lines.japanese: 現場には数名の警官がいた。
lines.english: Several police officers were at the scene.

lines.japanese:
ロープで立ち入りが制限され、野次馬が数名、周
囲で立ち話をしていた。
lines.english: The area had been roped off, and several onlookers stood nearby talking among themselves.

lines.japanese:
近所の人間らしい。
　質問してみると、
lines.english: Apparently, they were neighbors. He asked them what had happened—

lines.japanese: 「……首が、切られたって……」
lines.english: “…They say someone was… beheaded…”

lines.japanese: 「最近はやりのアレみたいだ」
lines.english: “Sounds like that thing that's been happening lately.”

lines.japanese: 「……おっとろしい……おっとろしいわ……」
lines.english: “…Frightful… just frightful…”

lines.japanese: 骸が発見されたようだ。
lines.english: A body had apparently been discovered.

lines.japanese: 「生きててもなんも楽しくないわ……」
lines.english: “There's no joy left in being alive…”

lines.japanese:
慰める言葉もない。
　ただ胸が痛むばかりだ。
lines.english: He had no words for her. All he felt was the ache in his chest.

lines.japanese:
犯人はどうなったのか。
　警官がやってきて、こう言った。
lines.english: What had become of the culprit? A police officer approached and said—

lines.japanese: 「皆さん、今日はしっかりと戸締まりをして―――」
lines.english: “Everyone, be sure to keep your doors securely locked today—”

lines.japanese:
捕まっていないらしい。
　その場を離れる。
lines.english: Apparently, the culprit was still at large. Shinobu left the scene.

lines.japanese:
千鳥からのメールが来ていた。
　目を通す。
lines.english: Another email from Chidori had arrived. He read it.

lines.japanese:
TITLE:犯行時刻
　
　
　遺体の発見時間は１２時４２分。
　死亡時間は不明。
　血液の凝固具合から、３０分前後。
lines.english: SUBJECT: Time of Offense   Body discovered at 12:42 p.m. Time of death unknown. Based on blood coagulation, approximately thirty minutes earlier.

lines.japanese:
才媛である。
　足を止めた。
lines.english: She was brilliant. He stopped walking.
(What if—)

lines.japanese: 自分で殺害をしたとしたら、どう動く？
lines.english: If he were the killer, what would he do next?

lines.japanese: 犯人の特性を考える。
lines.english: He considered the culprit's traits.

lines.japanese: 彼の身につけていた技術について。
lines.english: The techniques he had mastered.

lines.japanese:
考え方について。
　思想について。
lines.english: His way of thinking. His ideology.

lines.japanese: 瞑想して自らの中に再現する。
lines.english: He sank into meditation and recreated the culprit within himself.

lines.japanese:
自我が拡大すると、思想や変態性はどこまでも肥
大化する。
lines.english: As the ego expanded, ideology and perversity swelled without limit.

lines.japanese:
理性も感情も越えて、ただ強烈な自己定義として
機能しはじめる、思考的癌細胞。
lines.english: A cancer cell of the mind—beyond reason and emotion, functioning only as an overpowering definition of self.

lines.japanese: 考える。考える―――
lines.english: Think. Think—

lines.japanese:
額に汗が浮かぶ。
　どれほど思い巡らせても、解答はいっかな出てこ
ない。
lines.english: Sweat beaded on his brow. No matter how long he turned it over, the answer refused to come.

lines.japanese:
読み切れない。
　行動にまるで一貫性がないのだ。
lines.english: He could not read it. The culprit's behavior had no consistency at all.

lines.japanese:
これでは偶然、犯行現場に居合わせるしかないで
はないか。
lines.english: At this rate, his only hope was to stumble onto the scene of a crime in progress.

lines.japanese: ヒントは、どこにあるのだろう？
lines.english: Where was the clue?

lines.japanese: 犯人にもっとも近い単語とは、何だろう？
lines.english: What single word came closest to the culprit?

lines.japanese: 犯人の特性を一言で示す言葉は、何だろう？
lines.english: What word expressed the culprit's defining trait?

lines.japanese:
疑問と疑念は融合し、堂々巡り。
　無力な時間が過ぎた。その時。
lines.english: Questions and suspicions merged into one endless circle. Time passed without result. Then—

lines.japanese:
天啓とも言うべきイメージ。
　それは、簡単な言葉だった。
lines.english: An image that could only be called a revelation. It was a simple word.

lines.japanese: サムライ。
lines.english: Samurai.

lines.japanese: その単語は、連鎖的な閃きをもたらした。
lines.english: The word set off a chain of insights.

lines.japanese: サムライ。つまり武士。
lines.english: Samurai. In other words, a warrior.

lines.japanese: 武士は何を考えるか。
lines.english: What occupied a warrior's mind?

lines.japanese:
介錯。武家の誉れ。
　慈悲。
lines.english: The coup de grâce. A warrior's honor. Mercy.

lines.japanese: ならば、断じてそれは猟奇殺人ではない。
lines.english: Then it could not possibly be a bizarre murder.

lines.japanese: （……優しい……殺人……介錯……）
lines.english: (…A merciful… killing… a coup de grâce…)

lines.japanese:
どのような自我が拡大すれば、この結論に辿り着
くだろうか。
lines.english: What kind of expanded ego would lead to such a conclusion?

lines.japanese:
そして最終的に何を望むだろうか。
　矜持と考えて良いのだろう。
lines.english: And what would it desire in the end? Pride, he supposed.

lines.japanese: 矜持が全てなのだ。
lines.english: Pride was everything.

lines.japanese:
であるから、栄誉ある死は慈愛によってもたらさ
れる。
lines.english: An honorable death, then, was something granted out of compassion.

lines.japanese:
彼はおそらく、被害者達に憐憫さえ抱いているは
ずだ。
lines.english: The culprit probably even pitied the victims.

lines.japanese:
犯人にとって、生者の全てが生き恥をさらしてい
るように見えたなら、間違いなく。
lines.english: Certainly—if, in his eyes, every living person was living in disgrace.

lines.japanese:
せめて矜持を保ったまま、終わらせようとしてい
る―――そう思えた。
lines.english: He was trying to end their lives while at least leaving their pride intact— that was how it seemed.

lines.japanese: 他には、サムライは何が嬉しいか。
lines.english: What else would please a samurai?

lines.japanese:
実際の武士ではない。
　空想化されたサムライである。
lines.english: Not an actual warrior. An imagined samurai.
(A worthy foe—)

lines.japanese:
戦場で相まみえ一騎打ちをする栄誉。
　それは恍惚とともに迎え入れられる、最高の概念
ではなかろうか。
lines.english: The honor of facing a worthy opponent in single combat on the battlefield. Was that not the highest ideal—one to be welcomed with ecstasy?

lines.japanese: かつて斎はこう言ったことがある。
lines.english: Itsuki had once said this.

lines.japanese: 生き恥だ、と。
lines.english: That going on living was a disgrace.

lines.japanese: 背筋が震えた。
lines.english: A shiver ran down Shinobu's spine.

lines.japanese:
求めるものは二つ。
　強敵と、生き恥からの救済。
lines.english: He sought two things. A worthy foe, and salvation from the shame of living.

lines.japanese:
もしそうなら、一人、どうしても首を落とさねば
ならない人物がいるのではないか？
lines.english: If that was so, was there not one person whose head he absolutely had to take?

lines.japanese: 半身であった少女。
lines.english: The girl who had been his other half.

lines.japanese: 生き恥の片側を担う、塚本葉子である。
lines.english: Youko Tsukamoto, who bore one half of that living disgrace.

lines.japanese: 千鳥に電話をかけた。
lines.english: Shinobu called Chidori.

lines.japanese:
すぐではないかも知れないが、犯人が狙う可能性
のある人物について告げた。
lines.english: He told her who the culprit might target, if not immediately.

lines.japanese: 塚本葉子。
lines.english: Youko Tsukamoto.

lines.japanese: 『縁のある名前ですね―――』
lines.english: “That name has ties to us—”

lines.japanese: かすかな感慨とともに、千鳥は息を吐いた。
lines.english: Chidori exhaled with a faint note of emotion.

lines.japanese:
『……了解。彼女の身辺に変化があったら、
　連絡が行くようにします』
lines.english: “…Understood. If anything changes around her, I'll arrange for word to reach you.”

lines.japanese:
『しかしやはりというか、現場の動きに即応できる
　のはあなただけ……だから私はあなたの無茶を止
　めることは難しい……』
lines.english: “But as expected, you’re the only one who can respond at once to developments on the ground… which makes it difficult for me to stop you from doing anything reckless…”

lines.japanese:
『私たちの間で取り定めたルールが、尊く守られる
　ことを期待します』
lines.english: “I trust that the rule we agreed upon will remain sacrosanct.”

lines.japanese:
電話を切った。
　次に短縮ダイヤルから葉子の番号にかけた。
lines.english: He ended the call. Then he called Youko using speed dial.

lines.japanese: 電話が鳴って、葉子はむっくりと身を起こした。
lines.english: The phone rang, and Youko lurched upright.

lines.japanese: 寝ぼけ眼だった。
lines.english: Her eyes were bleary with sleep.
“…Ngh.”

lines.japanese:
少しムカついたので、コール十回まで待ってから
取った。
lines.english: A little annoyed, she let it ring ten times before picking up.

lines.japanese:
昼過ぎまで寝ていたことなどは、考慮の対象外だ
った。
lines.english: The fact that she’d slept past noon did not enter into her calculations.

lines.japanese: 「……もしもし？」
lines.english: “…Hello?”

lines.japanese: 『葉子、僕だけど』
lines.english: “Youko, it's me.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、忍さん……ごめんなさい」
lines.english: “Oh, Shinobu… I'm sorry.”
“What?”

lines.japanese:
「いえ、気にしないでください。
　で、どうしました？　デートですか？
　デートの呼び出しなのですか？」
lines.english: “No, never mind. What is it? A date? Are you calling to ask me on a date?”

lines.japanese: 『うん、デートは後回しにしよう』
lines.english: “Yeah, the date can wait.”

lines.japanese: 『葉子、君はそこで引きこもりまくって欲しい』
lines.english: “Youko, I need you to go full shut-in and stay right where you are.”

lines.japanese: 「得意です。引きこもることは」
lines.english: “Being a shut-in is one of my specialties.”

lines.japanese: 『頼もしいお言葉だよ』
lines.english: “That's very reassuring.”

lines.japanese: 「なにゆえ？」
lines.english: “Why, pray tell?”

lines.japanese: 『君は狙われている』
lines.english: “Someone is targeting you.”

lines.japanese: 「地球がいつも狙われているようにですね」
lines.english: “The way Earth is always under attack, you mean.”

lines.japanese: 『そうさ』
lines.english: “Exactly.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふふ、ふふふふふ」
lines.english: “Heh heh heh. Heh heh heh heh.”

lines.japanese: 『……お兄さん、連れて帰るから』
lines.english: “…I'll bring your brother home.”

lines.japanese: 「どうでもいいです、それは」
lines.english: “I don't particularly care about that.”

lines.japanese: 「なんちゃって」
lines.english: “Just kidding.”

lines.japanese: 『冗談に聞こえなかったけど……』
lines.english: “That didn't sound like a joke…”

lines.japanese:
「本当は心配してます。
　けど……忍さんも無事戻って欲しいです」
lines.english: “I really am worried. But… I want you to come back safe too.”
“…Yeah.”

lines.japanese: 「間がありました。やりなおし」
lines.english: “There was a pause. Try again.”

lines.japanese: 『戻るよ』
lines.english: “I'll come back.”

lines.japanese:
『心強い味方もいるし……
　なんとかなりそうな感じはある。
　でも正直、きついかな……斎次第』
lines.english: “I’ve got a reliable ally, too… It feels like we might pull this off. Honestly, though, it might be rough… Depends on Itsuki.”

lines.japanese: 「しょーもない人です」
lines.english: “He really is hopeless.”

lines.japanese: 『……叱ってあげると、いいよ。戻ったら』
lines.english: “…You should give him a good scolding. When he gets back.”

lines.japanese: 「そうしま」
lines.english: “I'll—”

lines.japanese: 『いい、そこを出ないようにね？』
lines.english: “Got it? Don't leave, okay?”

lines.japanese: 「あい」
lines.english: “Aye.”

lines.japanese: 『生理用品とか買いに行ったらダメだからね』
lines.english: “And don't go out for period products or anything, okay?”

lines.japanese: 「でもストックがありません」
lines.english: “But I'm out.”

lines.japanese:
『僕のシャツとか……
　なんでも、代用していいから……』
lines.english: “Use one of my shirts… or anything else you can find…”

lines.japanese: 「どきどきしませんか、それ？」
lines.english: “Wouldn't that get your heart racing?”
“…I wonder if it would…?”

lines.japanese: 『あとあんまんとかもみだりに買いに行くな』
lines.english: “And no wanton runs for red-bean buns, either.”

lines.japanese: 「命令形……」
lines.english: “An imperative…”

lines.japanese: 『とにかく例外なくダメ。ヒキって！』
lines.english: “Anyway, no exceptions. Stay shut in!”

lines.japanese: 「うす」
lines.english: “Yessir.”

lines.japanese: 『じゃあまた連絡するから』
lines.english: “I'll call you again later.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、忍さん」
lines.english: “Wait, Shinobu.”

lines.japanese: 『なに？』
lines.english: “Yeah?”

lines.japanese:
葉子は受話器にディープキスをした。
　むちゅう。
lines.english: Youko planted a deep kiss on the receiver. Mmmwah.

lines.japanese: 「……でした」
lines.english: “…There.”

lines.japanese: 『……はい、ごちそうさまです……』
lines.english: “…Right. Thanks for the treat…”

lines.japanese: 「からまつさまでした」
lines.english: “Thanks for the tree.”

lines.japanese: 『その調子で、頑張って生きていきましょう』
lines.english: “That's the spirit. Let's both stay alive.”

lines.japanese:
電話は切れた。
　性急な感じだった。
lines.english: The call ended. It felt abrupt.

lines.japanese:
「……みだりに買いに行くなと命令形で言って私を
　小粋に濡らした忍さんですが、しかし淫らに買い
　に行くなとは言ってない、か」
lines.english: “Shinobu commanded me to make no wanton shopping runs, and the imperative left me wet in the most tasteful fashion… but he did not command me not to go shopping while wanton, did he?”

lines.japanese: とんちだ。
lines.english: A feat of wordplay.

lines.japanese:
「それにこの塚本葉子、存在感のない歩き方を心得
　ておりまする」
lines.english: “Besides, I, Youko Tsukamoto, have mastered the art of walking without attracting notice.”

lines.japanese: 目立たないよう制服に着替えた。
lines.english: She changed into her uniform so she wouldn't stand out.

lines.japanese:
実はこの制服はかなり目立つ。
　ブレザータイプでもセーラーでもないからだ。
　とても有名な制服であった。
lines.english: In fact, the uniform made her extremely conspicuous. It was neither a blazer nor a sailor uniform. And a very famous one at that.

lines.japanese: 葉子は知らない。
lines.english: Youko had no idea.

lines.japanese: 「よし、と」
lines.english: “Right, then.”

lines.japanese: 小銭入れを手に、外に出た。
lines.english: She took her coin purse and headed outside.

lines.japanese:
「にくまんと生理グッズ買いつつ、家の様子見に行
　こう」
lines.english: “I'll grab a meat bun and some period products, then go see how things are at the house.”

lines.japanese: こういう人間だった。
lines.english: That was the sort of person she was.

lines.japanese:
門倉に徴集された兄を、忍が連れ戻すと言って出
て行って、どれくらいになるだろう。
lines.english: Shinobu had gone off saying he would bring back her brother, whom Kadokura had conscripted. How long ago had that been?

lines.japanese:
以前は男子御用達の仮眠用ベッドが、今では葉子
専用になってしまった。
lines.english: The boys' old napping cot had now become Youko's private bed.

lines.japanese: 門倉が戻ってきた。
lines.english: Kadokura had returned.

lines.japanese:
事実は重く、忍に何ができるのかと思う。
　不安でもある。
lines.english: The reality of it weighed on her. What could Shinobu possibly do? It worried her, too.

lines.japanese: しかし―――
lines.english: And yet—

lines.japanese:
葉子はなぜか、そのことについては斎は戻ってく
ると確信できていた。
lines.english: For some reason, Youko was certain: Itsuki would come back.

lines.japanese: 感覚としては予知に近い。
lines.english: The feeling was almost like precognition.

lines.japanese:
忍のそばにいると、途方もない心の広がりを垣間
見ることがある。
lines.english: At Shinobu's side, she sometimes caught a glimpse of an unfathomable expanse of mind.

lines.japanese:
球形の世界を見渡すことはどれほどの視力を持っ
ていても物理的に不可能だが、全人類の視野をいち
どきに見通したような……そう、全視感だ。
lines.english: No matter how keen the eyesight, no one could physically see every side of a spherical world. Yet it felt as though she had taken in all humanity's fields of vision at once… Yes: a sense of omnivision.

lines.japanese:
以前は、忍の器が大きいのだと思っていた。
　そうではなかった。
lines.english: She used to think Shinobu's own heart was simply that vast. It wasn't.

lines.japanese: 「だって、苦しんでいるから―――」
lines.english: “Because he's suffering—”

lines.japanese:
囁きは微風に押し流される。
　聞く者はいない。
lines.english: Her whisper dissolved on the breeze. No one was there to hear it.

lines.japanese:
葉子の身辺にアンテナを張れば、あとはもう見回
るだけだった。
lines.english: With a watch in place around Youko, all that remained was to patrol the area.

lines.japanese:
次の犠牲者が葉子か否かは、正直わからない。
　葉子以外が殺されることもあり、そちらを阻止す
る手段はない。
lines.english: Honestly, there was no knowing whether Youko would be the next victim. Someone else might be killed instead, and there was no way to prevent that.

lines.japanese:
だがもし、偶然遭遇することができれば……向こ
うはこちらを放置しないだろう。
lines.english: But if they happened to cross paths… the killer would hardly ignore him.

lines.japanese: そう読んでもいた。
lines.english: That, too, was his assessment.

lines.japanese:
人通りの少ない街を、練り歩く。
　微風が吹き抜ける。
lines.english: He walked through streets nearly empty of people. A light breeze swept past.

lines.japanese: 予感した。
lines.english: He felt it coming.

lines.japanese:
子供の頃から、いや、もっと以前から綿々と継承
されてきた美意識が、途絶えた。
lines.english: An aesthetic sensibility handed down unbroken since his childhood—no, since long before then—had come to an end.

lines.japanese:
歴史は広く大きい地図の如きものではない。
　過去から現在に向けて、這いずり現れる蛇である。
　ことに家風を重んじる土地においては、特に。
lines.english: History was no broad and sprawling map. It was a serpent crawling out of the past and into the present. Especially in a land that set such store by family tradition.

lines.japanese:
ある種の思想エネルギーといってもいい。
　本来なら未来に向けて膨張・拡大し、波及し―――
繁栄を維持・獲得するのが門倉の存在意義である。
lines.english: It might even be called a kind of ideological energy. By rights, it should swell toward the future, expanding and spreading— for Kadokura existed to preserve its prosperity and increase it.

lines.japanese:
出口を閉ざされ、もがきのたうち、弾けようとし
ている。
lines.english: With its outlet sealed, it writhed and thrashed, straining to burst.

lines.japanese: その最高潮を、間近に感じるのだ。
lines.english: He could feel that pressure nearing its peak.

lines.japanese: 近い。
lines.english: Close.

lines.japanese:
目の前に壁となってそそり立っている。
　手を伸ばす。
　触れてみる。
lines.english: It towered before him like a wall. He reached out. Tried to touch it.

lines.japanese:
指先は空を切った。当然だ。
　別に幻覚を見たわけではないのだから。
lines.english: His fingertips cut through empty air. Of course. He wasn't hallucinating.

lines.japanese:
突きだしたまま、てのひらを閉じて拳にする。
　拳の中心に羽虫でも握っているような掻痒感がある。
lines.english: Keeping his arm extended, he closed his hand into a fist. A prickling itch lay in his palm, as though he had closed it around a gnat.

lines.japanese:
引き戻し、開いてみても何もない。
　不可視の虫を観測することはできない。
lines.english: He drew it back and opened it. Nothing. There was no way to observe an invisible insect.

lines.japanese: 突風。
lines.english: A gust.

lines.japanese:
風は殺害情報を含んでいた。
　血の匂いともいうのかも知れない。
　あるいは気配とも。
lines.english: The wind carried information about a killing. Perhaps it could be called the smell of blood. Or a presence.
(He moved—)

lines.japanese: 電撃に打たれたように、直感が働く。
lines.english: His intuition fired like a bolt of lightning.

lines.japanese:
脳裏に、連結器がはまった音。
　なぜ葉子のことを思いついた時、ここまで考えら
れなかったのか。
lines.english: In his mind, a coupling clanked into place. Why hadn't he followed the thought this far when Youko first came to mind?

lines.japanese: 彼は、聖なる粛清を行う―――
lines.english: He was carrying out a sacred purge—

lines.japanese:
葉子だけではない。
　その他の親族も同罪……同じ立場だ。
lines.english: Not only Youko. The rest of the family were equally guilty… in the same position.

lines.japanese: 彼らは矜持を担う者たち……武家である。
lines.english: They were the bearers of that pride… members of a warrior house.

lines.japanese:
あの日、彼らは担い損ねた。
　武士としての責任を取らねばならない。
lines.english: That day, they had failed to bear it. They had to answer for that failure as warriors.

lines.japanese: 殺害が市内だけに起きていたこと……偶然ではない。
lines.english: The murders had all occurred within the city… It was no coincidence.

lines.japanese:
地域全体の罪を、濯ごうとしているのだ。
　街を怨ずる者として。
lines.english: He meant to wash clean the guilt of the entire region— as one who bore a grudge against the town.

lines.japanese:
屋敷はひっそりとしていた。
　しかしいつもと違う点が一つ。
　人の気配がないのである。
lines.english: The estate lay hushed. But this time, one thing was different. There was no sign of anyone.

lines.japanese: いつものこと？
lines.english: Wasn't that always the case?

lines.japanese: 違う。この静けさは異質なものだ。
lines.english: No. There was something alien about this silence.

lines.japanese:
日頃静寂に彩られた屋敷ではあるが―――空気ま
で殺害されてしまったことはない。
lines.english: The estate was always steeped in silence—but never before had the very air been murdered.

lines.japanese:
違和感が大音声をかき鳴らしている。
　音も気にせず、砂利を踏み歩く。
lines.english: The sense of wrongness clamored at full volume. He strode across the gravel, heedless of the noise.

lines.japanese:
おそらくもう気に掛ける必要はなかった。
　庭を横切り、屋敷に近づき、土足のまま縁に上が
った。
lines.english: There was probably no longer any need to mind the noise. He crossed the garden, made for the house, and stepped onto the veranda without removing his shoes.

lines.japanese:
むせかえるほどの血臭が立ちこめていた。
　ためらいを押し殺し、障子戸を開け放つ。
lines.english: The stench of blood hung thick enough to choke him. Suppressing his hesitation, he flung open the shoji.

lines.japanese:
臭いどころではない。
　部屋には死が充満していたのだから。
　言葉もない。
lines.english: It went beyond smell. The room was saturated with death. He had no words.

lines.japanese:
乱れ桜に紅を撒き、それは美しい地獄だった。
　狭い室内でありながら、居合わせた全員が、首を
落とされて死んでいた。
lines.english: Crimson splashed across a riot of cherry blossoms: a beautiful hell. Though the room was small, every person gathered there had been decapitated.

lines.japanese:
何人かは、正座の形を維持したまま事切れている。
　転がった首が床に四つ転がっていた。
　一目見ただけでは、誰が誰のものかわからない。
lines.english: Several had died still kneeling in formal posture. Four severed heads lay scattered across the floor. At a glance, there was no telling which belonged to whom.

lines.japanese: 血の海だった。
lines.english: A sea of blood.

lines.japanese: 新鮮な、血の海だった―――
lines.english: A fresh sea of blood—

lines.japanese: （葉子は……工場にいるはずだよな……）
lines.english: (Youko… should be at the factory…)

lines.japanese: 電話が鳴った。
lines.english: The phone rang.

lines.japanese:
誰からの連絡か、容易に想像がついてしまう。
　無視したいところだがそうも行かない。
lines.english: He could all too easily guess who was calling. He wanted to ignore it, but couldn't.

lines.japanese: 果たしてそれは千鳥からであった。
lines.english: Sure enough, it was Chidori.

lines.japanese: 『今、門倉の屋敷に連絡が取れないそうです』
lines.english: “I'm told they can't reach anyone at the Kadokura estate.”

lines.japanese: 事情を話した。
lines.english: He explained the situation.

lines.japanese:
『……そうですか。３０分前に一度、門倉の車が戻
　っています』
lines.english: “…I see. Kadokura’s car returned thirty minutes ago.”

lines.japanese:
『その時点では門を開ける人間がいたようですから、
　犯行はそれから実行された可能性がありますね』
lines.english: “Someone was apparently still there to open the gate at that point, so it is possible the killings were carried out afterward.”

lines.japanese: 信じられない早業だ。
lines.english: Unbelievably fast work.

lines.japanese:
部屋を次から次へと調べていく。
　先ほど見たのは、話し合うための大部屋である。
lines.english: He searched one room after another. The room he'd just seen was a large meeting chamber.

lines.japanese:
この屋敷に常時いるのは、家政婦や庭師なども含
めると１５名前後。
lines.english: Roughly fifteen people were normally at the estate, counting housekeepers and gardeners.

lines.japanese:
寝泊まりするのはそのうち１０名ほどであり、こ
こに斎と葉子も含まれる。
lines.english: About ten lived on the premises, including Itsuki and Youko.

lines.japanese:
日曜日である。
　休日は、地方や都内から親族が来ることもあるし、
逆に出かけることもある。
lines.english: It was Sunday. On days off, relatives sometimes came in from elsewhere in the country or from Tokyo, while people from the estate might go out.

lines.japanese:
庭師などもいないことがある。
　先ほどの４人だけですんでいるのかどうか。
lines.english: The gardeners might not be there, either. Were those four the only ones?

lines.japanese:
厨房に向かう。
　死体がふたつ。いや、二組。
　古くからいる料理人と給仕役の老婦。とその首。
lines.english: He headed for the kitchen. Two bodies. No—two sets. The longtime cook and the elderly serving woman. And their heads.

lines.japanese: これで６名。
lines.english: That made six.

lines.japanese:
残りふたりは比較的若い。
　ひとりは正道。
lines.english: The remaining two were relatively young. One was Seidou.

lines.japanese:
そしてもう一人は、正道の補佐をするため屋敷で
経営学を学んでいる若者。
lines.english: The other was a young man studying management at the estate so that he might assist Seidou.

lines.japanese:
気が付けば、ゴルフバッグから得物を取り出して
いる。
lines.english: Before he realized it, he had drawn his weapon from the golf bag.

lines.japanese:
重みは手に頼もしいが……果たして―――
　考えるのをやめた。
lines.english: Its weight was reassuring in his hand… but would it— He stopped thinking.

lines.japanese: 件の若者の部屋。
lines.english: The young man's room.

lines.japanese: 死亡、確認。
lines.english: Confirmed dead.

lines.japanese:
もう心は揺るがない。
　淡々と次の部屋を見に行く。
lines.english: His heart no longer wavered. Dispassionately, he went to inspect the next room.

lines.japanese: 最後の部屋だけは、祈るようにあらためた。
lines.english: Only the final room did he check as if in prayer.

lines.japanese: 葉子の部屋―――
lines.english: Youko's room—

lines.japanese: 不在。
lines.english: Empty.

lines.japanese:
双肩に重しが乗せられた。
　安堵の重量だ。
lines.english: A weight settled across his shoulders. The weight of relief.

lines.japanese:
人ひとりの命を気に掛けるというのは、岩を背負
うような気苦労を強いる。
lines.english: Caring about a single life meant bearing a weight of worry like a boulder on his back.

lines.japanese: （万が一にも……戻ってなくて良かった）
lines.english: (Thank goodness… she hadn't come back.)

lines.japanese: 最初の部屋に戻る。
lines.english: He returned to the first room.

lines.japanese: 死亡者は以上だ。
lines.english: That accounted for all the dead.

lines.japanese:
千鳥に簡潔に連絡を済ませる。
　あとは向こうでやってくれるだろう。
　誰が殺されたのか、確認はあとで済ませれば良い。
lines.english: He gave Chidori a brief report. They would probably handle the rest on their end. The dead could be identified later.

lines.japanese:
常駐している人間が狙われた。
　やはり一度、葉子と対面しておくべきだろう。
lines.english: The people who lived here had been targeted. He needed to see Youko in person after all.

lines.japanese:
すでに夕刻になっていた。
　一瞬のようで、濃密な時間を過ごしたらしい。
　ほどなく夜になる。
lines.english: It was already evening. It had felt like an instant, yet the time had been impossibly full. Night would fall before long.

lines.japanese: もう、饗宴は終わらなければならない。
lines.english: This banquet had to end now.

lines.japanese: 虚空に問いかけた。
lines.english: He asked the empty air a question.

lines.japanese: その向こうにいるはずの、かつての友に向けて。
lines.english: It was meant for the friend he had once known, who should be somewhere beyond it.

lines.japanese: もう、満足しただろう？
lines.english: You've had your fill by now, haven't you?

lines.japanese:
携帯から葉子の番号にかけた。
　繋がらなかった。
lines.english: He called Youko's number from his cell phone. The call didn't connect.

lines.japanese: 夜気と同時に這い寄った、戦慄とともに知る。
lines.english: A shudder crept over him with the night air, and he knew.

lines.japanese:
頭を空にしてかけずり回り、体力の最後の一滴、
尽きる気力の一絞りまでをも燃焼しなければならな
い時がやってきたのだ、と。
lines.english: The time had come to empty his mind and run himself ragged, to burn through the final drop of his strength and wring out every last shred of his failing will.

lines.japanese:
今日のために鍛えていた。
　そう思えた。
lines.english: He had trained for this day. That was how it felt.

lines.japanese:
虚ろな時間の果て、ついに両者は邂逅を果たすこ
とになる。
lines.english: At the end of that hollow stretch of time, the two would finally come face to face.

lines.japanese:
しかしそれは、様々な無力の代償としての結果だ
った。
lines.english: But that meeting came at the cost of so many forms of helplessness.

lines.japanese: 不幸すぎる出会いだった。
lines.english: It was too tragic a meeting.

lines.japanese: 何もかもが遅すぎた。
lines.english: Everything was far too late.

lines.japanese: だとしても、今さら時を遡りようもない。
lines.english: Even so, there was no going back in time now.

lines.japanese: るる
lines.english: In rivulets.

lines.japanese:
葉子は壁によりかかり、縷々と流したおびただし
い血によって、床に地図を描いていた―――
lines.english: Youko leaned against the wall, the copious blood streaming from her in rivulets drawing a map across the floor—

lines.japanese: あってはならないことだった。
lines.english: This could not be.

lines.japanese: 決して、傷つけてはいけない相手だったのだ。
lines.english: She was someone who must never be harmed.
“Ah… you're here…”

lines.japanese: あどけない顔で、葉子が笑う。
lines.english: Youko smiled, her face as innocent as a child's.

lines.japanese: 「やっと……来た……」
lines.english: “Finally… you're here…”

lines.japanese: 疲労の色が濃い。
lines.english: Exhaustion was written all over her.

lines.japanese:
逃げ続けて、ここで捕まったらしい。
　かろうじてでも生きていてくれたことが、ありが
たかった。
lines.english: After fleeing all this time, she seemed to have been caught here. He was grateful that she had held on to life, if only barely.

lines.japanese:
大勢の人間を殺し、今また葉子を傷つけた人物が、
今目の前に立っている。
lines.english: The person who had killed so many and now wounded Youko stood before him.

lines.japanese: 来訪者の存在に、警戒を示している。
lines.english: He watched the newcomer warily.

lines.japanese:
三人以外、誰もいない地下道。
　たちこめる血の香り。
　暗がりの向こうに、立つ人影。
lines.english: An underground passage. No one but the three of them. The reek of blood thick in the air. A figure standing in the darkness beyond.

lines.japanese:
そしてその手に、鞘から剥かれ狂気をのせて青む
一刀。
lines.english: And in the figure's hand, an unsheathed sword, its blue-tinged steel freighted with madness.

lines.japanese:
月光もなく、なお冴え冴えと煌めく様に、主の殺
意に映える様子が仄見える。
lines.english: No moon shone, yet the blade glittered cold and clear, faintly aglow with its master's murderous intent.

lines.japanese: 棒反りにして見栄えなく、先身狭めに小賢しく。
lines.english: Its even curve was graceless, its blade narrowing shrewdly toward the point.

lines.japanese:
古鉄含みの刃は荒いばかりの瓢箪肌。
