れ、武用に耐えて精緻な切れ味。
lines.english: Its old iron showed only a coarse, gourd-skin grain. Yet the linked gunome in its hamon formed the beadlike pattern known as juzu-ba, while the blade itself was fit for battle, its edge exquisitely keen.

lines.japanese:
実直な殺意の代行者、鍛え抜かれたその一刀に、
三ッ胴截断の添銘を戴く最上大業物―――
lines.english: A forthright instrument of murderous intent: this masterfully forged, supreme-grade cutting blade bore an added inscription recording that it had severed three stacked bodies in one stroke—

lines.japanese: それはまさに、門倉の象徴そのものであったのだ。
lines.english: It was, in every sense, the very symbol of Kadokura.

lines.japanese: 「ごめんなさい……もう……」
lines.english: “I'm sorry… I can't…”

lines.japanese:
無銘の刀を、袈裟に構える。
　話し合う暇もあるのかどうか。
　命の狭間に数打ちものの、鈍い曇りもスッと晴れ。
lines.english: He raised his unsigned sword in a diagonal guard. Was there even time to talk? At the threshold of life and death, the dull haze lifted cleanly from the mass-produced blade.

lines.japanese: 両者は殺意の橋をかけたのだった。
lines.english: A bridge of murderous intent stretched between them.

lines.japanese:
相手が死人の動きで前に出た。
　暗所から歩み出た、かつての友と対峙する。
lines.english: His opponent advanced with the movements of a dead man. He faced the friend he had once known, now stepping out of the darkness.
(…Itsuki—)

lines.japanese: そして彼は、
lines.english: And then he—

lines.japanese: 門倉正道と対峙した。
lines.english: —faced Seidou Kadokura.
(…Huh?)

lines.japanese: 門倉が狂気に屈し、どれほどの時が流れたのだろう。
lines.english: How much time had passed since Kadokura succumbed to madness?

lines.japanese:
予感できた結末であり、そして一度は友と呼ばれ
た相手、と一抹の情けくらいは持ち合わせた。
lines.english: The ending had been foreseeable. And he had at least a trace of compassion for someone he had once called a friend.

lines.japanese:
幼い頃、実直にすぎて不正を拒んだ斎少年を、門
倉はそれもまた友のあり方とねじ伏せた。
lines.english: When they were children, Kadokura had forced the painfully upright Itsuki, who refused wrongdoing, into submission by declaring that this, too, was friendship.

lines.japanese:
事情から実家より離され、召使いとして引き取ら
れた二人は、ただその言葉に納得するしかなかった。
lines.english: Separated from their own home by circumstance and taken in as servants, the two of them had no choice but to accept his words.

lines.japanese: 葉子の人形の有様もまた、幸福なのだと欺瞞して。
lines.english: They even deceived themselves into calling Youko's life as a doll a happy one.

lines.japanese:
想えばたった一言、一度限りの友だった。
　だとしても。
lines.english: Looking back, it was a friendship born of a single sentence, spoken only once. Even so.

lines.japanese: 短く斎は息を吐く。
lines.english: Itsuki let out a short breath.

lines.japanese:
一度はその言葉に乗った。弱さゆえに。
　状況を覆せないことに、屈服した。
lines.english: Once, he had gone along with those words. Out of weakness. He had surrendered because he could not change their circumstances.

lines.japanese: （なんだ……これ……？）
lines.english: (What… is this…?)

lines.japanese:
門倉正道と塚本斎、そして葉子。
　ただ三人だけの世界だった。
　他に人気はない。
lines.english: Seidou Kadokura, Itsuki Tsukamoto, and Youko. Only those three existed in that world. There was no sign of anyone else.

lines.japanese: （僕が…………いない？）
lines.english: (I'm…… not here?)

lines.japanese: 「斎か」
lines.english: “Itsuki?”

lines.japanese: 門倉が語りかけてくる。
lines.english: Kadokura spoke to him.

lines.japanese: （……斎の……視点を……見ていた？）
lines.english: (…Was I seeing everything… from Itsuki's point of view?)

lines.japanese: （なら、僕は）
lines.english: (Then I—)

lines.japanese: （どこにいるんだ―――？）
lines.english: (Where am I—?)

lines.japanese: 503 Service Unavailable
lines.english: 503 Service Unavailable
“…Itsuki?”

lines.japanese:
門倉正道が口を開いた。
　斎の眉が動く。
lines.english: Seidou Kadokura spoke. Itsuki's brow twitched.

lines.japanese: 理性がある？
lines.english: Was he still capable of reason?

lines.japanese: 「斎、俺のそばで動けよ」
lines.english: “Itsuki, come work at my side.”

lines.japanese: 「来るべき日のためにな」
lines.english: “For the day that is to come.”
“Itsuki—”

lines.japanese: 「俺とおまえで、大きな仕事をしよう」
lines.english: “Let's do something great together, you and me.”

lines.japanese: 上澄みだった。
lines.english: It was only the surface layer.

lines.japanese: 再生―――
lines.english: Playback—

lines.japanese: 斎はそんな単語を思い出す。
lines.english: Itsuki remembered the word.

lines.japanese: 「そして新しい時代に取り戻す。栄光のすべてを」
lines.english: “And in the new age, we will reclaim it. All our glory.”

lines.japanese:
教職を退いた千鳥の言葉を思い出す。
　自我拡大症について。
lines.english: He recalled what Chidori had said after leaving her teaching post. About Ego Expansion disorder.

lines.japanese:
『自我拡大……
　これはいわゆる自我肥大とは異なります』
lines.english: “Ego expansion… This is distinct from what is commonly called ego inflation.”

lines.japanese:
「さあ斎、葉子を連れてこい。あれにも仕事を与え
　てやる」
lines.english: “Now, Itsuki, bring me Youko. I'll give her work to do as well.”

lines.japanese: ふら、と正道が歩む。斎に向けて。
lines.english: Seidou took an unsteady step toward Itsuki.

lines.japanese:
『拡大症は、本来あるべきサイズを越えて、その人
　間の根幹にあたる部分……変態性とも言うべき欲
　求が無限に膨張していきます』
lines.english: “In Ego Expansion disorder, a desire at the very foundation of the person— a desire one might even call deviant—swells without limit beyond its natural proportions.”

lines.japanese: 『それは心の癌細胞と言えます』
lines.english: “It could be called a cancer of the mind.”

lines.japanese:
『結果、身体機能に異変が生じます。特に恒常性が
　冒された場合死に至ることもありますが、大方は
　自意識と肉体の自由を失い生ける死人と化します』
lines.english: “The result is abnormal bodily function. If it compromises homeostasis, it may even be fatal; more often, however, the sufferer loses self-awareness and control of the body, becoming a living corpse.”

lines.japanese:
『その状態になった人間は、かつて人であった規範
　にいびつに縛られるようになります』
lines.english: “Someone in that state becomes grotesquely bound to the norms that governed them when they were human.”

lines.japanese: 『害し、犯し、食すようになります』
lines.english: “They begin to harm, violate, and devour.”

lines.japanese:
『全てが無軌道な暴徒になるわけでもなく、肩が接
　触したとか、当人が思うなりの手順を踏んで感情
　の移行を行うことが多いようです』
lines.english: “They do not all become indiscriminate rioters. Often, something like a brush against the shoulder will set off a sequence that makes sense only to them, carrying them from one emotional state to the next.”

lines.japanese: 『表面的にはまったく変化のない者もいます』
lines.english: “Some exhibit no outward change whatsoever.”

lines.japanese: 『働き、話し、過ごします』
lines.english: “They work, they talk, they pass their days.”

lines.japanese:
『しかしそれは、豊かな心によって保たれたもので
　はありません』
lines.english: “But what sustains those lives is not a rich inner life.”

lines.japanese:
『決められた日々を繰り返すことが、当人にとって
　もっとも強い倫理―――守るべき日々として刻み
　つけられていたためです』
lines.english: “Because living out the same prescribed routine, day after day, had been carved into them as their strongest ethical imperative—as the life they were bound to preserve.”

lines.japanese:
『人の行動をなぞってはいても、それは形式ばかり
　のもの。中身のともなわない再生行為』
lines.english: “Though they imitate the actions of a person, all that remains is form— playback without substance.”

lines.japanese: 『上澄みでしかないのです』
lines.english: “Nothing but the surface layer.”

lines.japanese: 刀を手に、斎に寄ってくる門倉。
lines.english: Sword in hand, Kadokura closed on Itsuki.

lines.japanese:
歩調は頼りなく、引きずるようだ。
　言葉を繰りながら、言葉を聞かない。
lines.english: His gait was uncertain, almost dragging. He kept speaking without listening.

lines.japanese: 「門倉は、終わらない」
lines.english: “Kadokura will not end.”

lines.japanese: 「名誉を守れば、道も残るからだ」
lines.english: “For if its honor is preserved, a path will remain.”

lines.japanese: 斎が口にする恨み言のひとつも、聞けない、
lines.english: Not a single word of Itsuki's resentment could reach him.

lines.japanese:
「貴宮にはしてやられたものだ。だがヤツもゆくゆ
　くは俺に下る」
lines.english: “Atemiya outmaneuvered me. But in time, he too will submit to me.”

lines.japanese:
正道の口はいつかどこかで告げた言葉を垂れ流し、
その肉体は乱れなく地を擦った。
lines.english: Seidou's mouth spilled words he had spoken somewhere, sometime, while his body skimmed the ground without the slightest break in form.

lines.japanese: もはや潰えた立身出世。
lines.english: His ambitions—already brought to ruin.

lines.japanese:
実現できる技と力をそのままに、醜く捩れて、心
潰した。
lines.english: The skill and strength that might have realized them remained intact, grotesquely twisted, while the mind itself lay crushed.

lines.japanese:
若く哀れな旗頭。
　かける情けがあるとすれば、それはただ―――
lines.english: A young and pitiful standard-bearer. If there was any mercy to grant him, it could only be—
“—Forgive me.”

lines.japanese: 斎の動作は、戦いのものとなった。
lines.english: Itsuki's body shifted into combat.

lines.japanese: 「知らない顔だが、使えそうな奴なら連れてこい」
lines.english: “I don't know that face. If he looks useful, bring him to me.”

lines.japanese: 正道の姿が消えた。
lines.english: Seidou vanished.

lines.japanese: 焦点を外されたのだ。
lines.english: Seidou had slipped out of his focus.

lines.japanese:
門倉流居合斬道、ならびに組討。いずれにも属す
る外しの極意、駆術だ。
lines.english: Both Kadokura-style iaijutsu and its grappling art contained a supreme method for slipping free of an opponent's focus: Kakejutsu.

lines.japanese:
だが斎の目を瞬時に眩ます精度は、あまりにも現
実離れしていた。
lines.english: But the precision with which he made Itsuki lose sight of him in an instant was too perfect to seem real.

lines.japanese: 無論、退く。
lines.english: Of course, Itsuki retreated.

lines.japanese: 真後ろに跳ねた。
lines.english: He sprang straight backward.

lines.japanese:
先ほどまで首が置かれていた場所を、白んだ何か
が通過した。
lines.english: Something pale passed through the space where his neck had been an instant earlier.

lines.japanese: さらにもう一度跳ねる。
lines.english: He sprang away once more.

lines.japanese:
連撃を避けてのものだが、正道は刀を振り切った
まま硬直していた。
lines.english: He had done so to evade a follow-up strike, but Seidou remained frozen at the end of his swing.

lines.japanese:
「年寄りどもは、俺を軽んじる。当主を軽んじ、利
　用しようとする蛇だ」
lines.english: “The old men scorn me. They scorn the head of their own house—snakes who mean to use me.”

lines.japanese:
聞き覚えのある言葉ではないか。
　かつて仲間を集め、語った内容と似ている。
lines.english: He had heard those words before. They resembled something Kadokura had said when gathering his comrades.

lines.japanese:
『ただ虚ろになってしまったのであれば、まだ良い
　のです』
lines.english: “If they merely became hollow, that would still be preferable.”

lines.japanese:
『稀に、内在する欲求が、その人間から全てのリミ
　ッターを外してしまうケースがあります』
lines.english: “In rare cases, a person's innate desire strips away every limiter.”

lines.japanese:
『その知識に根ざすあらゆる技術、運動、術理を発
　揮することも確認され……』
lines.english: “They have been observed exercising every technique, motion, and principle rooted in their knowledge…”

lines.japanese:
『これがある種の有害行動と結びついた時、極めて
　危険な存在である彼らを―――』
lines.english: “When this is joined to certain forms of harmful behavior, we call these exceptionally dangerous beings—”

lines.japanese: 『フリークス、と呼ぶのです』
lines.english: “Freaks.”

lines.japanese:
「年寄りは嘆く。先祖代々かためた地歩を、奴らは
　金と権力で全て奪い取っていく」
lines.english: “The old men lament. Every foothold our ancestors secured over generations, they strip away with money and power.”

lines.japanese: 「誇りのない力、理念のない仕方で」
lines.english: “Power without pride. Methods without principle.”

lines.japanese: 「だから門倉は堕ちた。それを取り戻す」
lines.english: “That is why Kadokura fell. I will take it back.”

lines.japanese: 門倉流居合斬道・雷火―――
lines.english: Kadokura-style iaijutsu: Lightning Fire—

lines.japanese:
本来は逆袈裟に斬り上げるものだが、水平に飛来
した……その意味に背筋も凍るほどの符号を見た。
lines.english: Normally, it was an upward diagonal cut. This one had come horizontally… and in that change Itsuki saw a meaning that chilled him to the bone.

lines.japanese:
首を狩るためのものなのだ。
　斎は静かに、構えを戻す。
　速度で言えば、雲燿にも届かんとする敵である。
lines.english: The technique was meant to take heads. Itsuki quietly resumed his guard. In sheer speed, the man approached even Un'you, the lightning-flash ideal.

lines.japanese: 門倉流居合斬道の希う、最上さえも越えている。
lines.english: He surpassed even the highest ideal of Kadokura-style iaijutsu.

lines.japanese:
言ってしまえば、真正面から斬り捨てるだけの技。
　しかしこの狭い通路では、全てと言えた。
lines.english: Put simply, it was a technique for cutting an enemy down head-on. But in this narrow passage, that was everything.

lines.japanese:
対する斎の組討は、逃げる敵を仕留め影から攻め
る凶の技。
lines.english: Itsuki's grappling art, by contrast, was a sinister discipline that struck from the shadows and finished fleeing foes.

lines.japanese: 真っ向から挑むための理合に欠ける。
lines.english: It had no principle for meeting an enemy head-on.

lines.japanese:
卑劣の剣。
　闇―――
lines.english: A coward's sword. Darkness—

lines.japanese: 瞬間、斎は視線の中心をわずかに正道からずらした。
lines.english: In that instant, Itsuki shifted the center of his gaze slightly away from Seidou.

lines.japanese:
基本さえ忘れていた。
　暗所で戦う心得として、対象を直視してはならない。
lines.english: He had forgotten even the fundamentals. When fighting in darkness, one must never look directly at the target.

lines.japanese:
桿体は中心窩にはほとんど存在しないかわりに、
周辺部に環状に埋め込まれている。
lines.english: Rod cells were almost absent from the fovea; instead, they formed a ring around the retinal periphery.

lines.japanese:
それは鍛錬によって、薄闇の中で人に光明をもたら
す仕掛けへと変じる。
lines.english: With training, that arrangement could be turned into a means of finding light in the half-dark.

lines.japanese:
凝視するより捉えやすくなる。
　またも正道が消えかけた。
lines.english: A figure was easier to catch that way than by staring straight at it. Once again, Seidou began to vanish.

lines.japanese: かろうじて、斎はとらえた。
lines.english: Itsuki caught him—barely.

lines.japanese:
打ち込まれる一刀をかいくぐる自信がない。
　ならば、
lines.english: He did not trust himself to slip beneath the incoming blade. In that case—

lines.japanese:
刀の両端を手に、水平線を描く太刀筋を鳥居打ち
に払う。
lines.english: Gripping his sword at both ends, he swept upward into the horizontal stroke with a torii block.

lines.japanese: 「月の訪れは―――」
lines.english: “When the moon arrives—”

lines.japanese: 言葉が途絶えた。
lines.english: The words broke off.

lines.japanese:
横薙ぎに来るとわかれば、視認の必要もない。
　そのまま踏み込む。
lines.english: Once he knew the strike would sweep horizontally, he did not need to see it. He stepped in without pause.

lines.japanese: 駆術である。
lines.english: Kakejutsu.

lines.japanese: 上弦、下弦、居待月―――
lines.english: First Quarter. Last Quarter. Seated-Waiting Moon—

lines.japanese:
人間の視野感覚は一定ではなく、極めて立体的に
感知されるものである。
lines.english: Human vision was not a uniform field; its sensitivity rose and fell across a sharply contoured landscape.

lines.japanese:
眼球中心部の感度は槍のように突出し、外側にず
れるごとに斜面となって鈍くなり、最後は絶壁に落
ち込むように０となる。
lines.english: At the eye's center, sensitivity rose to a spearpoint. Toward the edges, it dulled along a slope, then dropped like a cliff to zero.

lines.japanese:
明るさ、動き、静物、見通す目の機能は全能では
なく、さまざまな欠損を持っている。
lines.english: The eye was far from infallible in its perception of brightness, motion, still objects, and depth; it was riddled with gaps.

lines.japanese:
ありとあらゆる人体の機能、その隙間を突くのが
駆術の深奥。
lines.english: The innermost principle of Kakejutsu was to exploit every gap in every function of the human body.

lines.japanese: 夕月、残月、寝待月―――
lines.english: Evening Moon. Lingering Moon. Bed-Waiting Moon—

lines.japanese:
技量に長けた武者を、闇に忍び殺害するための技
術であった、
lines.english: It was an art devised to slip through darkness and kill a warrior of consummate skill.

lines.japanese:
卑劣である。
　悪辣である。
lines.english: Cowardly. Vicious.

lines.japanese: 門倉流居合斬道が決して持ち得ない体術なのである。
lines.english: A physical art Kadokura-style iaijutsu could never possess.

lines.japanese: 正道が太刀行く。見当違いの方角に跳ねたそれは、
lines.english: Seidou's sword moved. It sprang in entirely the wrong direction—

lines.japanese: ―――切り返しのもつれもなく、瞬時に落ちてきた。
lines.english: —then dropped in an instant, its reversal perfectly smooth.

lines.japanese: 正確に斎の頭部を狙って。
lines.english: Straight at Itsuki's head.

lines.japanese:
大上段の一刀を頭上で受け、膝を抜いた。
　身を捻って懐に飛び込み、左手で正道の構えその
ものを脇に抱えこみ、柄手を握る。
lines.english: He caught the downward stroke over his head and let his knees buckle. Twisting, he drove inside Seidou's reach, trapping his entire guard under his left arm and seizing the hand at the hilt.

lines.japanese: 封殺。
lines.english: The weapon was locked down.

lines.japanese: 斎の右、抜き身の刃が正道の喉に伸びた。
lines.english: On Itsuki's right, his bare blade reached for Seidou's throat.

lines.japanese:
この技をどう防ぐと言うのか。受けられたら封じ
られ、首を突かれておしまいだ。
lines.english: How could anyone defend against this technique? Once the strike was caught, the weapon was pinned and the throat pierced. The end.

lines.japanese:
もはや門倉正道の死は、夜明けの訪れより明らか
に思えた。
lines.english: Seidou Kadokura's death now seemed more certain than the coming dawn.

lines.japanese: 錯覚だ。
lines.english: An illusion.

lines.japanese:
正道が身を捻る。繊細にして強力。捻りつつしゃ
がめば、あらゆる戒めから解放された正道の刀が、
この次には斎の喉を突く構え。
lines.english: Seidou twisted—delicately, powerfully. As he turned and crouched, his sword slipped free of every restraint and came into position to thrust through Itsuki's throat.

lines.japanese:
斎は消えた。
　正道が消えた。
lines.english: Itsuki vanished. Seidou vanished.

lines.japanese:
二人の軌跡は互いの死角を目指して隠れあい、桿
体を欺き気配を惑わし際限なく舞い続けた。
lines.english: Their paths sought each other's blind spots. They vanished in turn, deceiving the eye's rod cells, confounding every sense of presence, and dancing without end.

lines.japanese:
時折噛み合う刃の響きが、足音さえも殺した両者
の実存の証として、甲高い戦の合奏を奏であげる。
lines.english: Every so often, blades rang together. The sound proved that they existed even after silencing their footsteps, a shrill concerto of war.

lines.japanese:
ほとんど意識を失いつつある葉子は、ぼんやりと
した視野に、かすかに閃く火花の連なりだけを見た。
lines.english: Nearly unconscious, Youko saw only a faint chain of sparks flickering within her blurred vision.
“…Brother.”

lines.japanese:
ほう、と息を吐いて喪心する。
　殺生の音色を子守歌に―――
lines.english: She let out a soft breath and lost consciousness. The music of slaughter her lullaby—

lines.japanese: 正道の動きに思考はない。
lines.english: There was no thought in Seidou's movements.

lines.japanese:
拡大された身体感覚は、あらゆる奥義を再現して
のける。
lines.english: His expanded bodily awareness reproduced every secret technique to perfection.

lines.japanese: あらゆる迷いと未熟を排して。
lines.english: All hesitation and immaturity stripped away.

lines.japanese:
斎もまた、頭を白熱させ身体に叩き込んだ術理の
みに身を委ねはじめている。
lines.english: Itsuki, too, began to surrender wholly to the principles beaten into his body, his mind burning white.

lines.japanese: くみ
lines.english: favored

lines.japanese:
状況は芳しくない。
　隘路での斬り合いは正道の王道剣に与し、駆術に
おいては斎が一馬身先を行く。
lines.english: The situation was not favorable. A sword fight in this narrow passage favored Seidou's orthodox blade, while Itsuki remained one length ahead in Kakejutsu.

lines.japanese:
互角に思えて、しかし極限まで拡大された門倉の
技は、もはや戦術の域を超えている。
lines.english: They seemed evenly matched. Yet Kadokura's techniques, expanded to their absolute limit, had already transcended tactics.

lines.japanese:
一瞬一瞬が、斎にとっては死路の歩み。
　いつ槍の飛び出すともわからない床を、延々と歩
み続ける心境に―――しかし斎の心に恐怖はない。
lines.english: Each passing instant carried Itsuki another step down the road to death. It was like walking forever across a floor where a spear might spring up at any moment—and yet Itsuki felt no fear.

lines.japanese: 「斎は犬だ―――」
lines.english: “Itsuki is a dog—”

lines.japanese: いつ誰に話した言葉か。
lines.english: When had he said those words, and to whom?

lines.japanese: 「―――劣るが、役に立つ」
lines.english: “—inferior, but useful.”

lines.japanese: 言葉が胸をえぐる。
lines.english: The words gouged into his heart.

lines.japanese:
正道の人格は知っていた。
　斎が純真過ぎただけだ。
lines.english: He had known what kind of man Seidou was. He himself had simply been too innocent.

lines.japanese:
理解しておきながら、なお縋らねばならない弱さ
とともに、日々を重ねた。
lines.english: He had gone on day after day, knowing the truth yet too weak to let go.

lines.japanese: そして強くなった。
lines.english: And he had grown strong.

lines.japanese:
この私闘は門倉正道という徒花への最後の忠信で
あり、幼かった頃の弱さを濯ぐ塚本斎の巣立ちの祝い。
lines.english: This private duel was his final act of loyalty to the fruitless blossom that was Seidou Kadokura— the coming-of-age rite by which Itsuki Tsukamoto washed away his childhood weakness.

lines.japanese:
今という時代でなければ、決して許されなかった
はずである。
lines.english: In any age but this one, it could never have been permitted.

lines.japanese: 鋭く息を吐く。
lines.english: He breathed out sharply.

lines.japanese:
身隠しの道理は理性の外に飛んでいた。
　激情を駆り立てつつも、四肢の駆動とは切り離す。
lines.english: The logic of concealment had passed beyond reason. He drove his passion higher but severed it from the motion of his limbs.

lines.japanese:
究極の上澄みと極限の感情、その激突が、暗路に
十字を斬り結ぶ。
lines.english: The ultimate surface layer clashed with emotion pushed to its limit, and their steel carved a cross through the dark passage.

lines.japanese:
かすかな手応えに、刃の損傷を実感した。
　対し、正道の得物はさすが超絶の名刀、一方的に
切り口をつけられたのは斎の方だ。
lines.english: From the faint resistance, he knew his blade had been damaged. Seidou's weapon, by contrast, was a transcendent masterpiece; only Itsuki's blade had come away scarred.

lines.japanese:
腕の差もあったろう。
　刃こぼれも、微細なものならどうということはない。
lines.english: The gap in skill may have played a part as well. A minute nick in the edge was nothing to worry about.

lines.japanese:
しかし刀の強度というものを考えたとき、斬り結
ぶ行為そのものは決して誉められるべきものでもない。
lines.english: But given the limits of a sword's strength, crossing blades was never wise.

lines.japanese:
代用刀はない。
　ただ一刀。それのみである。
lines.english: There was no replacement. One sword. That was all.

lines.japanese: 体術での決着など考えられない。
lines.english: Settling this through unarmed combat was unthinkable.

lines.japanese: 斎か、正道か。
lines.english: Itsuki, or Seidou.

lines.japanese:
いずれにしても死線を引く筆は、相互に手にした
日本古来の牙だけである。
lines.english: Whichever man it was, the only pen that could draw the line of death was the ancient Japanese fang each held in his hand.

lines.japanese:
またも正道の姿がかき消える。
　見失っても、移動は予測できる。同じ場所から伸
びた支流の如き、二つの流派だ。
lines.english: Once more, Seidou's figure vanished. Even if Itsuki lost sight of him, he could predict the movement. Their two schools were tributaries of the same source.

lines.japanese:
致命傷を受けるより早く、予想した相手の位置、
死角に身を滑りこませる。
lines.english: Before he could suffer a mortal wound, he slipped into his opponent’s blind spot, anticipating where the man would be.

lines.japanese: その繰り返し。
lines.english: Again and again.

lines.japanese: 互いの行動を何手先までも読む。
lines.english: Each read the other's actions many moves ahead.

lines.japanese:
十手、二十手、三十手先の自分がどこに身を置く
のか、克明に感じ取る。
lines.english: He could feel with perfect clarity where his body would be ten, twenty, thirty moves ahead.

lines.japanese: この極めて幾何学的闘争は、互角に見えて斎が劣勢。
lines.english: This supremely geometric struggle seemed even, but Itsuki was losing.

lines.japanese:
先ほどから、正道の動きは一糸乱れず、敵を幾度
となく死地に送りかけている。
lines.english: Seidou's movements had not faltered once; time and again, he had brought Itsuki to the brink of death.

lines.japanese: 斎は防戦で精一杯だ。
lines.english: Itsuki could do no more than defend.

lines.japanese:
ただ食い下がり、死中の生を数えられないほどに
掴み、死出の碁盤を埋めていく。
lines.english: He did nothing but hang on, snatching life from death again and again as he filled death's Go board one point at a time.

lines.japanese: 闘争開始からすでに無限に近い時間が過ぎていた。
lines.english: An eternity seemed to have passed since the struggle began.

lines.japanese: 正道の姿が―――何度目のことだろう―――消えた。
lines.english: Seidou's figure—how many times did this make?—vanished.

lines.japanese: が、完全には消えない。
lines.english: But not completely.

lines.japanese:
片手だけを不自然に宙に残していた。
　広げた五指は、紅葉の形。
　見てしまった。
lines.english: One hand remained, suspended unnaturally in the air. Five spread fingers made the shape of a maple leaf. Itsuki looked despite himself.

lines.japanese: ミスディレクション―――
lines.english: Misdirection—

lines.japanese: 誤認させられた。
lines.english: He had been misdirected.

lines.japanese:
手を見てはいけなかった。
　見ずに、ただ予測のままに行動すべきだったのだ。
lines.english: He should not have looked at the hand. He should have acted on prediction alone, without looking.

lines.japanese:
戸惑いが遅らせた行動は、コンマの世界の出来事
だが……正道には充分に過ぎる。
lines.english: The instant of confusion delayed him only a fraction of a second …but for Seidou, that was more than enough.

lines.japanese:
猛然と斜め後方に跳ねた斎の、頬を名刀の切先が
かすめた。
lines.english: The tip of the masterwork blade grazed Itsuki's cheek as he hurled himself diagonally backward.

lines.japanese:
真後ろへの回避は読まれていた。
　万全を期しての斜め後方への身かわしが、斎に命
を拾わせた。
lines.english: Seidou had anticipated an evasion straight backward. Itsuki's diagonal retreat—chosen to leave nothing to chance—was what saved his life.

lines.japanese: が、仕切直し。
lines.english: But they were back at the start.

lines.japanese:
時間の流れが遅くなる。いや、戻った。
　ぬるい空気にも似た虚脱が、斎をとらえて離さない。
lines.english: Time slowed. No—it rewound. A languor like lukewarm air seized Itsuki and would not let go.

lines.japanese: また一から組み直し、である。
lines.english: He would have to build the whole exchange again from the first move.

lines.japanese:
勝てないかもしれない。
　そんな予感も、よぎった。
lines.english: Perhaps he could not win. For a moment, the thought crossed his mind.

lines.japanese:
「戦国に生まれれば良かったと、思ったことはない
　か？」
lines.english: “Have you ever wished you'd been born in the Warring States period?”

lines.japanese:
つい応じたくなる。
　上澄み相手に、と思いつつも、斎は首を横に振る。
lines.english: The words nearly drew a reply from him. Though he knew he faced only the surface layer, Itsuki shook his head.

lines.japanese: 正道の言葉は紛い物。
lines.english: Seidou's words were counterfeit.

lines.japanese:
言葉同士の意味も、考えられてはいない。
　無作為に抽出されてくるだけのものだ。
lines.english: No thread of meaning connected one phrase to the next. They were simply selected at random.

lines.japanese:
だから再生と呼ばれる。
　拡大症に陥った者の、特徴的な言動の一つである。
lines.english: That was why it was called playback. It was one of the characteristic behaviors of those afflicted with Ego Expansion disorder.

lines.japanese: 「俺はある」
lines.english: “I have.”

lines.japanese: 繋がるはずのない会話が、なぜか意味を持った。
lines.english: Somehow, a conversation whose parts should never have connected took on meaning.

lines.japanese: 「未来には、身も凍るような絶望が欲しかった」
lines.english: “I wanted the future to hold despair enough to freeze me to the bone.”

lines.japanese: 「いっそ国が乱れればと、思いもした」
lines.english: “I even wished the country would descend into chaos.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえは言った。この願いは実現すると」
lines.english: “You told me that wish would come true.”

lines.japanese: 「だから俺は……おまえに下った」
lines.english: “And so I… submitted to you.”

lines.japanese: 斎の瞳が、驚愕に見開かれる。
lines.english: Itsuki's eyes went wide.

lines.japanese:
誰かに語った内容。
　それは誇り高い門倉正道が、過去、何者かに魂を
売り渡したことを示していた。
lines.english: Words once spoken to someone. They showed that proud Seidou Kadokura had once sold his soul to some unknown figure.

lines.japanese:
「もはや全ては望むべくもない。俺を走狗として使
　えばいい」
lines.english: “There is no hope of gaining it all now. Use me as your hound if you wish.”

lines.japanese: 「そのかわり、俺を戦国に連れて行け―――」
lines.english: “In return, take me to the Warring States—”

lines.japanese:
自由を得るため、闘争を現実のものとするため、
正道は加担した。
lines.english: To win freedom, to make battle a reality, Seidou had become an accomplice.

lines.japanese: そして外界へと躍り出たのだ。
lines.english: And then he had leapt into the outside world.

lines.japanese:
失われた炎が、深い部分に灯された。
　怒りのような。それでいて憐憫のような。
lines.english: A long-lost flame kindled deep inside him. It was something like anger. Yet also something like pity.

lines.japanese: 落胆。殺意。失望。憎悪。
lines.english: Disappointment. Murderous intent. Disillusionment. Hatred.

lines.japanese: わからない。
lines.english: He did not know.

lines.japanese:
わからないがしかし、全身に漲るものは疑う余地
もなく闘志である。
lines.english: He did not know. But whatever now coursed through his entire body was, beyond all doubt, the will to fight.

lines.japanese:
再びの対峙。
　刀筋を通すため、そっと柄を握り込み、引いた。
lines.english: Again they faced each other. To give his blade a clear path, Itsuki closed his hand gently around the hilt and drew it back.

lines.japanese: この戦い、闇を制した側が勝つだろう。
lines.english: The one who mastered the darkness would win this battle.

lines.japanese: 即ち―――
lines.english: Which meant—

lines.japanese:
振り返れば、やはりどこかに、正道との決闘を経
て陽の下に立つという願望があったのかも知れない。
lines.english: Looking back, perhaps some part of him had truly wanted to duel Seidou and step afterward into the light of day.

lines.japanese:
しかし今、冷静になって考えれば、やはり斎は縁
の下。
lines.english: But viewed calmly now, Itsuki belonged beneath the floorboards.

lines.japanese:
日陰を動くが自然。
　剣術で勝利しようとする思いもまた然り。
lines.english: His natural place was in the shadows. Even his wish to win by the sword belonged there.

lines.japanese:
あのまま殺意を結び合っていたら、首が飛ぶのは
何手先だったろうか？
lines.english: Had they gone on with their murderous intent locked together, how many moves before his head flew?

lines.japanese: 二十一手か、二十二手か。
lines.english: Twenty-one? Twenty-two?

lines.japanese:
生き残るためには、斎の持つ全ての闇を用いるし
かない。
lines.english: To survive, Itsuki had no choice but to use all the darkness within him.

lines.japanese:
日だまりにとどまってはならない。
　正道の下ではなくとも、走狗には違いない。
lines.english: He must not linger in the warmth of the sun. He might no longer serve under Seidou, but a hound was a hound.

lines.japanese: もとより斎は、正道に対し私怨があるわけではない。
lines.english: Itsuki had never borne Seidou any personal grudge.

lines.japanese:
かつての主だ。
　主に腐るも腐らぬもない。
lines.english: He was Itsuki's former master. A master remained a master, rotten or not.

lines.japanese:
世の良識が否定しようとも、塚本斎とはそういう
人間なのだった。
lines.english: Whatever the dictates of decent society, that was simply the kind of man Itsuki Tsukamoto was.

lines.japanese: そこは変わらない。
lines.english: That had not changed.

lines.japanese:
不意の日だまりで過ごした数年間は、ひとときの
こと。
lines.english: The few years he had spent in an unexpected patch of sunlight had been only an interlude.

lines.japanese:
思い出は尊く、形を変えずに残り続ける。
　だが本当の覚悟は、今まで持てなかったのだろう。
lines.english: The memories were sacred, and would remain forever unchanged. But perhaps he had never found true resolve until now.

lines.japanese:
中途半端な位置にいたものだ、と斎は口元に微笑
を張りつかせた。
lines.english: He had spent all this time caught in between, Itsuki thought, a smile fixed to his lips.

lines.japanese: 今こそ、最後の覚悟を決めた。
lines.english: Now, at last, he steeled himself.

lines.japanese: 「……言っていた」
lines.english: “…He said…”

lines.japanese:
決然と相手……かつての主を見据える。
　そして迷うことなく、今の主の名を口にした。
lines.english: Resolute, he stared down his opponent—his former master. Then, without hesitation, he spoke the name of the master he served now.

lines.japanese: 「忍様は、言っていた」
lines.english: “Master Shinobu said…”

lines.japanese:
救われたと確信した日以来のこと。
　この主代わりを知る者は、忍と葉子だけである。
lines.english: It had been true ever since the day Itsuki knew he had been saved. Only Shinobu and Youko knew whom he had chosen to serve in his old master's stead.

lines.japanese: 「輝かしい希望など、過去にしかないと」
lines.english: “That brilliant hope existed only in the past.”

lines.japanese:
「未来には苦しみしかなかった、と。
　まるで見てきたように」
lines.english: “That the future held nothing but suffering. He spoke as though he had seen it himself.”

lines.japanese: 「それでも、生きねばならん―――人は」
lines.english: “And even so, a man must live—”

lines.japanese:
腰の裏にて剣先を平に寝かせ、奇しくも薙ぎ払う
形は正道のそれと酷似する。
lines.english: He laid the point of his sword flat behind his waist. Curiously, the resulting sweeping posture closely resembled Seidou's.

lines.japanese:
「何者かの犬にならずとも、あなたの宿願は果たさ
　れただろう」
lines.english: “You could have fulfilled your heart's desire without becoming anyone's dog.”

lines.japanese:
「たとえ不利であろうとも、一からの出直しになろ
　うとも、純粋な思いがあるのなら、誰に頼ること
　もなく切り開くべきだった」
lines.english: “However badly the odds were stacked against you, even if it meant starting over from nothing, if your conviction was pure, you should have carved out a path by your own hand.”

lines.japanese: 「しかしあなたは古い時代の体現者たろうとした」
lines.english: “But you sought to become the embodiment of an old age.”

lines.japanese: 「望んで挑み、そして敗れ、ついには腐れた」
lines.english: “You chose to fight. You lost. And in the end, you rotted.”

lines.japanese:
「哀しいかなそれが現実であり、苦しみしかない未
　来の一端だった」
lines.english: “Sad though it is, that was reality—one fragment of a future that held nothing but suffering.”

lines.japanese:
「あなたは見落とした。戦国はあなただけに優しく
　はなかった。身も凍るような絶望というのは、そ
　ういうことも含むものだからだ」
lines.english: “You failed to see one thing. The Warring States would have shown you no special kindness. That, too, is what it means for despair to freeze a man to the bone.”

lines.japanese: 「お悔やみ申し上げる」
lines.english: “You have my condolences.”

lines.japanese: 「……そして俺は、門倉の末期を看取る者になろう」
lines.english: “…And I shall be the one to see Kadokura through its final moments.”

lines.japanese:
「塚本斎の名において、覇者の血没する、墓所まで
　の供として」
lines.english: “In the name of Itsuki Tsukamoto, I shall accompany the victor's blood to the grave where it sinks from sight.”

lines.japanese:
今にも斬りかかる構えを見せるが、微塵の殺意も
発さない。
lines.english: His stance was ready to strike at any moment, yet not the slightest trace of murderous intent escaped him.

lines.japanese:
もとより無心の正道も同様で、三間の間合いを挟
み、大地に根を張り微動だにしない。
lines.english: Seidou, mindless from the outset, was no different. Some 5.5 meters away, he stood rooted to the earth without the faintest movement.

lines.japanese: 時が過ぎた。
lines.english: Time passed.

lines.japanese:
先刻の熱気は消散し、かわりに場を支配したのは
水も凍るような緊張だ。
lines.english: The earlier heat dissipated, replaced by a tension cold enough to freeze water.

lines.japanese:
動の対に置かれた静の構図中、両者の殺法は次第
に力をたくわえ、鋭さをいやます。
lines.english: In this stillness, set against motion, their killing arts slowly gathered strength and sharpened.

lines.japanese: ともに実戦というものを経験したことはないはずだ。
lines.english: Neither man should ever have experienced real combat.

lines.japanese:
が、両名の技は雑念のない、抽出された純一をも
っておのおのの手に馴染む。
lines.english: Yet each man's art settled into his hands in a pure, distilled form, free of every stray thought.

lines.japanese: 相手を殺害する機能だけを研ぎ上げていく。
lines.english: Honing nothing but the power to kill the other.

lines.japanese:
刹那に、斎が思ったことは複雑を極める。
　言葉にした通りの憐憫もあった。
lines.english: In that instant, Itsuki's thoughts were tangled beyond measure. He felt the pity he had put into words.

lines.japanese:
自分のことは意に介さないが、葉子のことで、憎
悪の片鱗もあったかも知れない。
lines.english: He cared nothing for what had been done to him. But when he thought of Youko, perhaps there was some shard of hatred as well.

lines.japanese:
門倉正道は復興に憑かれていた。
　忍は未来を怖じていた。
lines.english: Seidou Kadokura had been possessed by the dream of restoration. Shinobu had feared the future.

lines.japanese:
それぞれの未来展望は相反しており、事実忍の恐
怖は実現し門倉の夢をも引き裂いた。
lines.english: Their visions of the future stood opposed—and Shinobu's fear had in fact come to pass, tearing Kadokura's dream apart in the process.

lines.japanese: 全て最初から決まっていたことのように思えた。
lines.english: It seemed as though everything had been decided from the beginning.

lines.japanese:
救いのない穴ぐらだ。
　出ることができない。
lines.english: A pit without salvation. There was no way out.

lines.japanese:
薄暗い闇の底に沈み、人の心は病んでいく。
　正道が心を壊したこと、偶然ではない。
　必然であった。
lines.english: At the bottom of that dim darkness, the human heart sickened. Seidou's mind had not broken by chance. It had been inevitable.

lines.japanese:
門倉の繁栄など、最初からどこにも用意されてい
なかった。
lines.english: There had never been a prosperous future waiting for Kadokura.

lines.japanese: 矛盾に満ちた思惑は、決して正鵠には届かない。
lines.english: Plans riddled with contradiction could never hit their mark.

lines.japanese: 自らの歪曲にさえ気付けないのが盲信。
lines.english: Blind faith was the inability to see even the distortions in oneself.

lines.japanese:
射抜けるはずもなく結果、斎と正道の対立もあら
かじめ予定されていたことのように、今ここに置か
れている。
lines.english: Nothing so blind could ever strike true. And so the clash between Itsuki and Seidou lay before them now as though it, too, had been ordained from the start.

lines.japanese: この滑稽さは何だ？
lines.english: What kind of farce was this?

lines.japanese:
人を道具立てた門倉郎党への因果応報と考えるに
しても、あまりにも酷な現実ではないか。
lines.english: Even if this was just punishment for the Kadokura retainers, who had made tools of others, wasn't reality still far too cruel?

lines.japanese:
迷いがわずかに刀身に伝わりかけ、呼気にまぎれ
て邪念を外に吐き出した。
lines.english: A trace of doubt nearly traveled into his blade. He breathed it out with every other stray thought.

lines.japanese: 門倉正道は最後の宗家となるだろう。
lines.english: Seidou Kadokura would be the last head of the Kadokura school.

lines.japanese:
武の終焉を、見送る役目を買って出た。
　葬送はつつがなく行われるべきだ。
lines.english: Itsuki had volunteered to see the martial tradition to its end. Its funeral must proceed without incident.

lines.japanese:
そうして瞬間が丹念に重ねられ、やがて秒に届き
分に達するという頃、
lines.english: One painstaking instant was laid upon another, until the seconds accumulated and nearly made a minute.

lines.japanese: 斎と正道との間は、３メートルほどに縮まっていた。
lines.english: The distance between Itsuki and Seidou had narrowed to some three meters.

lines.japanese:
足が大地を握りしめたまま、足指だけで這いずる
術がそれを成した。
lines.english: The gap had closed by inches as they crept on their toes, their feet still gripping the earth.

lines.japanese:
３メートル。
　一足飛びにも及ばない距離だ。
lines.english: Three meters. Not even a single bound.

lines.japanese:
前触れなく、ふたりの足が地を離れた。
　この上なく静かに、慎ましく。
lines.english: Without warning, both men's feet left the ground. Perfectly silent. Almost modest.

lines.japanese:
澄んだ刀身が柔らかく合わせられ、何拍も遅れて
甲高い響きが地下を埋める。
lines.english: The bright blades touched softly; several beats later, a high ring filled the underground passage.

lines.japanese: 刃こぼれに、合わせられた。
lines.english: The stroke met the nick in Itsuki's edge.

lines.japanese: 斎の刀が、破片もなく砕ける。
lines.english: Itsuki's sword shattered cleanly, without scattering a single fragment.

lines.japanese:
太刀折りの妙技はむろん正道の目当てによるもの
だが、このときすでに斎の体は、その視界から完全
に消失していた。
lines.english: The masterful sword-breaking stroke had been Seidou's aim, of course, but by then Itsuki's body had vanished entirely from his field of vision.

lines.japanese:
へし折れた刀身の下方、柄を握るはずの諸手が失
せている。
lines.english: Below the snapped blade, the two hands that should have held the hilt were gone.

lines.japanese:
もし正道に理性があったなら、瞳術を極めた斎の
凶技に戦慄せずにはいられなかっただろう。
lines.english: Had Seidou possessed reason, he would have shuddered at Itsuki's sinister art, perfected through mastery of the eye.

lines.japanese: 返す刃で断ち切るはずの、首を失い正道は惑った。
lines.english: Seidou faltered: the neck his returning stroke should have severed was gone.

lines.japanese:
斜め前方に漂う顔がまるで見えていないかのよう
に、首を巡らせた。
lines.english: He turned his head as though unable to see the face hovering at an angle before him.

lines.japanese:
マリオット盲点に沈めた身を、正道は視認するこ
とはできなかったのだ。
lines.english: Seidou could not see the body submerged in Mariotte's blind spot.

lines.japanese: 駆術・新月―――
lines.english: Kakejutsu: New Moon—

lines.japanese: 上にして凶。
lines.english: Supreme—and wicked.

lines.japanese:
視細胞の欠損とともに喉笛を貫く、卑劣極まりな
い暗殺の秘奥。
lines.english: The vilest secret of assassination: a thrust through the throat from within a gap in the eye's photoreceptor cells.

lines.japanese:
いつかどこかの言葉を終えるより早く、襟足に手
刀は優しく置かれた。
lines.english: Before he could finish the words he had once spoken somewhere, sometime, a knife-hand came gently to rest against the nape of his neck.

lines.japanese: 「粛滅、御免」
lines.english: “For this purge—forgive me.”

lines.japanese: 驚くほど滑らかに、首を落とした。
lines.english: With astonishing smoothness, he took off the head.

lines.japanese: 斎は正道の膝の裏を蹴る。
lines.english: Itsuki kicked the backs of Seidou's knees.

lines.japanese:
力を抜いたように身が沈み、正座の形を模し……
その膝の上に、感情を失った頭部が転がり落ちた。
lines.english: The body sank as if all strength had gone, folding into a formal kneel …and the head, emptied of emotion, rolled into its lap.

lines.japanese:
順番は違えども、恐らく正道が被害者に対して同
様の行いをしたはずだった。
lines.english: Though in a different order, Seidou had presumably done the same to his victims.

lines.japanese:
蹴り落とし、膝を突かせて斬り殺す。
　名誉ある死の形を、彼らの上にくれてやるために。
lines.english: He had kicked them off their feet, forced them to their knees, and struck them dead— granting them the form of an honorable death.

lines.japanese:
「……貴宮流抜刀術にて、介錯、確かに務めさせて
　いただいた」
lines.english: “…With the Atemiya school of battoujutsu, I have duly carried out the duty of second.”

lines.japanese: 身を引きずり、葉子の脇にしゃがみこんだ。
lines.english: He dragged himself over and crouched beside Youko.

lines.japanese: 「……葉子、葉子？」
lines.english: “…Youko? Youko?”

lines.japanese: 「ん……兄、さん？」
lines.english: “Mm… Brother?”

lines.japanese: 少女がうっすら目を開ける。
lines.english: The girl's eyes opened a sliver.

lines.japanese:
古来、切腹は武士の名誉を重んじた自害の方法と
して採用されてきた。
lines.english: Since ancient times, seppuku had been used as a form of suicide that preserved a warrior's honor.

lines.japanese:
苦痛に満ち、死に至るまで長く苦しむ方法であり、
その果敢な様子が武士にふさわしいとされ、戦場
ばかりか後の刑罰にまで広く採用された。
lines.english: It was agonizing, prolonging one's suffering until death. The courage it displayed was considered worthy of a warrior, and the practice spread from the battlefield to later forms of punishment.

lines.japanese:
切腹は実質介錯による斬首ではあったが、体面の
上では自ら罪に服する名誉ある死に様とされた。
lines.english: In practice, seppuku amounted to being beheaded by a second. In outward form, however, it was held to be an honorable death—a man submitting himself to judgment.

lines.japanese: 少女は薄く笑う。
lines.english: The girl smiled faintly.
“…Did you win?”

lines.japanese: 「無事に、終えた」
lines.english: “It is done. Without mishap.”

lines.japanese: 「そう」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese:
悲壮な面相に、感じるものがあったのか、葉子も
茶化すことはなかった。
lines.english: Perhaps she read something in his grim expression. Whatever the reason, Youko did not tease him.

lines.japanese: 正道の亡骸を見て、
lines.english: She looked at Seidou's remains—

lines.japanese: 「やっと、終わったね」
lines.english: “It's finally over.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「どうする？」
lines.english: “What will you do?”

lines.japanese: 「変わらない」
lines.english: “Nothing changes.”
“…I see.”

lines.japanese:
いつしか穏やかな斎の顔と、かすかに傾く葉子の
面差し。天秤のように入れ替わった。
lines.english: Before long, Itsuki's face had grown serene while Youko's had begun to fall. Like the pans of a balance, they had traded places.

lines.japanese:
時には、切腹を果たせないこともあるだろう。
　両腕を失った時、心乱した時、意識を失った時。
lines.english: There were times when a man could not carry out seppuku: when he had lost both arms, lost his composure, or lost consciousness.

lines.japanese:
身内による汚名返上の術となれば、ただ一つしか
あり得ない。
lines.english: If his family wished to erase that disgrace, there was only one way.

lines.japanese:
正道は知っていたはずだ。
　凶の継承者が、時に背く身内を粛清する役目を負
っていたことを。
lines.english: Seidou must have known that the heir to the sinister art was sometimes charged with purging a kinsman who had strayed.

lines.japanese: 何となれば、こうなるも必定であったのだ。
lines.english: If the need arose, this outcome had been inevitable.

lines.japanese:
わざわざ卑しい斎をそばに置いたのは、いざとい
う時、自らの恥を濯ぐためでもあったのだ、と―――
そう信じたかった。
lines.english: Perhaps Seidou had kept a lowly man like Itsuki at his side precisely so that, when the hour came, Itsuki might wash away his shame— or so Itsuki wanted to believe.

lines.japanese: これにて斎は、お役御免と相成る。
lines.english: With that, Itsuki's duty was done.

lines.japanese:
地下道には電話が備え付けられていた。
　幸い繋がったので、それで千鳥に連絡を取った。
lines.english: A telephone had been installed in the underground passage. Fortunately, it still worked, and he used it to contact Chidori.

lines.japanese: 「ずっと大人しかったんだけど……ね」
lines.english: “He'd been so quiet the whole time…”

lines.japanese:
「感染してから発症まで、時間がかかることがある
　んだ」
lines.english: “There can be a delay between infection and the onset of symptoms.”

lines.japanese: 「……突然だった」
lines.english: “…It was so sudden.”

lines.japanese: 「家にいたのか？」
lines.english: “Were you at home?”

lines.japanese: 「最近は、工場と家をいったりきたり」
lines.english: “Lately, I've just been going back and forth between the factory and home.”

lines.japanese:
「突然、暴れ出して、出て行って……
　捜したみたいだけど見つからない……
　とここまではメールで説明した通りで」
lines.english: “All of a sudden, he went wild and left… They searched, but couldn't find him… Up to that point, it was just as I explained in my message.”

lines.japanese:
「突然戻ってきて、わけのわからないことを口にし
　て……その場にいたみんなを突然」
lines.english: “Then he suddenly came back, started saying things that made no sense …and everyone who was there, he just—”

lines.japanese: 葉子の隣に座り込む。
lines.english: Itsuki sat down beside Youko.

lines.japanese: 「よく逃げられたな、おまえの腕で」
lines.english: “I'm surprised you got away, given your fighting skills.”

lines.japanese: 「……存在感薄いから」
lines.english: “…I'm easy to overlook.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、納得だ」
lines.english: “Ah. That explains it.”

lines.japanese: 「……さすがに痛い」
lines.english: “…Okay, this really hurts.”

lines.japanese: 「見た感じ、血は止まってる。死なないだろう」
lines.english: “From the look of it, the bleeding’s stopped. You probably won’t die.”

lines.japanese: 「死んでたまりますか……」
lines.english: “Like hell I'm dying…”

lines.japanese: 「子供も産んでないのに」
lines.english: “Not when I haven't even had a child yet.”

lines.japanese: 「子供生むと、報償金出るぞ」
lines.english: “They give you a bonus for having one.”

lines.japanese: 「狙ってる」
lines.english: “That's what I'm after.”

lines.japanese: フ、と斎は不敵に口元を吊り上げた。
lines.english: Itsuki's lips curled into a daring grin.

lines.japanese: 「最後の技……あれなに？」
lines.english: “That last move… what was it?”

lines.japanese: 「見てたのか？」
lines.english: “You saw it?”

lines.japanese: 「ちょっとだけ、ぼんやりと」
lines.english: “Only a little. It was all a blur.”

lines.japanese: 「……貴宮流抜刀術だ」
lines.english: “…The Atemiya school of battoujutsu.”

lines.japanese: 「クビキリブレードだ」
lines.english: “The Neck-Cutter Blade.”

lines.japanese: 「……なぜ知っている」
lines.english: “…How do you know that?”

lines.japanese: 「本人から聞いたから」
lines.english: “He told me himself.”

lines.japanese:
「ご主人様からもらった技の名前を勝手に変えると
　いう―――」
lines.english: “So you went and changed the name of a technique your master gave you —”

lines.japanese: 「知っていて聞いたのか」
lines.english: “You asked when you already knew?”

lines.japanese: 「嘘つくだろうなと思って」
lines.english: “I thought you'd lie.”

lines.japanese: 「不忠な部下発見」
lines.english: “Disloyal subordinate spotted.”

lines.japanese: 「……違う、そういうことではなく……」
lines.english: “…No, that's not…”

lines.japanese: 「格好悪かったので、名前変えた」
lines.english: “You changed it because it sounded lame.”

lines.japanese: 「忍さんに言いつけよう」
lines.english: “I'll tell Shinobu.”
“What…?”

lines.japanese: 「言いつけよう」
lines.english: “I'll tell him.”

lines.japanese:
そうして瞬間が丹念に重ねられ、やがて秒に届き
分に達するという頃、
lines.english: One painstaking instant was laid upon another, until the seconds accumulated and nearly made a minute.

lines.japanese: 「……黙っていてくれ」
lines.english: “…Please don't tell him.”

lines.japanese:
すがりついた。
　薄暗い地下道に、長閑な笑声が響いた。
lines.english: He begged. Carefree laughter echoed through the dim underground passage.

lines.japanese: 加藤ハム製のポークウインナー
lines.english: Kato Ham Pork Wieners

lines.japanese:
原材料名
　豚肉、でん粉、植物性たん白、卵たん白、ぶどう糖、水あめ、食塩、脱脂
粉乳、香辛料、ブタブイヨン、アミノ酸、リン酸塩、酸化防止剤、発色剤
　（原材料の一部に小麦、大豆を含む）
lines.english: Ingredients Pork, starch, vegetable protein, egg white, glucose, starch syrup, salt, skim milk, spices, pork bouillon, amino acids, phosphates, antioxidant, color-fixing agent (Some ingredients contain wheat and soy.)

lines.japanese:
ミニミニサイズだからお弁当にピッタリ！
　火の通りがすぐだからいろいろなお料理に重宝します。
lines.english: Mini-mini size—perfect for lunch boxes! They cook through quickly, so they're handy for all sorts of dishes.

lines.japanese:
生食用。セニョリータとも。
　短くてコロッとした小型のかわいらしいバナナです。
　甘味も香りもいい。皮は薄く、果肉はとろけるように柔らかい。
lines.english: For eating raw; also known as the Señorita banana. A cute little banana, short and plump. Sweet and fragrant, with thin skin and meltingly soft flesh.
